## 第002篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

Air pollution in many cities around the world is increasing. What are the causes of this problem and what measures can governments take to reduce it?

### 文章

Air pollution is a serious problem in many cities today. This essay will discuss the main causes of air pollution and suggest some solutions that governments can implement.

The main cause of air pollution is the increasing number of cars and trucks on the roads. Vehicles produce harmful gases like carbon dioxide and nitrogen oxide, which make the air dirty. Another cause is factories that release smoke and chemicals into the atmosphere. In developing countries, many factories do not have proper filters to clean their emissions. Additionally, the burning of coal and gas for electricity contributes to poor air quality.

Governments can take several steps to address this problem. Firstly, they can invest in public transportation systems to reduce the number of private cars on the roads. If buses and trains are cheap and convenient, more people will use them. Secondly, governments can create stricter laws for factories regarding pollution limits. Companies that break these rules should receive heavy fines. Finally, governments should promote renewable energy sources like solar and wind power to replace fossil fuels.

In conclusion, air pollution is mainly caused by vehicles, factories, and fossil fuels. Governments can reduce this problem by improving public transport, enforcing pollution laws, and supporting clean energy.

https://www.ielts.international/ielts-sample-essays

## 第005篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

Some people believe that children should not be allowed to use smartphones until they are at least 12 years old. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

In today's world, smartphones have become an important part of daily life. Some people think children under 12 should not use smartphones. I partially agree with this view because while smartphones can be harmful for young children, they also offer some educational benefits.

On the one hand, there are good reasons to keep smartphones away from young children. First, children can become addicted to games and social media, which affects their studies and physical health. Many children spend hours watching videos instead of playing outside or reading books. Second, young children may see inappropriate content online that they are too young to understand.

On the other hand, smartphones can be useful for education. There are many apps that help children learn mathematics, languages, and science in an interesting way. Also, children need to learn how to use technology because it is essential for their future careers. If they only start using smartphones at 12, they may fall behind their classmates.

In conclusion, I believe that a complete ban on smartphones for children under 12 is too strict. Instead, parents should limit screen time and monitor what their children do on their phones. This way, children can benefit from technology while avoiding its dangers.

## 第008篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

An increasing number of organisations are considering a four-day working week without reducing employees' salaries. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?

### 文章

It is becoming increasingly common for organisations to consider a four-day working week without reducing employees' salaries. Although this development has some disadvantages, I believe that its advantages are considerably greater because it can improve employees' work-life balance and increase workplace productivity.

On the one hand, there are some disadvantages associated with a four-day working week. One major disadvantage is that employees may have to work longer hours on the four working days. This is mainly because organisations still need to complete the same amount of work within a shorter working week. For example, an employee may have to work longer hours each day to complete all the tasks that were previously completed over five days. As a result, employees may become tired and experience greater pressure at work. Therefore, this is a genuine concern that should be considered.

On the other hand, I believe that the advantages are considerably greater. The primary advantage is that a four-day working week can improve employees' work-life balance. This is mainly because workers have an additional day for rest, family activities and personal responsibilities. For example, employees can use their extra day off to spend time with their families or complete personal tasks without taking additional leave. As a result, they can have more time for their personal lives and feel more satisfied.

Furthermore, another important advantage is that a shorter working week can increase workplace productivity. This is because employees who have more time to rest may return to work with greater energy and concentration. For instance, a well-rested employee may be able to focus more effectively on important tasks during working hours. Consequently, the employee may complete tasks more efficiently and maintain better performance. Therefore, I believe that the advantages clearly outweigh the disadvantages.

In conclusion, although the disadvantage of employees having to work longer hours on the four working days is a valid concern, I believe that the advantages of a four-day working week are substantially greater. This is mainly because it can improve employees' work-life balance and increase workplace productivity.

## 第010篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

Art classes, such as painting or drawing, are as important for children’s development as other subjects, so it should be compulsory in high school. Do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

Art classes, such as painting and drawing, are important for children's development as other subjects, so they should be compulsory in schools. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

The majority of individuals contend that art classes like painting and drawing are as indispensable components as other subjects for learners' psychological and emotional development; therefore, they demand that these subjects be compulsory in schools. I completely agree with this stance since the role of art is inevitable in fostering a student's personal progress.

Firstly, the branches of the arts positively affect adolescents' cognitive growth. Engaging in painting or drawing regularly besides obligatory subjects offers students an opportunity for relaxing and clearing their minds. For example, in exam week, learners who are doing drawing can mitigate stress, which is a good circumstance for their mental health. As a result, this creative outlet proves highly beneficial for their mental well-being.

Furthermore, artistic education is a major determinant of a child's future career, particularly in fields that require special creativity and ability. In other words, drawing teaches children how to understand shapes and spaces. This assists them in thinking creatively and seeing things from different angles, which is paramount for their future. For instance, professions like architecture, engineering, and design heavily depend on these creative skills. If schools do not offer art classes, students may find it challenging to succeed in these career paths later in life.

To conclude, I strongly believe that making art classes mandatory is an advantageous step for the the next generations. In fact, since painting and drawing not only significantly mitigate academic stress but also enhance the spatial-visual intelligence required for upcoming careers, physical schools cannot afford to overlook them. Therefore, integrating these classes into the core curriculum is essential for achieving holistic student development.

On the one hand, both students and their country can benefit from this trend. First, students can choose more suitable education methods for themselves because there are more options. The course and teaching methods are quite different from China . According to foreign experts, the higher education in China is really not good as that of those developing countries, especially in contrast with Europian or US. Secondly, people can improve their foreign language, but, they can contact with others when they are in a foreign country, and they will quickly master the foreign language. Thirdly, it helps to promote the mutual understanding between their mother land and their destination countries. These students exchange information with the locals. Students can get better understanding of the destination countries. People in their home country will get more vivid information about other countries through these messages . Similarly, the locals also can get more clear recognition about other countries.

On the other hand, there are disadvantages too. Firstly, it costs people a lot of money to begin college in foreign countries. Many families have to take out all their savings to support their children to go abroad. Secondly, some students cannot stand the big difference of the new environment, they maybe quit their study and come back home.

To conclude, given the undisputable fact that to begin college in foreign countries helps students with their studies and promotes the mutual understanding between countries, even if there are some drawbacks, I think the benefits outweigh the problems.

## 第018篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

Buying things on the internet such as book, air ticket and groceries is becoming more and more popular. Do the advantages of shopping in this way outweigh the disadvantages.

### 文章

Purchasing goods through online marketplaces, such as books, airplane tickets and daily necessities, has grown significantly in popularity. This undoubtedly provides numerous benefits to the customers, but they need to be more selective and have cashless payment options. I believe the advantages for customers would be greater than the disadvantages of using online platforms to buy goods. This essay will examine both aspects in detail.

On the one hand, buying products through online marketplaces is really effective and minimizes time consumption for customers, who only need to hold their smartphones or laptops then open digital platforms such as Amazon, Alibaba and Carousell. This allows customers to save commuting time, avoid traffic congestion on the roads and shop more cost-effectively compared to visiting physical stores. In addition, people are able to compare prices, specifications and delivery times prior to checking out their shopping carts, which helps them to secure the best deal. For example, if customers buy a shirt, they can compare the price and delivery time across different vendors. They are able to choose the cheapest one, while it has the longest delivery time, as long as it is suitable for their preferences.

On the other hand, consumers are also exposed to negative risks of the product quality. They cannot visually check the condition of the products prior to delivery, which quite often leads to a dispute with the sellers. If such a case occurs, consumers need more time to return the items and wait for the replacement. Furthermore, most payment methods are only available digitally or via cashless systems. Customers must have credit cards or other digital wallets to support transactions, which would be challenging for people from rural areas.

In conclusion, I believe the benefits of online digital platforms will be far greater than their drawbacks. People can save more time, and they have more alternative stores to compare with. However, people also need to be mindful of the product quality and the availability of payment methods.

## 第020篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

Childhood obesity has become a serious problem in recent years. What are the primary causes of this? What measures should be taken to reduce childhood obesity?

### 文章

Nowadays, infants are facing a serious problem of obesity. The issue seems to be happening globally , even for developed countries. The main cause of the problem is the substitution of mother’s milk for formula milk. To address this, the education and material support for an early family are needed. Analysing why it becomes the major cause and explaining the solutions to overcome that will answer the question of how to reduce the number of overweight children.

In modern eras, mothers face several problems , such as limited time to take care of the baby because they are working to support their family, leaving them with no choice but to give their baby formula milk. Moreover, the health issue prevents mothers from breastfeeding their baby, for instance, the milk doesn’t flow out. As a result, formula milk with unhealthy amounts of sugar and fat replaces the pure nutrients of mother’s milk.

In order to prevent that from happening, a lot of support is needed for women from an early stage. First, the parents have to be aware that the needs of mother’s milk are non-negotiable because of nutrients and bonding effects between mother and baby. Second, the preparation of vitamins and foods that have to be consumed by pregnant women. The husband needs to guarantee these needs, so that later the supply of milk would not be a problem. Third, the tools and scheduling to pump the milk for working mothers have to be planned.

All in all, the increase in processed milk consumption for children is projected as the primary cause of childhood obesity and preparation from the early stage of pregnancy is needed, so the parents can still provide their baby with their mother’s milk. As awareness is increasing, I believe the issue will progressively decline.

## 第022篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

Countries with longer working hours are more economically successful than other countries. To what extent do you agree?

### 文章

It is often argued that if the public of any country works many hours, there is an evolving economy in that country. From my perspective, I completely disagree with this statement as productivity determines a country's success rather than working hours.

The major reason is that working many hours doesn’t influence the country’s economy. According to  foreign professors, people can only  work effectively for 5 hours a day. If workers operate for more than 5 hours, they may experience mental fatigue, which can reduce their concentration and efficiency. As a result,  the state can only achieve economic success if its performance is good. It is not about working long hours. For example, a videographer or journalist spends little time on work. They participate in shooting time , for them, it is more important the quality of shooting rather than the total hours.

Additionally, a country's productivity determine economical success. The reason for that is that productivity per hour is more important than total hours. If a country has advanced technology and automation, it allows  countries to produce more in less time. For example, in Ireland average annual hours worked is  1150 hours, and GDP per Capita is 140,000$,  in Norway average annual hours worked is 1420 hours, and GDP per Capita is 106,000$. To be clear, average annual hours don't determine the economic output of a country, it is more about productivity. Therefore, in terms of economic success, long working hours aren't important as productivity and a skilled workforce.

In conclusion, countries with longer working hours aren’t more economically successful because  productivity determines a country’s success rather than working hours. Therefore, governments should prioritise improving employees’ productivity and working conditions instead of simply increasing working hours.

By combining education with practical support, this can strengthen employment rates and reduce dependence on financial aid from the government.

In conclusion, adults who lack basic proficiency mostly miss job opportunities, face challenges in daily life and experience difficulty in social mobility. ## 第048篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

In many countries today, crime novels and tv crimes dramas are becoming more and more popular. Why do you think these books and tv shows are popular? What is your opinion of crime fiction tv crime dramas?

### 文章

In many countries, crime novels and TV crime dramas are becoming increasingly popular. I believe this trend is mainly driven by the suspenseful storylines and intellectual stimulation that these forms of entertainment provide. In my view, crime fiction is generally a positive form of entertainment because it can both engage people and encourage them to think critically.

One major reason for the popularity of crime novels and TV dramas is their ability to stimulate curiosity. Suspenseful plots encourage readers and viewers to follow the storyline closely and try to identify the criminal or solve the mystery before the ending. This makes the experience more engaging than forms of entertainment in which the outcome is predictable. In addition, crime fiction often requires people to analyse clues, compare different possibilities and predict what might happen next. For example, detective novels such as the Sherlock Holmes series present complex cases that encourage readers to examine evidence and develop their own theories. Therefore, the combination of suspense and intellectual challenge can make crime fiction particularly appealing.

In my opinion, crime-fiction TV dramas can also have several positive effects when watched in moderation. They provide an opportunity for people to relax and take their minds off their daily responsibilities, while also exposing them to issues related to criminal behaviour, investigation and justice. Moreover, viewers may improve their analytical skills by trying to understand the motives of different characters and predict the outcome of an investigation. However, excessive exposure to violent content may have negative effects, particularly on younger viewers, so such programmes should be consumed responsibly. For example, in a detective series, viewers may be given several clues about a murder and have to analyse the evidence and the suspects’ motives before the detective reveals the identity of the criminal. This encourages them to pay close attention to details and consider different explanations rather than simply watching the programme passively.

In conclusion, crime novels and TV crime dramas are becoming increasingly popular because their suspenseful storylines stimulate curiosity and provide an intellectual challenge. I believe that crime-fiction dramas are a valuable form of entertainment when watched in moderation because they can help people relax while also encouraging them to analyse evidence and think critically.

Therefore, many people believe that parents should prepare their children before they reach this important age. ## 第069篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

Many aspects of the way people dress today are influenced by global fashion trends. How has global fashion become such a strong influence on people’s lives? Do you think this is a positive or negative development? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

### 文章

Nowadays, globalisation of fashion has become more and more prevalent among youths in the majority of countries. The increasing popularity of pop cultures and social media applications is considered to be a huge catalyst for this fashionglobalisation. However, I am in favour of the view that these trends can have adverse effects on the cultures of minority groups as well as their identity. The following paragraphs will delve into how fashion trends started to spread globally and why I believe that it can have drastic effects on local cultures.

This globalisation of clothing styles can be said to stem from the rise of pop cultures and social media platforms. World-famous singers and artists have millions of fans from all over the world, and they have the ability to influence their fans in many aspects of life. This is even more fuelled by the invention of applications such as Facebook and Instagram, which allow fans to catch up with what kind of styles their idols are adopting, and to imitate those immediately in their daily life. For example, if a picture of Taylor Swift wearing a plain white T-shirt while shopping circulated online, thousands of her fans across the world would definitely find it fashionable to wear those plain white T-shirts on a daily basis. If it had not been for social media and pop artists, this would never have happened.

On the other hand, it is concerning that this can put other minority cultures and fashion styles at risk. Seeing as many youths are a lot more into global cultures in fashion, it may become significantly challenging for locals to persuade the younger population to preserve their traditional styles. An obvious impact of this would be the loss of cultural identity, since global fashion trends took over. For instance, these days in Myanmar, most would rather choose to wear global designs such as denim jackets and hoodies than Myanmar traditional longyis made of cotton, which makes it hard for us to showcase the best of Myanmar cultural fashion styles to other foreign countries. If it were not for this globalisation, more Myanmar traditional costumes would still be seen in public places of our country.

To conclude, pop music and the internet contributed mainly to the surge in global fashion trends. Despite its popularity, I am still convinced that it can threaten the fashions of minority cultures. Doing awareness campaigns to promote local cultures and fashion might reduce its negative impact to some extent, thereby eliminating the concerns to loss of cultural value in fashion.

Firstly, the most impacted part of  society by fast food outlets is youth. The food made in these restaurants lacks nutritional value because it is cooked in multiple steps before it is served to the customers to save time. Take an example of a processed junior chicken burger, it would take them less than a minute to make because of pre-cooked patties, frozen vegetables and a same cooking oil for days. On top of it, these fast food chains add a large amount of preservatives to provide longevity and to increase the shelf life of their stock. These days youngsters eat all the time from these places which leads to helath issues like diabetes, obesity and poor development of the brain and body. In a recent survey, obesity in kids surged to 140 percent since the year 1990 due to eating calorie-dense food.

Secondly, people have no choice but to eat from these restaurants because of their busy lifestyles. It is nearly impossible to raise a family with a single household income because of the increase in inflation and consumerism. Hence, both of the parents have to work to provide for their family , which results in very little or no time for cooking or to spend with their children. Due to advancements in technology, it is so easy to order food online that is delivered warm straight to their door, which is really tempting. So, they just ignore the studies and facts about the negative impact of eating junk food on their body and families.

Finally, the fast food industry needs huge amounts of packaging materials from the transportation of raw materials to the final order for their consumers. Moreover, it requires refrigeration for months to meet the surging demand from their purchasers. This whole process demands devastating amounts of energy consumption that harm nature by releasing CO2 and methane gases in the environment.

In conclusion, while fast food caters to the demands of a fast-paced lifestyle, its widespread negative impacts on individual health, family dynamics, and the environment are undeniable. Relying on processed meals daily creates lasting harm that outweighs any temporary convenience.

Many museums and historical sites are mainly visited by tourist and not locals. What is the cause? and give solutions.

### 文章

Locals' low interest in visiting museums and historical sites is one of the most pressing issues facing many societies today. This problem has led to numerous negative consequences, such as the loss of cultural heritage and reduced social awareness of common values. This essay will examine the root causes of this issue and propose practical solutions to address it effectively.

One of the primary causes of locals not preferring to visit museums is the lack of marketing. For instance, people try to discover the USA because of the Hollywood effect, which in turn means they are not aware of their country's historical and natural sites. This leads to the loss of cultural heritage because these sites may not get sufficient funds to maintain due to the lack of interest. A viable solution to this would be for locals to promote these places by advertising and organizing free tours. For instance, they could raise awareness among children, encouraging them to visit these sites through free school tours, which would likely increase popularity among locals.

A further significant problem is the cost of entrance fees. This is evident in cases where locals who cannot afford to purchase a ticket would not visit these sites. As a result, society is likely to face a reduction in social awareness of common values because people would not see any shared roots with their community. To tackle this, it is essential that authorities regulate these entrance fees for their citizens. Implementing measures such as a low-price ticket policy would help encourage people to visit these sites, allowing them to comprehend their history and culture.

In conclusion, while problems like the cost of entrance fees and the lack of marketing for museums and historical places are undoubtedly complex, they are not insurmountable. By adopting solutions such as consolidated advertisement strategies and effective price policies, we can mitigate the adverse effects of locals' low interest in visiting museums and historical places. It is crucial for both governments and citizens to take proactive steps to ensure a better future.

## 第078篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

Many people feel it is a waste of money to try to save endangered species, for example the tiger or the blue whale. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?

### 文章

Over the past few centuries, the number of endangered species has drastically increased. This worrying situation has raised the question of whether we should try to save them or not. Many people hold the view that this would be a waste of money. Whilst there are some reasons to justify this point, I do not entirely agree with it.

On the one hand, all actions aimed at saving endangered animals require a vast amount of resources. This includes large territories with restricted access, the means of transport necessary, as well as the special equipment needed for medical controls. Moreover, all people implied, such as veterinarians, scientists, pilots, drivers, guards and all members of rescue teams must receive proper training. These resources come at a high cost, taking into account that most of them are very specific to their purpose, and cannot be easily manufactured or replaced, and there are views that these sums could be spent to make a greater impact. Therefore, it seems logical not to waste sums that could potentially end humanity’s greatest problems, including famine, poverty and unemployment, and focus on solving them.

On the other hand, many endangered species play a major role in nature. For example, they regulate the population of their prey or act as natural sanitizers in their ecosystems. Their removal could generate disastrous consequences, affecting not only the environment, but also humans. A case in point is the extinction of the Tasmanian wolf, which led to a dramatic increase in the number of kangaroos in Tasmania. Consequently, they damaged significant areas of grazing land and negatively affected sheep farming. That is why I think we should protect them from extinction, as that could cause significant problems in crucial economic branches such as agriculture, which are of paramount importance in our existence.

In my opinion, such actions should be well-funded. I believe that they represent a way to prevent catastrophes from interrupting economic activities.

In conclusion, while some people argue that saving animals on the verge of extinction is a waste of resources, I disagree entirely. I feel that society as a whole benefits from it, and should be informed more about their role in nature.

The common archetype of the „starving artist“ begs the question whether governments should sponsor artistic professions. While the monetary support might put additional strain on taxpayers, there is an element of cultural identity to art that makes it worth preserving. I am of the opinion that artists should be eligible for government grants, because otherwise the profession might suffer to the detriment of our cultural heritage.

Due to the recent increases in price due to high rates of inflation, many German citizens are anxious to reduce their spending. An increase in taxes would likely be received poorly. However, the likelihood of additional government funding without a citizen-funded pool of money , such as the „Solidaritätszuschlag",is unlikely. This extra tax has been widely debated and is generally seen as extremely unpopular. Therefore, passing a law that prescribes such a grant in combination with changes to the tax system is nigh impossible. It could, however, be said that the money spent on artists might aid the economy in the sense of buying art supplies. If those art supplies were obtained from smaller businesses, the money would benefit a larger percentage of the population. Despite this, it may be very difficult to garner the support needed to pass such a bill in Congress.

Conversely, while funding for art is not usually treated as important compared to larger societal issues such as inflation, artistic works are the cornerstone of culture and should be preserved. When we consider where our knowledge of past civilisations, stems from, the answer is almost unanimously "from their art". For millennia, creative works were utilised to record stories and histories. From the cave painting in France, showing the existence of certain animals, the tattoos on ice age mummies exhibiting craftsmanship, to the highly evolved cultures of ancient Egypt, Rome and Greece with their advanced architecture, varied cultural and religious practices , and enduring concepts such as the Olympic Games, the remnants of their art illuminate their cultures for us. Without these glimpses into the past, much of history would possibly be lost. While it might be difficult to decide, which works of art are worth funding and thus preserving, it is highly relevant that we as a society do not condemn art to become an afterthought. If artists are not supported at least partially, we might risk losing aspects of our culture for future generations.

For these reasons, the importance of documenting culture in works of art and the valuable insights this provides to scientists and historians, provisions should be made to support low-income artists. Despite the difficulties in implementing such legislation, the economy might actually benefit in the form of increased revenue for small businesses selling art supplies.

This is because the brain needs to rest in order to function well, but without enough sleep, people struggle to focus on work. Hence, a decline in screen time can prevent people from sleep deprivation, allowing them to get sufficient sleep during the night.

In conclusion, insufficient sleep has a negative impact on people's lives, as it reduces their productivity and concentration. To tackle this, reducing screen time can provide an effective method to overcome this issue, as it helps people to get sufficient sleep.

This shows that using a phone at night can take a toll on a person's health in the long term.

Beyond this, the problems can even escalate to low levels of productivity. As individuals do not get the right amount of sleep they are supposed to, they are prone to showing less enthusiasm and efficiency during the next day. Not only does this lead to delays in their daily commitments, but it also affects people psychologically as if their days were wasted. A case in point is doom-scrollers, who usually report that their lives are meaningless, possibly because they waste the majority of their time scrolling and binge-watching during the night, resulting in poor levels of productivity and dissatisfaction with their lives.

As a result, they might enhance their lives because they sleep enough and effectively. For example, if a country introduces a new TV channel, especially in terms of technology, people can receive useful knowledge about the drawbacks of using phones at night, thus avoiding the use of such devices.

Another possible solution for this trend is that individuals should be forced to turn off their mobile phones during the night because of app restrictions produced by officials. In other words, governments with the help of doctors might introduce new limits on mobile phone usage, and people have to delete social media and other apps when they reach their daily limit. Consequently, not only might they improve their concentration, but they may also develop their personal skills and find new hobbies because they do not spend a lot of time on their phones.

To conclude, although using mobile phones can contribute to health-related problems and reduced productivity, I believe that these severe issues can be tackled through public campaigns and app restrictions.

ome people think that exercise is the key to health, while others feel that having a balanced diet is more important. Discuss both sides and give your opinion.

### 文章

It is often argued that exercise is the key to maintaining a healthy lifestyle, while others believe that having a balanced diet is more important. Although fitness training has many benefits for our physical health, I believe that a balanced diet has a greater impact because it provides the essential nutrients that our bodies need.

On the one hand, exercise is an important part of staying healthy. Regular physical activity helps people maintain a healthy weight by burning calories and reducing excess body fat. It can also improve physical fitness and make people feel more energetic in their daily lives. For example, people who exercise regularly are more likely to have stronger muscles and better physical endurance. Therefore, fitness training can play an important role in preventing health problems associated with an inactive lifestyle.

On the other hand, I believe that a balanced diet is more important because the body needs nutrients to function properly. Foods containing vitamins, minerals, protein, and fiber provide the body with the substances it needs for growth, energy, and maintaining a strong immune system. If a person does not receive enough essential nutrients, they may become weaker and more vulnerable to health problems. In contrast, even if someone exercises regularly, their health may still be negatively affected if their diet does not provide adequate nutrition. This is why I believe that diet has a greater influence on overall health.

Nevertheless, exercise and diet are closely connected and should ideally be maintained together. Exercise increases the body's energy requirements, while a nutritious diet provides the energy and nutrients needed to support physical activity and recovery. Therefore, although I consider a balanced diet to be slightly more important, the healthiest lifestyle involves combining both regular exercise and good nutrition.

In conclusion, both exercise and a balanced diet are essential for maintaining good health. However, I believe that a balanced diet is more important because it provides the nutrients necessary for the body to function properly, while exercise mainly strengthens and supports physical fitness.

One of the dire consequences of the over-consumption of single-use plastic is that it attracts flies and rodents to landfill sites. Moreover, it is essential to educate the public as most people are unaware of the negative impacts of plastic on the environment. Some people argue that these international sporting events are vital for mitigating global political tensions and providing a safe outlet for national pride. I completely agree with this perspective, as these competitions foster cross-cultural unity and channel patriotism into harmless entertainment, provided that spectators maintain mutual respect.

On the one hand, international sports serve as an excellent vehicle for releasing nationalistic fervor constructively while alleviating societal stress. During world-class tournaments, citizens can passionately cheer for their country's athletes, which temporarily unifies a population and satisfies the human desire for tribal belonging. This display of patriotism is generally safe because it is confined to a playing field with strict rules of sportsmanship. Furthermore, these events provide a massive source of entertainment, offering a healthy escape for families and friends to bond and decompress from the rigors of daily work or academic life.

On the other hand, it must be acknowledged that hyper-nationalism can occasionally catalyze bitter disputes between nations when matches become overly contentious. For instance, biased refereeing decisions or perceived fouls frequently spark toxic arguments among social media users of different nationalities, which can alienate communities and damage diplomatic goodwill. Moreover, the spirit of fair play is sometimes tarnished by the darker side of sports culture, such as illicit gambling and match-fixing. Nevertheless, these negative behaviors are usually confined to a radical minority of fans and do not diminish the overarching diplomatic benefits of the games.

In conclusion, international sporting spectacles are undeniably advantageous in bridging cultural divides and offering a peaceful arena for patriotic expression. While excessive fan fanaticism and gambling can occasionally lead to localized conflicts, the collective benefits of entertainment and global harmony heavily outweigh these drawbacks. Ultimately, as long as spectators prioritize respect and fair play, sports will remain an invaluable tool for global unity.

## 第101篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

Should parents give children money for doing household work?

### 文章

Some people believe that parents should give their children money for doing household chores, while others think that children should help at home without receiving payment. In my opinion, giving children a small amount of money for some tasks can be useful, but they should also learn that helping their family is a responsibility.

On the one hand, paying children for household work can teach them important financial skills. For example, parents can give their children a small amount of pocket money for completing tasks such as cleaning their rooms, washing dishes or taking out the rubbish. Children can then learn how to save and spend money responsibly. This may also encourage them to work harder and become more independent.

On the other hand, children should not expect to receive money every time they help their family. Household chores are a normal part of family life, and all family members should contribute. If children are always paid for their work, they may develop the idea that they should only help others when they receive something in return. For example, a child might refuse to help an elderly family member because there is no financial reward.

In conclusion, I believe that parents can give children money for additional or more difficult household tasks, but basic responsibilities should be completed without payment. This approach can help children understand both the value of money and the importance of responsibility.

On the one hand, global institutions have an enormous amount of resources to fight against environmental problems, such as global warming, while governments don't have. For instance, Greenpeace have many supporters and fundraisers from all around the world, enabling the organisation to purchase and maintain expensive technological tools, such as radars that can report forest fires in advance across the world.  Therefore, global organisations can provide solutions at the international level, while governments cannot afford to implement  global strategies due to limited budgets.

On the other hand, these organisations have a wide range of human resources, such as scientists, researchers and workers from different backgrounds and experience , whereas governments don't have such people. This is because these people take some mandatory training and classes where they improve their knowledge and abilities in organisations' centres, which gives them hands-on experience to tackle environmental issues. To illustrate, the Arctic Organisation employs many scientists in different periods, and they provide them opportunities to research root problems of melting ice in the Polar Zone, which gives them a chance to build a clear understanding of possible solutions. Thus, international organisations not only employ experts but also create a space where they can find the core of the problem; however, governments sometimes struggle to employ such experts.

In conclusion, although governments have some responsibilities to tackle environmental problems, I firmly maintain that international institutions have not only trained and experienced people but also sufficient funds to fight against the problems; as a result, they should take more responsibility than authorities.

Band 6.0

### 题目

Some experts believe that once a country is already rich, any additional increase in economic wealth does not make its citizens any more satisfied. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

Many experts argue that once a country has reached a high level of economic prosperity, increases in wealth do not make its citizens happier. I largely agree with this view because, additional wealth has only a limited impact on people's overall happiness.

It is undeniable that economic development plays a crucial role in improving people's quality of life. In less developed countries, higher national income enables governments to invest in essential public services such as healthcare, education and infrastructure. In terms of individual level, rising incomes allow people to afford better housing, nutritious food and financial security. As a result, increasing wealth often leads to higher levels of happiness because it satisfies people's basic needs and reduces financial stress.

However, economic growth does not necessarily result in greater life satisfaction. In many wealthy countries, people already enjoy a comfortable standard of living, meaning that additional income contributes little to their overall happiness. Instead, factors such as physical and mental health, strong family relationships, work-life balance become far more crucial. For example, many high-income societies continue to experience rising levels of stress, loneliness and depression despite their economic success. This suggests that happiness depends on a combination of social and personal factors rather than just wealth.

In conclusion, although economic growth is vital for improving living standards, I agree that its influence on happiness becomes limited once a country is already wealthy. At that stage, factors such as good health, meaningful relationships, personal fulfilment and overall well-being contribute far more to people's satisfaction than additional economic prosperity.

## 第109篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

Some people argue that all experimentation on animals is bad and should be outlawed. However, others believe that important scientific discoveries can be made from animal experiments. Can experimentation on animals be justified? Are there any alternatives?

### 文章

Whether animals should be used for experiments and in laboratory research is a deeply debated issue. While animal testing has helped a lot of scientists with discoveries, the ethical concerns surrounding this topic have led to discussions for completely banning animal testing.

On the one hand, supporters argue that animal testing is beneficial and necessary for medical progress. Animals share a lot of biological similarities with humans, which is why they are ideal for experiments and testing how a drug or disease affects the body. For example, many of the cures have been tested on animals, such as vaccines, antibiotics and other treatments. From this point of view, doing research on animals is justified since it has saved millions of lives.

On the other hand, other people believe that since animals are beings that feel fear and pain, it is unethical and cruel to put them in laboratories and do all kinds of painful experiments on them. Furthermore, animals do not have the exact same biology as us humas, so a cure that works on mice might be ineffective or bad for the human body.

Fortunately, modern technology offers several alternatives that would help ban animal testing. Scientist can now test their discoveries on lab grown human cells instead of living animals. Additionally, artificial intelligence can predict the way the human body will react to different cures. Another way of testing treatments would be on human cadavers, this way scientists can do their research, surgical trials, and other complex anatomical studies without causing harm to living creatures.

To conclude, although animal experimentation played an important role in the past, today using the modern technology that we have, we have the option to completely ban animal testing.

Band 6.0

### 题目

Some people believe that all workers, regardless of their job or skills, should receive the same salary. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

Nowadays, salary rates depend on the type of occupation and skill level. I disagree with the idea that all workers should receive the same salary regardless of age or working hours.

First, motivation is essential for increasing both quality and productivity. If everyone earns the same pay, work output will decline because employees will lack incentive to upgrade their skills. Although most companies offer career progression based on seniority, paying a veteran with a decade of experience the same as an entry-level trainee is inherently unfair.

Additionally, different occupations carry varying levels of risk and stress. For example, pilots and cabin crew spend most of their working hours airborne, facing higher safety risks than ground staff. Similarly, doctors and nurses often work demanding 24- to 48-hour shifts, which requires double or triple the effort of standard jobs under intense pressure. In contrast, teachers usually work regular office hours (8:00 AM to 4:00 PM), allowing them more leisure time after work.

Proponents of equal pay argue that it ensures everyone can afford essential needs like food and shelter. However, this view overlooks the broader economic impact. Equal salaries would stifle economic growth and financial circulation, demotivating people from generating wealth and leaving saving as their only focus.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with the notion of equal pay across all professions. A system without financial incentives destroys passion, discipline, and accountability, ultimately damaging workplace morale and economic stability.

In contrast to previous generations, children today are granted greater freedom in making everyday decisions, such as what they eat and wear. Although some argue that this trend may lead to selfishness in adulthood, I support this trend, and this essay will examine both perspectives.

On one hand, those who oppose children’s autonomy in decision-making argue that granting young individuals  unrestricted freedom could negatively affect social interactions. Childhood shapes individuals’ future lives since behaviors that become deeply ingrained during this period can be difficult to change later in life. Therefore, if they become accustomed to putting their own interests first, they may not only develop a self-centred attitude, but also show little consideration of others. Consequently, this tendency could have detrimental effects on social cohesion. For example, some studies revealed people who demonstrate poor collaborative skills in the workplace had been raised with unrestricted autonomy.

On the other hand, advocates of giving children the right to make personal choices contend that this freedom cultivates a profound sense of responsibility. When parents encourage children to choose their own food or clothing, they not only provide them with the opportunity to practice making responsible decisions in a safe environment under parents’ supervision, but also teach them to take on the accountability for their decisions and to encounter the natural consequences of their choices. For instance, when children opt for a certain snack, they must accept the outcome of their choice whether it results satisfaction or regret.

In conclusion, while granting unlimited autonomy to children could foster an excessive individualistic mindset, giving freedom within a structured framework can enhance the sense of responsibility in children. Ultimately, parents should strike a balance between empowering children with independency and setting reasonable boundaries to mitigate the potential negative consequences.

## 第115篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

Some people believe that cheap, fast transportation is required for successful international business, while others believe that good technology is more important. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

### 文章

It is widely acknowledged that being successful in global trade depends on some parameters. While a significant number of people believe that well-connected and low-cost transportation is a key factor for global firms which aiming at reaching top-class level, others argue that advanced technology plays an important role in their success. I strongly believe that transportation cost and type are a main consideration for international companies to maximise their profits while minimising their operating cost. This essay will elaborate on both sides and my position.

On the one hand, the means of transportation and cost are the main drivers of business models. This is because when companies produce their products, they have to transport them to selected destinations, such as ports, customers, or other plants. These destinations are generally far from their production sites; as a result, they have to pay substantial costs to transport their products to reach them, and they have to deliver on time. While it builds a trust relationship with customers, which is crucial for their operations, technology can only manage their internal business.  To illustrate, when companies don't deliver their products on time due to the lack of well-connected transportation, they may face serious penalties, forcing them to pay an excessive amount of penalties that increase their cost. Thus companies' profits and success depend on transportation cost and time.

On the other hand, advanced technology has positive consequences in the long term for companies. It allows them to process a large amount of data that determines their productivity and efficiency at work. This is because data collection and processing require great consideration, which would be manageable by using some AI tools, such as machine learning algorithms, while it takes a long time to be completed when people do it. ### 题目

Some people believe that children should start learning a foreign language in primary school rather than in secondary school. Do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

Learning new languages has become an important part of the modern academic curriculum. Some people support the idea of introducing foreign languages at the primary level instead of secondary school, and I strongly agree with this argument.

To begin with, young children have faster learning abilities. Their brains are still developing, which allows them to absorb grammar rules and pronunciation more easily. Because they are not yet fully influenced by one dominant language, they can learn new sounds and structures without confusion. For instance, learning French can be challenging for older students who already have a strong foundation in English, as both languages share similar spellings but differ in pronunciation. Younger learners, however, tend to adapt more quickly to these differences.

Furthermore, the difficulty level of school subjects increases significantly in higher grades. Secondary students often face pressure from complex subjects such as mathematics, science, and literature, which leaves them with limited time to focus on learning a new language. In contrast, primary school students have a lighter workload, allowing them to dedicate more time and effort to language learning. For example, a grade 4 student can easily allocate extra time to practicing vocabulary and speaking skills, whereas a grade 11 student may already feel overwhelmed by academic responsibilities.

In conclusion, introducing foreign languages in primary school offers clear advantages compared to secondary school. Younger children learn more naturally and have fewer academic pressures, making early language education far more effective. Therefore, I strongly agree with this approach.

## 第121篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

Some people believe that it is best to accept a bad situation, such as an unsatisfactory job or lack of money. others argue that it is better to try and improve such conditions discuss both these views and give your own opinion

### 文章

When faced with difficult circumstances, such as an unfulfilling job or financial hardship, opinions diverge sharply on the wisest course of action. Some maintain that acceptance is the more pragmatic response, while others insist that actively working to change one's situation is preferable. In my view, while acceptance has its place in certain contexts, deliberate efforts to improve one's circumstances generally yield far greater long-term benefits.

Proponents of acceptance argue, first and foremost, that it protects mental wellbeing. Constantly striving against circumstances that cannot easily be changed — a chronic illness, for instance, or a deeply unstable economy — can generate persistent stress and a corrosive sense of failure when improvement proves elusive. Philosophies such as Stoicism have long championed this view, holding that peace of mind stems not from controlling external events, but from mastering one's own response to them. There is also a pragmatic dimension: not every unsatisfactory situation is within an individual's power to resolve, and recognising this can prevent the exhaustion of energy on efforts that are ultimately futile.

Advocates of active change, however, contend that most difficulties, however entrenched, admit at least partial improvement, and that resignation forecloses possibilities that effort might otherwise realise. A person trapped in an unsatisfactory job, for example, can pursue further qualifications, seek a transfer, or actively search for alternative employment; someone facing financial hardship can budget more carefully, acquire new skills, or seek additional income streams. Historical and contemporary examples abound of individuals who transformed dire circumstances through sustained effort rather than passive endurance — entrepreneurs who built successful enterprises from poverty, or workers who retrained entirely to escape declining industries. To accept such situations uncritically, this view holds, is to squander agency that could otherwise be exercised productively.

On balance, I find the case for active improvement more persuasive, though not unconditionally so. The distinction, I believe, lies in whether a circumstance is genuinely immutable or merely difficult. Where a situation can plausibly be improved through reasonable effort, resignation often reflects avoidance rather than wisdom, and forfeits the chance of a better outcome. Where a circumstance is truly beyond one's control, however, acceptance is not merely sensible but necessary, since persistent struggle against the immovable serves only to compound suffering. The wisdom, then, lies not in choosing acceptance or effort as a universal principle, but in accurately judging which applies to a given situation.

In conclusion, both acceptance and active improvement have legitimate roles depending on circumstance, but I believe that where meaningful change remains genuinely possible, the effort to pursue it is almost always the more constructive path. Passive endurance should be reserved for what truly cannot be altered, not adopted as a default response to difficulty.

## 第133篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

Some people say that history offers no practical benefit to society while others claim that history teaches us to understand the present. Discuss both views and give your own opinion .

### 文章

Certainly! Here's a strong and comprehensive IELTS essay on the topic, using advanced vocabulary, clear structure, and balanced argumentation:

Some people say that history offers no practical benefit to society while others claim that history teaches us to understand the present. Discuss both views and give your own opinion

The value of history is a subject of enduring debate, often eliciting contrasting perspectives. While some argue that history holds no practical significance for modern society, others maintain that it is crucial for comprehending the complexities of the present. Both views present compelling points, yet I firmly believe that history is indispensable in shaping our understanding of the world today.

On one hand, critics contend that history is largely irrelevant in practical terms. They argue that the rapid pace of modern technological advancements and scientific discoveries renders historical knowledge obsolete. For instance, learning about ancient civilizations or outdated ideologies may seem disconnected from solving contemporary problems such as climate change or economic instability. Moreover, in an age where innovation and future-oriented thinking dominate, dwelling on past events might be perceived as a waste of time or resources. This school of thought prioritizes applicable skills and knowledge that directly address current challenges rather than reflective or theoretical insights from history.

Conversely, proponents of history emphasize its essential role in helping society make sense of present circumstances. By examining historical events, patterns, and decisions, individuals and communities can glean invaluable lessons that prevent the repetition of past mistakes. For example, understanding the causes and consequences of past wars or economic crises can inform better policies and international relations today. Additionally, history fosters cultural identity and awareness by connecting people to their heritage, traditions, and shared experiences. This connection not only strengthens social cohesion but also cultivates empathy and critical thinking. Without a historical framework, the present might appear fragmented, lacking context and meaning.

In my opinion, history is far more than a mere record of bygone eras; it is a dynamic tool for interpreting current realities and guiding future actions. While it might not provide immediate solutions like technology or science, it equips society with perspective and wisdom that are fundamental for sustainable progress. Ignoring history risks repeating errors and losing sight of the values that have shaped civilization.

In conclusion, although history might seem impractical to some in today’s fast-moving world, its benefits in understanding and navigating the present are undeniable. A balanced approach that integrates historical knowledge with contemporary innovation is essential for holistic development.

Thus, a balanced approach to salaries can not only ensure the company's growth but also increase staff's motivation and job satisfaction.

To sum up, I firmly disagree with the existence of a huge salary difference between senior managers and employees because it can lead to inequality, which can decrease staff's productivity and motivation to perform their responsibilities more efficiently. Nevertheless, a reasonable difference can ensure both the company's and staff's development.

In this regard, zoos that profit from animals should aim for the same goal, to give visitors a chance to discover animals in their natural habitat without subjecting them to constant stress. Moreover, and no less important, the savings in food, veterinary, and maintenance would be enormous, since they would get all of that naturally.

To conclude, animal welfare in zoos should be a priority, considering that the animals are kept outside their natural habitats in confined spaces and exposed to intense external stimuli. ## 第148篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

some people think that hosting an international sporting event is beneficial for a country while others disagree. Do the advantages of hosting major sporting events outweigh the disadvantages

### 文章

Hosting major international sporting events has become increasingly common, and while some people believe that such events benefit the host country, others disagree. Although they can cause traffic congestion and require substantial initial investment, I believe the advantages outweigh these drawbacks because they create employment opportunities and stimulate the local economy.

One major advantage of hosting a major sporting event is that it provides employment opportunities for local residents. When such an event occurs in a country, it brings a large number of international visitors, providing local businesses with more customers. By providing services such as accommodation, food and transportation to these visitors, local businesses can earn greater profits. As a result, these businesses may need additional workers to meet the increased demand, creating more employment opportunities for local residents. Ultimately, stable employment can increase household incomes and improve people’s living standards, thereby strengthening the local economy.

Nevertheless, hosting a major sporting event can place considerable pressure on a country’s infrastructure and finances. A large influx of visitors can significantly increase the number of vehicles on the roads, resulting in severe traffic congestion and longer commuting times for local residents. In addition, governments may need to invest substantial amounts of money in constructing stadiums, improving transportation networks and providing security. As a result, less funding may be available for essential public services, such as healthcare and education. However, these drawbacks are often temporary, while the improved infrastructure and increased economic activity can provide benefits long after the event has ended.

In conclusion, although hosting international sporting events can cause temporary traffic problems and require significant public investment, I believe the advantages are greater. The employment opportunities, increased business activity and long-term economic benefits generated by these events can outweigh their short-term financial and infrastructural costs.

## 第150篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

Some people think that it's good for a country's culture if people watch some imported film or TV programs while some people argue that it could be better if people watch films of their own culture. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

### 文章

In the contemporary digital epoch, preserving the distinctive identity of individual ethnic groups has emerged as a paramount concern. The relentless march of technological innovation has effectively dismantled geographical frontiers, rendering cultural cross-pollination virtually inevitable. While a segment of society contends that consuming imported cinematographic and television content yields profound cognitive and social dividends for citizens, others maintain that prioritizing domestic media is indispensable for safeguarding national heritage and fostering socioeconomic growth. This essay will critically evaluate both dimensions of the debate before presenting a nuanced conclusion.

On the one hand, exposure to international media is an inescapable reality that can significantly broaden a population's horizons. In an increasingly globalized world, modern communication technologies have democratized access to foreign entertainment, making any protectionist censorship both impractical and counterproductive. For instance, the global hegemony of the English language over recent decades has not merely acted as a linguistic bridge, but has also facilitated the exchange of universal human values through cinema. Embracing such external cultural artifacts allows a citizenry to cultivate cosmopolitan perspectives, which ultimately drives national progress by fostering innovation, tolerance, and adaptability within the workforce.

On the counterparts, the unmitigated influx of foreign media can be perceived as an existential threat to local customs, morals, and linguistic traditions. Proponents of this view assert that a state's primary cultural mandate should be the stewardship and promotion of its indigenous creative industries. A nation’s collective identity is fundamentally anchored in its unique historical narratives and artistic expressions; while Western or mainstream global media may wield unmatched commercial dominance, it lacks the intrinsic authenticity and historical resonance found in traditional localized dramas. Ergo, actively nurturing a robust domestic film sector ensures that irreplaceable cultural legacies survive and thrive amidst the pressures of global homogeneity.

In conclusion, although both paradigms possess compelling justifications, I firmly believe that the integration of foreign television programs and films is overwhelmingly advantageous. Rather than eroding local values, the consumption of international media enriches the domestic cultural fabric, fostering cross-cultural empathy and global harmony while concurrently equipping citizens with a broader, more inclusive worldview.

While some individuals argue that universities should focus exclusively on career-specific technical skills, others believe that they should also teach critical thinking and problem-solving. This essay will discuss both perspectives and explain why I believe a balanced approach is essential.

On the one hand, proponents of vocational-focused education argue that the main objective of university is to prepare students for the job market. Advocates of this view emphasize that modern industries require graduates who possess concrete, job-ready competencies to integrate smoothly into specific professions such as engineering or medicine. Furthermore, sticking strictly to a syllabus tailored to workforce demands ensures economic efficiency and reduces the time needed for on-the-job training. Consequently, many believe that spending time on abstract theories can distract students from gaining practical expertise.

On the other hand, a compelling counterargument suggests that universities must cultivate higher-order cognitive faculties. Because modern workplaces are undergoing rapid transformations driven by technology, hyper-specialized technical skills can quickly become obsolete. By prioritizing critical analysis and multi-disciplinary problem-solving, higher education equips students with adaptive resilience to navigate unforeseen real-world challenges. For instance, institutions that encourage open-ended inquiry consistently produce graduates who can lead systemic innovations rather than merely execute routine operational tasks.

In conclusion, while a career-oriented focus guarantees immediate employability, exclusive reliance on technical training leaves graduates vulnerable to a changing global landscape. Therefore, I believe that universities must harmonize technical instruction with the development of critical thinking to ensure long-term professional success.

Moreover, space discovery also serves as a means of planetary defence against other potential threats from space objects. This benefit is able to secure our species' future and prevent terrestrial challenges.

Considering the other argument, funding for preserving our world substantially offers significant advantages to both environmental and social benefits. It is undeniable that planetary conservation safeguarding well-being of our globe and our offspring. By protecting the ecosystem, preserving biodiversity or mitigating the effects of climate change, humans can maintain the health of the globe. This investment, on the other hand, is more sustainable and obvious than depending on other planets' exploration, which is much more unclear and difficult. Furthermore, global saving money is also capable of ensuring citizens' access to clean air and water, while still addressing ecological issues. This positive impact of funding secures a sustainable and promising future.

After considering two arguments, I firmly assert that the authorities ought not to concentrate on profoundly investing in just one side, but they should allocate equally and sufficiently for all categories. This is due to the fact that both fields have significantly impacted each other. Thus, strongly focusing on one of them and neglecting the others can't maximise the consequences. As a result, governments have to strike a balance between spending for spatial exploration and global preservation, not only for the sake of the Earth, but also for the citizens of all countries.

In conclusion, both opinions have their own pros and cons. Therefore, from my point of view, governments ought to strike a balance between spending public money on searching for other planets and protecting the Earth. They should allocate the budget appropriately for each field while still ensuring a fulfilling life for residents all over the world.

## 第170篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

Surveillance cameras in banks, offices, shops and streets have been very successful in reducing crime in the workplace and public, but they are also took for their users to spy on people's private business. what problems

### 文章

Surveillance cameras have become an essential part of modern security systems. They help prevent crime in workplaces and public areas by discouraging illegal activities and providing evidence when crimes occur. However, despite these benefits, the widespread use of surveillance cameras has also raised serious concerns about privacy and misuse. This essay will discuss the problems associated with surveillance cameras and suggest possible solutions.

One major problem is the violation of personal privacy. In many public places and workplaces, people are constantly monitored without knowing how their recorded data will be used. In some cases, unauthorized individuals may access or share video footage, leading to harassment, blackmail, or identity theft. Moreover, excessive surveillance can make employees feel stressed and uncomfortable, as they may believe that every action is being watched, reducing trust between employers and workers.

Another issue is the misuse of surveillance technology by organizations or individuals. Some companies may monitor employees beyond working hours, while hackers can gain access to security systems and use the footage for criminal purposes. Such misuse not only violates people's rights but also undermines public confidence in surveillance systems.

To address these problems, governments should introduce and enforce strict privacy laws that regulate the installation and use of surveillance cameras. Organizations should be required to inform people when cameras are in operation and explain the purpose of recording. In addition, access to recorded footage should be restricted to authorized personnel only, with strong cybersecurity measures in place to prevent hacking and data leaks. Regular inspections and severe penalties for the misuse of surveillance footage would further discourage unethical practices.

In conclusion, although surveillance cameras play a significant role in reducing crime and improving public safety, they also create serious privacy concerns and can be misused. By implementing stricter legal regulations, improving data security, and ensuring responsible use, society can enjoy the benefits of surveillance while protecting individual privacy.

Nowadays, the use of surveillance cameras has become increasingly common in many countries. Although these devices can help reduce crime in public places and workplaces, they can create several significant problems. One of the main problems associated with surveillance cameras is the invasion of privacy. This is mainly because cameras continuously record people's activities in public places and workplaces. As a result, individuals may feel that they are constantly being watched and may lose their sense of privacy. Furthermore, another significant problem is the risk of data theft. This occurs because modern surveillance cameras are often connected to the internet and their recordings may be stored online. Consequently, hackers could gain unauthorised access to sensitive information, which can lead to data theft or the misuse of private information.

Several measures can be taken to tackle these problems. Firstly, governments should introduce strict privacy regulations. This could be achieved by limiting where surveillance cameras can be installed and controlling how recordings are used. As a result, people's privacy could be better protected. Furthermore, companies and organisations should strengthen their cybersecurity systems. One effective way to achieve this is to encrypt recordings and restrict access to authorised employees. Consequently, the risk of data theft could be significantly reduced. These measures could significantly improve the security of surveillance systems while protecting people's privacy.

In conclusion, although surveillance cameras can create significant challenges, particularly the invasion of privacy and data theft, these problems can be addressed through strict privacy regulations and stronger cybersecurity measures.

The given bar chart how many residents in UK spend their money in three categories (Food and drinks, Resturants and hotels, Entertainment) during 2004.

### 文章

The bar chart illustrates the percentage of expenditure allocated to three categories—food and drink, restaurants and hotels, and entertainment—across five age brackets in the UK during the year 2004.  Overall, expenditure on food and drink increased steadily with age. Conversely, younger citizens directed a larger share of their budgets to restaurants and hotels, while entertainment spending peaked among middle-aged to senior residents (61–75 years).

For food and drink, residents aged under 30 spent the lowest proportion, accounting for roughly 6% of their budget. This figure rose consistently across older demographics, climbing to 13% for 31–45 year-olds and reaching a peak of approximately 23% among those aged 61 and above.  In contrast, spending on restaurants and hotels followed a generally reverse trend. The under-30 demographic spent the highest proportion on this category at 14%. This proportion declined across older groups, dropping to a low of just 2% among individuals aged 61 to 75, before rising slightly to around 7% for those 76 and older.  Regarding entertainment, spending remained relatively modest for people under 45, hovering at around 7%. However, it rose sharply for the 46–60 age bracket (14%) and peaked at 23% among 61–75 year-olds, before dropping back to 13% for those over 76.

## 第179篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

The internet has made possible for everybody to read anything online for free. This will make it unnecessary to pay for printed materials such as books or newspapers in the future. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

### 文章

On the topic of whether the abundance and accessibility of digital media makes paying for print mediums redundant, I strongly disagree. While the internet provides a plethora of resources, habitual usage of physical media will ensure their enduring existence.

Admittedly, the vast amount of free resources available online might pose a threat to the relevance of print media. In a world in which almost anything can be found online, from news to novels, the continued existence of books could be questioned. There is a certain amount of convenience in not having to visit a physical store, in order to acquire new reading materials. It might also be beneficial for people who have to commute to work to carry less weight around. Plenty of different books and articles can be assembled on one e-reader. But when it comes to the question of whether those materials are inherently cheaper or even free, I would have to disagree. Most articles are hidden behind paywalls nowadays and e-books on the most common sites like “Apple Books” appear to increase in price dramatically as inflation continues to rise.

On the other side of the equation are habitual readers. These people are notoriously drawn to the qualities of real paper, such as the feel and even the scent. Avid readers nowadays often fall into one of two categories: young and enamoured with the concept and romanticism of reading as much as with the books themselves, and elderly with a long standing habit of reading the newspaper. Plenty of my friends read for both content and aesthetics. The publishing industry is very aware of this trend, selling specially bound editions that look deliberately pretty. The market for those books is flourishing despite the higher prices. Social media niches such as “Book-Tok” or “Book-Tube” have long since become instrumental in marketing- not only books, but an entire lifestyle centred around being a reader. Conversely, the older generations are creatures of habit. Many of my geriatric patients prefer to read the local newspaper over breakfast. I would earn a lot of dismay, if I were to suggest that they read online instead. And that does not even touch upon the matter of accessibility, which has been proven in a 2021 study from Copenhagen to plummet after a certain age range. As a digital native, it is hard to comprehend, but I experienced firsthand that digital media are not unlike learning a new language or advanced arithmetic for the elderly population.

For these reasons, a lack of accessibility for all age groups and ingrained habits with inherent marketability in most avid readers, I believe that books and newspapers will never be made redundant by online media. This statement holds despite the modern conveniences and cost saving potential that digital media bring to the table.
