## 第339篇

### 分数

Band 6.5

### 题目

Some believe that teenagers should concentrate on all school subjects. But others believe that teenagers should focus on the subject that they are good at or that they find the most interest. Discuss both sides and give your opinion.

### 文章

Some people believe that teenagers should study all school subjects equally, while others argue that they should focus mainly on the subjects they are good at or interested in. Although studying a wide range of subjects can provide students with general knowledge, I believe that teenagers should have the opportunity to concentrate more on the subjects that match their abilities and interests.

On the one hand, studying all school subjects can be beneficial for teenagers for several reasons. Firstly, it provides them with a broad range of knowledge and helps them understand different areas of life. For example, subjects such as mathematics, science, history and languages can develop different skills that may be useful in the future. Secondly, teenagers may not know exactly what career they want to pursue at a young age. Therefore, studying different subjects can help them discover their interests and choose a suitable career later in life. If students only focus on one subject from an early age, they may miss the opportunity to discover other areas in which they could potentially be successful.

On the other hand, focusing on subjects that students are good at or interested in can also have significant advantages. When teenagers study subjects they enjoy, they are generally more motivated and willing to spend time improving their skills. As a result, they may achieve better academic results and develop expertise in a particular area. For instance, a student who is particularly interested in computer science may benefit more from spending additional time learning programming rather than concentrating equally on subjects that they have little interest in. Furthermore, allowing students to specialise can help them prepare for their future careers and become highly skilled in their chosen fields.

In my opinion, teenagers should study all essential school subjects, but they should be given more freedom to focus on the areas they are particularly interested in or talented at. Basic knowledge of different subjects is important for developing well-rounded individuals, while specialisation can help students reach their full potential. Therefore, I believe that a balance between general education and personal specialisation is the most effective approach.

In conclusion, studying all school subjects gives teenagers broad knowledge and allows them to discover their interests, whereas focusing on particular subjects can increase motivation and help them develop specialised skills. I believe that students should learn the essential subjects but spend more time on the areas that suit their abilities and interests.

## 第345篇

### 分数

Band 6.5

### 题目

Some people believe that celebrity personal events ia a waste of money. Others feel that these celebrations play an important role in the lives of individual and in society as a whole. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

### 文章

Some people believe that celebrating personal events is a waste of money, while others think that these celebrations are important for individuals and society. This essay will discuss both views. In my opinion, personal celebrations are important, but people should spend money wisely.

On the one hand, some people think that personal events are a waste of money. Celebrations such as weddings, birthdays and graduation parties can cost a lot of money. People may spend money on food, clothes, decorations and entertainment. This money could be used for more important things, such as education, buying a house or saving for the future. For example, some people have a large wedding party even though they do not have enough savings.

On the other hand, other people believe that celebrations are important in our lives and society. Personal events can bring family and friends together. They also give people an opportunity to share happiness and create good memories. For example, a wedding celebration can bring two families together and make their relationship closer. In addition, celebrations can help people feel connected to their community.

In my opinion, personal celebrations are useful and important, but they do not need to be expensive. ## 第351篇

### 分数

Band 6.5

### 题目

Some people believe that university education should be free for everyone, regardless of their financial background. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

It is often argued that higher education should be provided free of charge to all students, irrespective of their financial circumstances. While I agree that university education should be accessible to people from disadvantaged backgrounds, I do not believe that making it entirely free for everyone is the most effective approach.

One major argument in favour of free university education is that it can promote equality of opportunity. Students from low-income families may possess considerable academic ability but be unable to afford tuition fees. If higher education were free, these individuals would have a greater chance of obtaining professional qualifications and improving their future career prospects. This could also benefit society as a whole, since countries would be able to develop a larger pool of highly educated workers in fields such as medicine, engineering and education.

However, providing free university education to everyone would place a substantial financial burden on governments. Public funds are limited, and money allocated to universities could otherwise be spent on essential services such as healthcare, public transport and primary education. Furthermore, wealthy families are generally capable of paying tuition fees themselves, meaning that universal free education could result in public money being used to subsidise people who do not actually need financial assistance. A more practical solution would therefore be to offer scholarships, grants or reduced fees to students from disadvantaged backgrounds while requiring those who can afford it to contribute towards the cost of their education.

In addition, charging reasonable tuition fees may encourage students to take their studies more seriously. When individuals make a financial investment in their education, they may be more motivated to attend classes, complete their coursework and graduate on time. Nevertheless, tuition fees should not be so high that they discourage capable students from poorer families from entering university.

In conclusion, although free university education can improve social mobility and provide greater equality of opportunity, I believe that making it universally free is neither financially sustainable nor necessary. A system in which financially disadvantaged students receive substantial government support, while those who can afford tuition contribute to the cost, would be a fairer and more sustainable alternative.

## 第353篇

### 分数

Band 6.5

### 题目

Some people believe that zoos are inhumane and should be closed down. Others argue that zoos play an important role in wildlife conservation. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

### 文章

Opinions are divided on whether zoological parks should be permanently shut down due to ethical concerns or maintained for their ecological benefits. While confining animals to enclosures is often criticized as cruel, I am a huge advocate for modern zoos, provided they prioritize top-notch conservation and rehabilitation programs.

On the one hand, opponents of zoos argue that holding wild animals in captivity is inherently inhumane. Their primary concern is that artificial enclosures, regardless of how well-designed they are, can never fully replicate the vast natural habitats these creatures require for survival. Consequently, many confined animals suffer from severe physical and psychological distress, often exhibiting abnormal, repetitive behaviors known as zoochosis. For instance, large roaming predators like tigers and polar bears frequently struggle to adapt to limited spatial boundaries. This reality leads critics to assert that exploiting animals primarily for human entertainment is an outdated and deeply unethical practice that should be abolished.

On the other hand, supporters emphasize the prodigious impact that accredited zoological institutions have on global wildlife preservation. In an era where countless species face imminent extinction due to rampant deforestation and illegal poaching, modern zoos act as vital biological sanctuaries. They provide a safe haven for vulnerable creatures and fund extensive captive breeding programs designed to restore dwindling genetic pools. A prime example is the successful recovery of the Arabian Oryx, a species that was brought back from the brink of extinction through dedicated zoo breeding initiatives before being safely reintroduced into its natural habitat.

Overall, while the ethical arguments against depriving animals of their freedom are valid, the critical role of regulated zoos in safeguarding global biodiversity cannot be ignored. Therefore, rather than closing all facilities, authorities must ensure they transition strictly into dedicated research and conservation reserves where animal welfare supersedes commercial entertainment.

People have different views about living in high-rise apartment buildings. While some people believe that this can be a lonely experience, others argue that it can create a strong sense of community. In addition, some residents may prefer to keep their lives private, which can make it difficult to build relationships with others.

However, those who prefer privacy may still feel isolated even when they live close to many people.

People who support advertisements have one good reason: they help the economy. When a business shows an ad, more customers learn about its products. For example, a shoe company puts an ad on TV, and many people go to the shop to buy the new shoes. This means the company sells more, which gives it more money. Because of this, the company can hire more workers and open new shops. If many businesses do this, the country has more jobs and more money. So ads help the economy grow.

However, I believe that the social effect of ads is worse, because ads make people unhappy with what they have. For example, a teenager sees an ad with a new phone and a happy family. Then he looks at his old phone and thinks it is not good enough. He feels sad, so he asks his parents to buy a new one. Many families do not have enough money, so they feel stressed. Over time, people start to buy things they do not need, only to feel better. Because of this, they compare themselves with others, and they never feel happy with what they have. If this continues, society becomes less happy. This is why I think the bad social effect is bigger.

In conclusion, advertisements can help the economy, because companies sell more and give jobs to people. However, I believe that the social effect is worse, because ads make people feel that they need more. This is why ads can be a problem for society.

## 第368篇

### 分数

Band 6.5

### 题目

Some people think it is more beneficial to take part in sports which are played in teams, like football, while other people think taking part in individual sports, like tennis or swimming, is better. Discuss both views and give your own opinion

### 文章

Some people believe that participating in team sports, such as football, is more beneficial, while others argue that individual sports, such as tennis or swimming, offer greater advantages. Although both types of sport have their own benefits, I believe that the best choice depends largely on a person's interests, abilities and personality.

On the one hand, team sports provide valuable opportunities to develop teamwork and communication skills. In football, for example, players have different roles, such as forwards, defenders and goalkeepers, but they must work together to achieve a common goal. During a match, they learn to understand their teammates through their movements, reactions and communication. Over time, this can help players anticipate other people's actions and respond effectively to different situations. These skills are also useful in everyday life because the ability to communicate and cooperate with others is important at school, at work and in society. Therefore, participating in team sports can help people develop strong interpersonal skills.

On the other hand, individual sports can help people develop independence, self-discipline and self-confidence. For instance, tennis players often have to make quick decisions and adjust their tactics according to their opponent's actions. Unlike members of a team, individual athletes cannot rely on teammates when they face difficulties. As a result, they learn to take responsibility for their own decisions and performance. Similarly, sports such as swimming require regular training, determination and a high level of self-discipline. These qualities can help people become more confident and responsible in other areas of their lives.

In conclusion, both team and individual sports can be highly beneficial. While team sports are particularly useful for developing communication and cooperation skills, individual sports encourage independence and self-discipline. In my opinion, neither type of sport is necessarily better than the other, as people should choose the one that best suits their interests, abilities and personality.

Adding another subject to the curriculum may increase pressure on young learners. Nevertheless, these challenges can be minimized if schools use engaging and age-appropriate teaching methods.

In conclusion, although introducing foreign languages in primary school may create some additional pressure, the long-term benefits, including improved language skills, cognitive development, and better career prospects, make it a worthwhile approach.

### 题目

Some people think that it would be better for large companies and industries to move to regional areas outside large urban centers. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this idea?

### 文章

Relocating large businesses and industries from major cities to regional areas has been suggested as a way of promoting more balanced economic development. Although this approach could create valuable employment opportunities for regional communities, it may also result in environmental damage in previously less-developed areas.

One significant advantage of relocating large companies to regional areas is the creation of employment opportunities for local residents. When large businesses establish operations outside major cities, they often require a substantial workforce to perform a variety of roles. By recruiting people from surrounding communities, these companies can provide local residents with access to stable employment without requiring them to migrate to major cities. Consequently, increased employment can raise household incomes and contribute to higher living standards in regional communities.

However, relocating industries to regional areas can have a detrimental impact on the local environment. As large industrial facilities require considerable amounts of land and supporting infrastructure, their development may involve clearing previously undeveloped areas for factories, warehouses and roads. Furthermore, increased industrial activity can generate additional waste and harmful emissions in areas that may previously have experienced relatively low levels of pollution. As a result, natural habitats may be damaged, and the overall environmental quality of these regions could decline.

In conclusion, moving large companies and industries to regional areas can benefit local communities by creating jobs and increasing household incomes. However, such relocation may also place considerable pressure on the environment through land development, waste and industrial emissions.

## 第380篇

Band 6.5

### 题目

Some people think young people should be required to have full time education until they are at least 18 years old. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

It is often argued that youngsters should be required to remain in full-time education until they reach the age of 18. I completely agree with this view, given that prolonged education not only provides adolescents with a stronger academic foundation, but also helps them to make more informed career decisions for the future.

The first major reason why young people should remain in education until the age of 18 is that it gives them sufficient time to obtain essential academic and social skills. Subjects, such as mathematics, chemistry and languages provide students with knowledge that may be applied to both career and higher education. Furthermore, those years help them to develop critical thinking, problem-solving and communication skills. For example, a pupil who continues studying mathematics and English tends to solve practical problems and express ideas easily. Therefore, compulsory education can substantially improve their academic and professional prospects.

Another compelling argument in favour of this view is that extending education can prevent learners from making premature career decisions. Teenagers often have limited information about the labour market and have not discovered their own strengths and interests. If they leave school too early, they may accept low-skilled jobs, thereby having several difficulties, say not adapting to the working environment or insufficient income. For example, in his mid-teens juvenile can work in any unskilled position, but his status and qualifications may remain restricted or limited, whereas two additional years of education may allow them to explore different subjects and identify a profession that genuinely suits their abilities. As a result, they can make exact and well-informed decisions about their future.

To conclude, I completely agree that young people should be required to remain in full-time education until the age of 18.

## 第381篇

### 分数

Band 6.5

### 题目

some people view the conflict between teenagers and parents as a necessary part of growing up, while others view it as something negative which should be avoided. discuss both views and give your own opinion. five reasons for your answer and include any relevant example from your knowloedge or experience.

### 文章

It is often argued that disagreements between teenagers and their parents are a normal and necessary part of growing up. However, others believe that family conflict is harmful and should be avoided. In my opinion, some disagreement is useful because it helps teenagers become independent, but serious and continuous conflict should be prevented.

There are several reasons why conflict can be considered a natural part of adolescence. First, teenagers gradually develop their own opinions and want more independence. As a result, they may disagree with their parents about clothes, friends, schoolwork or the time they should come home. This can help them learn how to express their ideas and make their own decisions. Second, arguments can improve communication if both sides discuss their feelings calmly. For example, a teenager who explains why they want to choose a particular course may help their parents understand their goals. In this way, conflict can lead to greater trust and a more mature relationship.

On the other hand, frequent arguments can have negative effects. One problem is that constant conflict may cause stress and sadness for both teenagers and parents. Teenagers who feel that they are always criticised may lose confidence or become secretive. Another disadvantage is that serious conflict can damage family relationships. In extreme cases, young people may spend more time away from home or make risky decisions simply to show their independence. Therefore, although small disagreements are normal, aggressive shouting and personal insults should be avoided.

In my view, conflict is not completely negative. It is an important part of growing up because teenagers need to separate themselves from their parents and develop their own identity. Nevertheless, disagreements should be controlled through respectful conversation and clear rules. For instance, in many families, parents allow their children to choose their hobbies while still setting reasonable limits on study and bedtime. This can reduce unnecessary arguments.

In conclusion, conflict can teach teenagers independence and communication skills, but excessive conflict may cause stress and weaken family relationships. Therefore, healthy disagreement should be accepted, while destructive arguments should be avoided.

### 分数

Band 6.5

### 题目

Some teenagers spend more time reading books, while others prefer to read online newspapers. The former group is likely to develop creative imaginations and have a much better grasp of language skills. Do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

The statement posits that teenagers who engage with physical books tend to develop more creative imaginations and superior language skills compared to those who read online newspapers. This essay will explore the merits of this assertion, arguing in agreement while providing a nuanced perspective.

Overall, while reading on screens offers convenience and access to modern tools, traditional book reading fosters deeper cognitive engagement and linguistic proficiency. The generational divide in reading habits further underscores these differences.

Firstly, adolescents from Generation Alpha exhibit a pronounced shift towards digital reading, owing to the portability and multifunctionality of smartphones. They adeptly navigate application menus to access e-books, which can stimulate their imagination through interactive features and multimedia content. However, this reliance on technology may paradoxically hinder their engagement with traditional books, as those habituated to screens are less likely to frequent school libraries or immerse themselves in linear narratives that demand sustained concentration. Consequently, while digital reading enhances certain cognitive skills, it may not inherently cultivate the same depth of creative imagination as physical books.

In contrast, elderly individuals often prefer print newspapers during their daily routines, such as enjoying coffee at home, as exemplified by cultural practices in Indonesia where newspapers accompany morning rituals. This demographic, having been educated in an era without widespread smartphone use, lacks familiarity with digital platforms, thereby sustaining their reading habits through physical media. Despite access to information, this generational gap in technology adoption has reinforced distinct reading preferences, with older adults relying on traditional formats that may be less conducive to linguistic evolution. However, this does not negate the value of digital reading for younger generations; rather, it highlights a divergence in linguistic and imaginative development shaped by technological exposure.

The adverse effect of sugar on health is well known to the public now. Some believe that the government should control the amount of sugar people consume. Others think that it is the responsibility of an individual to monitor their sugar intake. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

### 文章

The harmful effects of excessive sugar consumption are now well documented. Some people believe that governments should control how much sugar the public consumes, for example by taxing high-sugar products, whereas others argue that adults should make their own decisions while understanding the consequences. In my view, both sides are partly right. Governments should discourage excessive sugar consumption through measures such as taxes, but adults should ultimately be free to make their own choices.

Many children consume high-sugar products every day, which can lead to diabetes or obesity in the long term. Diabetes can affect their life permanently, as they may need to check their blood sugar three or four times a day, and later in life some may even lose a foot. Obesity affects their daily life through low energy, difficulty getting out of bed, breathing problems, and being physically unable to do everyday tasks. One way to protect children's health is to tax high-sugar products aimed at children, so that parents are less likely to buy products that harm them.

However, some adults use high-sugar products to get the energy they need for intense weightlifting, and taxing these products would be unfair to them. Unlike children, adults are capable of weighing the risks and deciding what is right for their own bodies. If governments begin controlling what adults eat, it could lead to further restrictions on personal freedom.

In conclusion, governments should protect children from the harmful effects of sugar, for example through taxes on products aimed at them. Adults, however, should remain free to make their own choices, as they are able to understand the consequences.

With the increasing number of environmental issues, it is often argued that addressing them is the responsibility of governments. Although governments can have a significant impact on these problems, I believe that protecting the environment is a shared responsibility between the state and individuals.

On the one hand, governments have various tools that can help address environmental issues. They have the financial resources to invest in projects that benefit the ecosystem, such as afforestation programmes. In addition, they have the authority to introduce laws that reduce harmful emissions by, for example, increasing fuel prices or imposing penalties on offenders. For instance, the Saudi government implements the Wildlife Protection Law, which sets penalties for activities that harm wildlife, such as overhunting and deforestation. On the other hand, individuals should also take responsibility for protecting the planet. They can also sort their waste and place it in the appropriate recycling bins, which can reduce the amount of rubbish that ends up harming marine life. Furthermore, people can limit their use of private cars by using public transport, thereby reducing harmful emissions.

In conclusion, I believe that addressing environmental problems is a shared responsibility between governments and individuals. While authorities have the power and resources to make large-scale changes, individual actions are equally important in protecting the environment.

## 第393篇

### 分数

Band 6.5

### 题目

The growing number of overweight people is putting a strain on the health care system in an effort to deal with the health issues involved. Some people think that the best way to deal with this problem is to introduce more physical education lessons in the school curriculum. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

The escalating number of obese individuals burdening the healthcare system in an effort to deal with the health complications involved has become a controversial topic. Many people argue that introducing more physical education lessons in the school curriculum is the best way to solve the problem, while others hold opposing views. As far as I am concerned, I strongly disagree with the former claim. This essay will present my viewpoint and opinions.

To begin with, I believe that implementing more physical education classes in the education system will not automatically lead to a decline in the population's obesity rate, since external factors such as diet and daily routines will not be taken into account. For example, although students may engage in higher levels of physical activity at school, their unhealthy eating habits outside school may remain unchanged. Moreover, obesity can be a hereditary trait, which means that some aspects are fundamentally unalterable due to genetics.

Furthermore, whether students are physically active beyond the classroom is outside the school's control. Since students come from different families with varying lifestyles, there is no guarantee that all of them will adopt habits that are beneficial for their health. With that said, fully addressing the issue of obesity requires utmost cooperation between educational institutions, families, and healthcare providers.

Additionally, physical education lessons may not be effective for every student, as a minority may have medical conditions, such as asthma, that limit their ability to participate in high-impact exercises. Therefore, simply increasing the amount of time allocated to physical education lessons will not ensure that students develop health-conscious habits in the long run.

To summarize, I reject the idea that increasing the number of physical education lessons is the most effective way to tackle obesity, as unhealthy dietary patterns, lifestyles, and biological factors also play significant roles in this issue.

## 第394篇

### 分数

Band 6.5

### 题目

The number of older people is increasing. Some people think this is causing problems in their countries while others feel that older people play an important role in society. Discuss both views and give your opinion

### 文章

A growing proportion of the population in many countries is now elderly, a demographic shift that has generated considerable debate. While some argue that older people make an invaluable contribution to society through their experience and expertise, others contend that an ageing population places a substantial burden on governments. Although the elderly can provide significant social and professional benefits, I believe that the financial and institutional pressures associated with population ageing are ultimately more consequential.

On the one hand, older people can make an important contribution to society because they possess knowledge and experience that cannot easily be acquired through formal education. In many professions, senior employees play a crucial role in mentoring younger colleagues, passing on practical expertise and helping them develop sound professional judgement. Beyond the workplace, older generations can also contribute to their communities through volunteering, childcare and other forms of social participation. Their experience and maturity can therefore strengthen both professional institutions and society more broadly. Nevertheless, technological developments have made it increasingly possible to preserve and disseminate knowledge through digital training programmes, online courses and recorded tutorials. As a result, some of the functions traditionally performed by experienced workers can now be replicated or supplemented by technology.

On the other hand, an ageing population can create significant economic and social pressures, particularly when the number of retirees rises relative to the working-age population. Older people are generally more likely to require healthcare and long-term social care, both of which can be extremely expensive to provide. Governments must also finance pensions and other retirement benefits, while a shrinking workforce may result in a smaller tax base with which to fund these services. Consequently, public expenditure may have to be redirected towards pensions, healthcare and social care at the expense of other essential areas such as education, infrastructure and investment. In countries where population ageing is particularly pronounced, this imbalance can place considerable strain on public finances and on younger generations who are required to support a growing retired population.

In conclusion, older people undoubtedly provide society with valuable experience, knowledge and social contributions, and their role should not be underestimated. However, I believe that the rapid growth of the elderly population creates greater long-term challenges, particularly because of rising healthcare and pension costs and the increasing financial pressure placed on the working-age population. Governments should therefore seek to benefit from the experience of older citizens while simultaneously implementing policies that make ageing societies economically sustainable.

There are a lot of people who think that online-based courses are a good alternative to attendance-based courses. While some individuals agree with the former view, others argue that studying at a university is crucial. In my opinion, while traditional university education offers vital interactive benefits, I believe internet-based courses represent a superior alternative overall due to their convenience and financial efficiency.

On the one hand, studying online offers profound advantages regarding flexibility and personal productivity. Principally, it enables learners to construct adaptable schedules, allowing them to balance academic pursuits with work or family commitments. Educational observations consistently show that the prospect of managing one's own pace is a primary cause of student ambition, driving learners to master time management while acquiring knowledge. Furthermore, by removing the necessity of daily commuting, online education not only saves substantial transportation costs but also converts hours previously wasted in transit into valuable study time, thereby enhancing overall academic output.

On the other hand, proponents of university-based learning argue that the quality of education is substantially higher in a traditional campus setting. Physical classrooms foster an environment of active engagement where instructors can observe students' body language, instantly gauge comprehension, and adapt their teaching methods accordingly. Moreover, the interactive nature of campus life allows for immediate academic feedback, collaborative group discussions, and a structured discipline that is difficult to replicate in an isolated online environment.

In conclusion, I firmly believe that internet-based courses offer a more practical solution for the modern learner due to the independence, flexible scheduling, and cost efficiency they provide. Nevertheless, traditional universities retain a crucial role for those who require direct peer interaction, real-time feedback, and structured academic accountability.

## 第400篇

### 分数

Band 6.5

### 题目

To meet the growing needs of food for the increasing population, country should make use of edible insects as foods. However, some people believe that insects are not only unhealthy but affect negatively the nature too. What are the benefits and drawbacks of eating insects? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

### 文章

The prospect of using edible insects as an alternative food source to accommodate the growing global demand for food has attracted considerable attention in recent decades. Although insects could provide a sustainable and nutrient-rich source of food for an expanding population, concerns have been raised regarding their potential implications for human health and the environment. This essay will examine the contribution of insect consumption to food security, while also considering the associated health and ecological risks.

Firstly, edible insects can provide a valuable source of protein while requiring substantially fewer resources than conventional livestock farming. By developing large-scale insect farming, countries could diversify their food supplies while alleviating pressure on increasingly scarce agricultural resources. This could be particularly advantageous in regions where conventional meat production is prohibitively expensive or constrained by the limited availability of arable land. From my own experience, crickets can be reared in relatively confined spaces and processed into protein-rich flour, which can subsequently be incorporated into a variety of everyday foods. This demonstrates that insect farming could offer a resource-efficient and potentially sustainable means of increasing food production. Therefore, incorporating edible insects into human diets may make a significant contribution to long-term food security.

Nevertheless, widespread insect consumption could pose considerable health and environmental risks in the absence of stringent regulation. Certain individuals may be susceptible to allergic reactions, while insects processed or stored under unsanitary conditions could become contaminated and potentially hazardous for human consumption. Furthermore, the excessive harvesting of wild insects could disrupt delicate ecosystems and adversely affect biodiversity. For example, removing substantial insect populations from their natural habitats could deprive insect-eating birds and other species of an essential food source, potentially disrupting established food chains. This illustrates how unregulated harvesting could have far-reaching ecological consequences. Therefore, rigorous food-safety standards and sustainable production methods are indispensable if insect consumption is to be expanded safely.

In conclusion, edible insects could constitute a nutritious and resource-efficient alternative to conventional sources of protein, thereby helping to accommodate the dietary needs of a growing population. Nevertheless, stringent safety regulations and environmentally sustainable farming practices are essential to mitigate potential health hazards and ecological damage.

## 第402篇

### 分数

Band 7.0

### 题目

Globalisation has led to the spread of multinational companies in all corners of the world. Some people think this is a positive development, while others disagree. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

### 文章

The proliferation of multinational corporations across the globe has generated polarised opinions regarding its impact on local economies and cultures. While these companies bring undeniable economic benefits, I believe their presence requires careful regulation to prevent the erosion of local business ecosystems and cultural identity.

The advantages of multinational expansion are primarily economic. These corporations create employment opportunities in regions where jobs may otherwise be scarce, often paying wages above local averages and providing training that develops the workforce. They introduce efficient business practices, advanced technology, and supply chain infrastructure that can modernise local industries. Consumers benefit from greater product variety, competitive pricing, and consistent quality standards that smaller domestic companies may struggle to match.

Conversely, the dominance of global brands can devastate local commerce. Small businesses frequently cannot compete with the pricing power and marketing budgets of international giants, leading to closures that hollow out traditional high streets and markets. This economic displacement often accompanies cultural homogenisation — identical coffee shops, fashion retailers, and fast-food chains replace distinctive local establishments that reflect community character. Furthermore, profits generated by multinationals are typically repatriated to headquarters abroad rather than being reinvested in the host economy.

My position is that globalisation through multinational presence is neither inherently positive nor negative — its impact depends entirely on governance. Countries that enforce fair competition laws, mandate local hiring quotas, and protect culturally significant businesses can harness economic benefits while preserving what makes their communities distinctive.

## 第403篇

### 分数

Band 7.0

### 题目

Some people believe that unpaid community service should be a compulsory part of secondary school education. To what extent do you agree or disagree? Some people believe that unpaid community service should be a compulsory part of secondary school education. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

Compulsory community service for secondary school students is increasingly proposed as a way to build civic responsibility. While I understand the appeal of this idea, I believe that making it obligatory is likely to undermine the very values it is meant to instil. Advocates of mandatory volunteering argue that teenagers who contribute to their communities develop empathy and practical skills that formal education rarely provides. Working in a food bank or a care home, for instance, exposes young people to social realities they would not otherwise encounter. There is a reasonable case that structured exposure to these environments benefits character development. However, the compulsory nature of such programmes is their central weakness. Volunteering, by definition, is a freely chosen act. When students are required to complete service hours under threat of academic penalty, the activity shifts from civic engagement to bureaucratic obligation. Research in behavioural psychology suggests that external compulsion frequently diminishes intrinsic motivation, a concept known as the "overjustification effect." Students may complete their hours without internalising any of the intended values, or worse, they may come to associate helping others with resentment. A more effective approach would be to make community service available and actively encouraged, with schools partnering local organisations and offering recognition for participation. This preserves the voluntary character of the activity while broadening access to it. In conclusion, although community service has genuine educational value, compulsion defeats its own purpose. Schools should create conditions in which students want to participate, rather than ones in which they are simply obliged to.

## 第406篇

### 分数

Band 7.0

### 题目

Some people say that the best way to improve public health is by increasing the number of sports facilities. Others, however, say that this would have little effect on public health and that other measures are required. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

### 文章

Public health remains a critical concern for governments worldwide, and the role of sports infrastructure in promoting physical well-being is frequently debated. While expanding sports facilities can encourage active lifestyles, I would argue that a multifaceted approach combining infrastructure with education and policy changes is considerably more effective.

Advocates of building more sports facilities contend that accessibility is the primary barrier to exercise. When gyms, swimming pools, and playing fields are readily available within communities, residents are more likely to incorporate physical activity into their routines. Research consistently demonstrates that proximity to exercise facilities correlates positively with activity levels, particularly in lower-income areas where residents cannot afford private gym memberships. The visibility of these facilities also serves as a constant reminder of the importance of physical fitness.

Nevertheless, simply constructing buildings does not guarantee usage. Many existing sports centres operate well below capacity, suggesting that the barriers to exercise are psychological and cultural rather than purely logistical. People who work long hours may lack the energy or motivation to exercise regardless of facility availability. Additionally, public health encompasses far more than physical activity — nutrition, mental health, preventive healthcare, and pollution reduction all play vital roles that sports facilities cannot address.

In conclusion, while improved sports infrastructure forms one component of a public health strategy, governments should simultaneously invest in health education programmes, subsidise nutritious food options, and implement workplace wellness policies. Only through this comprehensive approach can meaningful improvements in population health be achieved.

## 第407篇

### 分数

Band 7.0

### 题目

A portion of the human population believes that criminal behaviour has its roots in genes. Others think that circumstances lead people to commit crimes. Discuss your take on both views and put forward your opinions.

### 文章

Whether criminal behaviour is inherited through genes or influenced by a person's surroundings has been a subject of debate. While some people believe that genetics play an important role in shaping human behaviour, others argue that social and environmental circumstances are the main causes of crime. I believe that although genes may influence certain personality traits, criminal behaviour is primarily the result of a person's upbringing, education, and living conditions.

Those who support the genetic theory argue that some individuals may inherit personality traits such as aggression, impulsiveness, or poor emotional control, which could increase the likelihood of engaging in criminal activities. According to this view, these inherited characteristics make certain people more prone to violence or antisocial behaviour than others. Supporters also point to scientific research suggesting that genetics can influence human behaviour to some extent. However, possessing these traits does not necessarily mean that a person will become a criminal.

On the other hand, many people believe that crime is largely influenced by external circumstances. Poverty, unemployment, lack of education, family violence, substance abuse, and negative peer pressure often push individuals towards illegal activities. Children who grow up in unstable families or crime-ridden neighbourhoods may consider criminal behaviour to be normal because of the environment in which they are raised. For example, a teenager who lacks educational opportunities and is surrounded by gangs is more likely to become involved in criminal activities than someone raised in a stable and supportive environment.

In my opinion, environmental factors play a much greater role than genetics in determining whether a person becomes a criminal. Even if someone has inherited aggressive tendencies, proper parenting, quality education, counselling, and positive social support can help them develop into responsible citizens. Likewise, many people with no genetic predisposition to violence may still commit crimes if they experience severe social or economic hardship. Therefore, governments should focus on improving education, reducing poverty, and strengthening family and community support systems to prevent crime.

In conclusion, although genetics may influence certain aspects of personality, I believe that criminal behaviour is mainly shaped by social and environmental circumstances. By addressing the root causes of crime through education, employment opportunities, and community support, society can reduce criminal behaviour more effectively than by focusing solely on genetic factors.

## 第409篇

### 分数

Band 7.0

### 题目

Some people think that all university students should study whatever they like. Others believe that they should only be allowed to study subjects that will be useful in the future, such as those related to science and technology. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

### 文章

The question of whether university students should have complete freedom in choosing their subjects or be directed towards practically useful fields is a matter of ongoing debate. While there are compelling arguments for guiding students towards market-relevant disciplines, I believe that academic freedom, balanced with career awareness, produces the most well-rounded graduates.

Proponents of restricting choices to applied subjects argue that higher education represents a significant investment of public and private resources. From this perspective, it seems logical that graduates should emerge with skills that directly contribute to economic productivity. Countries facing skills shortages in engineering, healthcare, or technology may struggle to compete globally if too many students pursue subjects with limited employment prospects. Furthermore, students themselves may benefit from studying disciplines with clearer career pathways, reducing the risk of unemployment after graduation.

However, limiting academic choice overlooks several critical factors. Innovation frequently emerges at the intersection of diverse fields — philosophy informs artificial intelligence ethics, history shapes political policy, and psychology underpins user experience design. A society composed entirely of technical specialists would lack the critical thinkers, artists, and communicators who enrich cultural life and challenge established norms. Moreover, students who are passionate about their chosen field tend to achieve higher academic standards and develop transferable skills such as analysis, communication, and creative problem-solving.

In my view, universities should maintain broad subject availability while ensuring students receive honest guidance about employment realities. This approach respects individual agency while acknowledging practical considerations, ultimately producing graduates who are both fulfilled and employable.

In conclusion, water is a vital natural resource that needs to be protected as well. Free access to clean water for everybody is an ideal dream, but it doesn't exist in an achievable reality. I support the authority make a legislation to let users pay for their water consumption. Ultimately, the clean water can be preserved for this thirsty crowd who have no clean water for drinking.

## 第414篇

### 分数

Band 7.0

### 题目

Ambition is a positive quality for people to have in society today. How important is it for people who want to succeed in life? Is it a positive or negative characteristic?

### 文章

Being ambitious is one of the important qualities of human behaviour. While some people believe that excessive ambition can lead to unhealthy competition or stress, I believe that ambition is essential for achieving success and is, overall, a highly positive characteristic when balanced with ethical values and responsibility.

Ambition plays a crucial role in helping people accomplish their goals. It motivates individuals to work hard, overcome challenges, and continuously improve their skills. Without ambition, many people may lack the determination needed to pursue higher education, build successful careers, or start their own businesses. For example, entrepreneurs often invest years of effort and perseverance before achieving success. Their ambition encourages them to learn from failures, adapt to changing circumstances, and remain focused on their long-term objectives. Similarly, students with ambitious goals are generally more motivated to study consistently and perform well in examinations.

Ambition is predominantly a positive trait because it inspires people to realise their full potential and make meaningful contributions to society. Ambitious individuals are more likely to develop innovative ideas, create employment opportunities, and improve the quality of life for others through their achievements. For instance, Elon Musk, the CEO of Tesla, one of the leading producers of electric vehicles. Amid widespread scepticism and doubt when he first launched his ideas for an EV brand, Musk’s passionate ambition enabled him to go beyond the status quo and successfully transform the automobile landscape. In recent years, most automobile producers have followed in his footsteps and attempted to launch their own EV versions. 

However, one must be mindful of their health, as being overly ambitious can lead to overwork and exhaustion. It is not uncommon to see ambitious people achieving success at the expense of their mental and physical health. Therefore, ambition should always be accompanied by integrity, compassion, and a sense of social responsibility. It is essential for individuals to maintain a balance and take care of their health.

In conclusion, ambition is one of the vital quality that can dictate a person’s success. Nonetheless, ambitious individuals should pay attention to their health and manage to balance work and life to avoid jeopardizing their well-being on the road to success.

As a fan of those competitions, I agree with the idea that sporting events can be necessary for international relations and national unity, but only partially, because such events can have unintended effects on relationships between countries.

We all realized that they were very normal sports fans even though they were occasionally very secretive. Through the sports, two divided nations could reduce their political and ideological tensions and could feel the patriotic unity.

On the other hand, some sports matches can make international relations worse. Even much worse scenario is that the troubles caused by losing games affect the players directly.

In conclusion, I think that international sporting occasions can be one of the good ways to ease tensions or to release patriotism safely. However, I believe that games can not be the fundamental ways for the sound patriotism or peaceful international relations.

## 第422篇

### 分数

Band 7.0

### 题目

Demand of food is increasing worlwide. What are the causes of this? What measures can the international community take to make sure the food supply is enough?

### 文章

The need for food is increasingly rising globally. This essay attempts to shed light on the causes of this trend before suggesting some solutions to ensure that there is enough food supply.

The foremost reasons for the increasing food demand are population and globalisation. In recent ages, the number of newborn individuals has experienced a dramatic growth, which requires an enormous supply of food to nurture babies. That of animals simultaneously mirrors such a pattern, demanding enough diet to serve human benefits, including eating itself. Globalisation is also the root cause of this trend. Eating is no longer a habit for mere survival, but has turned into an international culture through exchanged foreign food and worldwide social media. By capturing delicious images of desserts, mastering new, rare, local dishes, or presenting luxury meals, more diverse, exotic cuisines are becoming desired and attracting millions to experience them. 

There are some possible measures to ensure the availability of food for the international community. The priority solution is to maintain open trade and fair distribution flowing across the world. Major food exporting nations should continue to provide internation market and consumers, while importing countries must keep ports and borders open, ensuring proper food safety provisions are in place. China is a strong example, which helps sustain market access through its green channels policy, enabling food to be fast-tracked both within provinces and at ports. Furthermore, the food and land use sector should be properly funded with the long-term capital and incentives needed to reward the supply of nutritious, affordable food. Investments can focus on increasing the resilience and diversity of food supply chains, reducing food loss and waste, developing regional food systems, providing vital social protection to farmers and to rural communities, accelerating greater digitisation and transparency across the value chain and rebuilding natural capital. This point must not be overlooked; there is no viable long-term response to the COVID-19 pandemic without the protection and restoration of the world’s critical remaining ecosystems, and a concerted effort to curb the wildlife trade.

In conclusion, the global world nowadays has met with surging food requirements, which can be attributed to a booming population and worldwide integration. With external trade and investment in diverse food and land, we can ultimately avoid a food crisis and ensure its availability.

More recently, artificial intelligence has begun to influence areas such as healthcare, education and employment, suggesting that the impact of modern technology will continue to grow.

In conclusion, earlier technological inventions undoubtedly brought revolutionary changes, particularly through improvements in  electricity, transport and communication. In conclusion, there are various indicators that are considered when defining a well-developed country, including advanced infrastructure, policies, and educational equality. ## 第430篇

### 分数

Band 7.0

### 题目

English is now widely used as the main language of education, especiallyin the education systems of some non-English speaking countries. Doyou think it is a positive or negative development?

### 文章

English has increasingly become the principal medium of instruction in many education systems, particularly in countries where it is not the native language. Although some people worry that this trend may marginalise local languages and weaken cultural identity, I believe its long-term benefits outweigh its disadvantages. By providing access to global knowledge and developing internationally valued skills, English-medium education contributes significantly to both educational and economic development. 

The main advantage of English-medium education is t hat it gives students direct access to the world's most important academic resources . As English is the dominant language of scientific research and higher education, students can read original research papers, internationally recognised textbooks and digital learning materials without relying on translations. It also helps learners develop an international academic perspective and participate in global research communities. For example, universities in Singapore have successfully adopted English as a principal teaching language, enabling graduates to pursue further study and collaborate internationally. As a result, English-medium education broadens educational opportunities and strengthens students' long-term academic competitiveness.

 It also brings considerable economic benefits. In today's globalised economy, employers increasingly value graduates who can communicate across linguistic and cultural boundaries. Studying in English equips students with transferable skills that improve their employability and prepare them for careers in multinational companies and international organisations. At the national level, a workforce with strong English proficiency attracts foreign investment, encourages technological cooperation and supports sustainable economic growth. Singapore's development into a regional financial and technological centre demonstrates how English-medium education can strengthen both human capital and national competitiveness. 

Admittedly, relying heavily on English may reduce the use of local languages and create difficulties for students with weaker educational backgrounds. However, these problems can be addressed through bilingual education which enables students to develop global communication skills while preserving their linguistic heritage and cultural identity. 

In conclusion, although English-medium education presents certain linguistic and cultural challenges, these are manageable and outweighed by its substantial advantages. By expanding access to global knowledge, enhancing students' career prospects and strengthening national competitiveness, it represents a highly positive development in today's interconnected world.

## 第436篇

### 分数

Band 7.0

### 题目

Extreme sports such as skydiving and rock climbing are very dangerous and should be banned. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this view?

### 文章

Extreme sports have gained immense popularity in recent years despite the risks they involve. While it is true that activities such as skydiving and rock climbing can result in serious injuries or even death, I disagree with the view that these sports should be banned. Instead, they should be carefully regulated to ensure participants' safety.

One of the main reasons why extreme sports should not be prohibited is that individuals have the right to choose how they spend their leisure time, provided that their actions do not harm others. Many people participate in these activities to challenge themselves, overcome fear, and improve their physical and mental resilience. Completing a difficult climb or a successful skydive often gives participants a sense of achievement and boosts their self-confidence. Therefore, banning such sports would unnecessarily restrict personal freedom.

Another important point is that extreme sports contribute significantly to local economies and the tourism industry. Popular destinations for activities such as mountain climbing, scuba diving, and bungee jumping attract thousands of domestic and international tourists every year. This creates employment opportunities for instructors, guides, equipment manufacturers, hotels, and local businesses. For example, many mountainous regions depend heavily on adventure tourism as a major source of income. A complete ban could therefore have negative economic consequences for these communities.

Admittedly, extreme sports involve considerable risks. Accidents may occur because of poor weather conditions, equipment failure, or a lack of proper training. However, these dangers can be greatly reduced by enforcing strict safety regulations, requiring professional supervision, and ensuring that participants use certified safety equipment. Governments should focus on improving safety standards rather than banning these activities altogether.

In conclusion, although extreme sports are inherently risky, I do not believe they should be banned. With appropriate regulations, professional training, and effective safety measures, people can continue to enjoy these activities while minimising the risks. Therefore, education and regulation are more practical solutions than prohibition.

## 第449篇

### 分数

Band 7.0

### 题目

In many countries, shopping is no longer just about buying what you need; it has become a popular hobby. Why is this the case? Is this a positive or negative development?

### 文章

In many parts of the world, shopping has evolved from a functional necessity into a leisure activity in its own right, with shopping malls now rivalling parks and cinemas as weekend destinations. This essay will consider why this shift has occurred and argue that, on balance, it represents a troubling development for both individuals and the environment.

Two forces have driven this change. The first is the sheer scale of modern retail: advances in manufacturing and global logistics mean that consumers are no longer choosing between a handful of options but between hundreds, each marketed with psychological precision through discounts, loyalty schemes and curated store layouts designed to prolong a visit. A quick trip for groceries can easily become an hour spent browsing clothing or electronics simply because the environment is engineered to encourage it. The second is the changing nature of urban life. As cities grow denser and public leisure space becomes scarcer or more expensive, shopping centres have filled the gap, offering air-conditioned comfort, social interaction and entertainment under one roof at little upfront cost to the visitor — even if no purchase is made.

I would argue that this normalisation of shopping as a pastime is largely negative. Psychologically, the act of buying triggers a short-lived dopamine response that can become habit-forming; when this response is repeatedly sought rather than the item itself, it fosters compulsive spending, mounting personal debt and clutter that serves no real purpose in people's lives. Environmentally, the consequences are more severe still. Goods purchased for the fleeting pleasure of acquisition, rather than genuine need, are disproportionately discarded soon after, swelling landfills and contributing to the plastic and textile waste already overwhelming natural ecosystems. A society that treats consumption as recreation is, in effect, normalising waste on an industrial scale.

In conclusion, the rise of shopping as a hobby stems from aggressive retail innovation and the erosion of low-cost public leisure options, but its psychological and environmental costs suggest this is a trend worth resisting rather than celebrating. Cultivating hobbies that do not depend on consumption would benefit both individual well-being and the planet.

In many countries, young people are leaving their homes in the countryside to live in large cities. Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?

### 文章

In many countries, increasing numbers of young people are moving from rural areas to large cities. Although this trend can create problems such as overcrowding and higher living costs, I believe that the advantages outweigh the disadvantages because cities offer greater employment, education and healthcare opportunities.

On the one hand, moving to large cities can provide young people with better opportunities for employment and personal development. Major urban areas usually contain a wider range of companies, industries and professional services than rural communities. For example, a young university graduate may move to a city to obtain an engineering or business job that is not available in his or her home village. This can provide a higher income and valuable experience for future career development. Cities also tend to offer better access to universities, training centres and specialised healthcare. As a result, migration can help young adults improve both their professional prospects and their quality of life.

On the other hand, large-scale migration to cities can create several problems. A rapid increase in population may raise demand for housing, which can make accommodation expensive and contribute to overcrowding. Traffic congestion may also become more serious when a large number of people commute within the same urban area. Nevertheless, these disadvantages can be reduced through effective urban planning, affordable housing and reliable public transport. Moreover, the benefits of better employment, education and healthcare can have a lasting effect on young people's future. Therefore, although rural-to-urban migration creates pressure on cities, its advantages are greater when appropriate planning is in place.

In conclusion, although the movement of young people to cities can cause overcrowding, high housing costs and traffic problems, I believe that the advantages outweigh the disadvantages. Better employment, education and healthcare opportunities can significantly improve young people's future prospects.

Besides that, they will be constantly dealing with the possibility of displacement. As they will be living in someone else's property , the lessor can end the leasing contract for justified or unjustified reasons, such as not paying the agreed rent, an agreement with new tenants , or even selling the property to another owner. For instance , it is common in some Middle Eastern countries for landowners to end the leasing contract with the tenant to re-lease the accommodation to a family member in need of a place.

Nonetheless , renting can be a great alternative in areas where accommodation prices are high or housing is scarce. It allows individuals to live in a desirable location without having to wait until they can afford to purchase a property there. Furthermore , renting provides greater flexibility, allowing people to change their homes as their needs evolve, whereas homeowners have to sell their property and find a suitable buyer before moving. For example , renting allows married couples to easily move to a larger property when they have children, while workers can relocate to accommodation closer to their workplace.

In conclusion, although renting can restrict tenants' freedom to customise their homes and expose them to the risk of eviction, it offers greater flexibility and allows people to live in desirable locations without the financial burden of purchasing a property .

## 第458篇

### 分数

Band 7.0

### 题目

In some countries the average weight of people is increasing and their level of health is decreasing. What do you think are the causes of these problems and what measures could be taken?

### 文章

In many countries, the average weight of the population is increasing, while people's overall health is gradually deteriorating. One major cause of this problem is the growing consumption of unhealthy fast food. However, I believe that imposing higher taxes on such food and increasing public awareness could help address this issue.

One of the main reasons for increasing obesity and declining health is the widespread consumption of fast food. Such food is generally inexpensive and easily accessible, making it particularly attractive to people with busy schedules who have limited time to prepare meals at home. Moreover, fast food often contains high amounts of calories, sugar, salt and unhealthy fats. Consequently, people who consume it regularly may take in more calories than their bodies require. This not only increases the likelihood of excessive weight gain but also raises the risk of developing serious health problems, such as heart disease and diabetes. Therefore, frequent reliance on fast food can have significant consequences for both people's weight and overall health.

Several measures can be taken to tackle this problem. Firstly, governments could impose higher taxes on unhealthy fast food, making it less affordable and therefore discouraging excessive consumption. If healthier alternatives become comparatively more affordable, consumers may be encouraged to make better dietary choices. Furthermore, governments should raise public awareness of the long-term health risks associated with unhealthy diets and obesity. Educational campaigns in schools, workplaces and through social media could help people understand the consequences of poor eating habits. As a result, individuals may become more motivated to reduce their consumption of unhealthy food and adopt a more balanced diet.

In conclusion, the increasing availability and consumption of inexpensive fast food are major contributors to rising obesity and deteriorating health. Higher taxation and greater public awareness could encourage healthier eating habits and ultimately improve public health.

## 第459篇

### 分数

Band 7.0

### 题目

In some countries, the government pays for health care. In others, the individual must pay for their own health care. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of each system.

### 文章

Countries use different methods to pay for health care. In some places, medical services are funded by the government, while in others, individuals are responsible for paying their own expenses. Both systems have significant advantages and disadvantages.

The main benefit of government-funded health care is that everyone can receive medical treatment regardless of their financial situation. People from low-income families can visit doctors and receive necessary treatment without worrying about the cost. This may also encourage patients to seek help at an early stage, preventing minor health problems from becoming more serious. However, providing free health care places considerable pressure on government budgets. The money must usually be collected through taxes, meaning that even healthy individuals contribute to the treatment of others. Furthermore, public hospitals may become overcrowded, leading to long waiting times and a lower quality of service.

A system in which individuals pay for their own health care also offers certain benefits. Private hospitals and clinics often compete with each other, which may encourage them to provide better services, modern equipment and shorter waiting times. This system also reduces government expenditure and allows public money to be spent on other important areas, such as education and transport. Nevertheless, the greatest disadvantage is that some people may be unable to afford essential treatment. Low-income individuals might delay visiting a doctor, while those who develop a serious illness could face severe financial difficulties. As a result, access to health care may depend on wealth rather than medical need.

In conclusion, government-funded health care provides equal access but can be expensive and inefficient, whereas individually funded care may offer faster and higher-quality services but create serious inequality. Therefore, a combined system may be the most effective approach, with governments covering essential treatment while individuals contribute towards additional or non-essential services.

## 第460篇

### 分数

Band 7.0

### 题目

In some countries, the use of surveillance cameras in public places is increasing. Some people think this is necessary for public safety, while others believe it infringes on personal privacy. Discuss both sides and give your own view.

### 文章

In recent years, there has been a growing trend towards the installation of surveillance cameras in public spaces. Proponents argue that this is essential for ensuring public safety, as it can deter criminal activities and aid law enforcement in solving crimes. Conversely, critics contend that such surveillance encroaches upon personal privacy, as it monitors individuals' daily movements without their explicit consent.

Those advocating for enhanced public safety maintain that surveillance cameras, especially in densely populated urban areas where crime rates are relatively high, serve as a powerful deterrent. The presence of CCTV can discourage potential offenders and provide invaluable evidence for law enforcement, thereby reducing crime and increasing the likelihood of prosecutions. For instance, in many major cities, CCTV footage has been instrumental in identifying and apprehending criminals, leading to safer streets and a greater sense of security among residents.

On the other hand, opponents of widespread surveillance raise valid concerns about the erosion of personal privacy. They argue that constant monitoring infringes upon an individual's right to go about their daily life without being observed, creating a 'Big Brother' society where citizens feel uneasy and distrustful. Moreover, the financial burden of installing and maintaining extensive CCTV networks can be substantial, potentially diverting resources from other crucial public services such as healthcare and education. For example, allocating a significant portion of the budget to surveillance systems in a developing country could hamper progress in essential sectors, thereby affecting the overall well-being of the population.

In my view, while the enhancement of public safety through surveillance is important, it should not come at the expense of fundamental privacy rights. The key lies in striking a balance: governments should implement surveillance measures judiciously, ensuring transparency, and adhere to strict data protection regulations. Additionally, the operation of such systems should be subject to independent oversight to prevent misuse. By adopting a responsible approach, societies can reap the benefits of increased security while safeguarding the privacy of their citizens.

### 题目

In the future, all cars, buses, and trucks will be driverless. The only people travelling inside these vehicles would be passengers. Do you think the advantages of driverless vehicles outweigh the disadvantages? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

### 文章

It is predicted that vehicles such as cars, buses and trucks will eventually become fully autonomous, with people travelling only as passengers. Although this development may cause job losses and create excessive dependence on technology, I believe its advantages outweigh the disadvantages because driverless vehicles could significantly improve road safety.

The primary advantage of driverless vehicles is that they could significantly improve road safety. A considerable number of road accidents are caused by human errors, such as speeding, distraction or driving under the influence of alcohol. Autonomous vehicles, however, are controlled by advanced computer systems that can not only follow traffic regulations consistently but also react quickly to potential dangers. As a result, fewer human errors may occur on the roads, leading to a reduction in traffic accidents and serious injuries. Ultimately, widespread use of autonomous vehicles could make travelling considerably safer for both passengers and other road users.

Nevertheless, the widespread adoption of autonomous vehicles could negatively affect employment, particularly among professional drivers. If buses, taxis and trucks operate without drivers, companies may no longer need to employ large numbers of people to operate these vehicles. Consequently, many professional drivers could lose their jobs and stable sources of income, placing considerable financial pressure on their families. However, this problem could be reduced through retraining programmes that enable affected workers to acquire new skills and secure employment in other industries. Therefore, although job displacement is a significant concern, it is potentially manageable compared with the long-term safety benefits of autonomous transportation.

In conclusion, although driverless vehicles may result in job losses among professional drivers, I believe their advantages are more significant. By reducing human error and preventing road accidents, autonomous vehicles could save lives and create a safer transportation system, while employment problems could be addressed through appropriate retraining programmes.

The chief excuse for my stance is that such a first step on the moon heralds humanity's power and motivates relentless effort to develop. In contrast to the past, when mankind was restricted by the earth itself, had no tools to reach the skies, and deemed planets and stars almost unfathomable, the journey to the moon broke our previous limits and showcased our strength in exploring and deciphering the unknown. The satisfying result emerging at the expense of these prices is indeed precious, a testament to meritocracy, where sacrifices can produce miracles at the end. Even after decades of that event, many, especially people working in astronomy, are still inspired and motivated to do tasks with challenges ahead, carrying a mindset of equivalent exchange - values are not created by nothing.

This is illustrated clearly in sectors like aerospace, commercial space flights (SpaceX or Blue Origin companies), medical tech, and the advanced image processing profession. The Apollo Guidance Computer pioneered the use of unproven integrated circuits to save weight, which helped spur the microchip revolution, leading to modern laptops, smartphones, and digital devices. Another case is that multi-layer reflective mylar insulation sheets were engineered to protect astronauts from extreme radiation and heat.These sheets were later packaged into lightweight emergency kits, marathon running wraps, and commercial home insulation. Such progress is undeniably impactful, changing our daily lives for the better convenience.

In conclusion, I fervently agree with the astronaut's highlight of the integral role of the travel to the moon. With its inspiration and practical applications to daily lives, it truly deserves the title of "one giant leap for mankind".
