## 第570篇

### 分数

Band 7.0

### 题目

Some people think the government should provide free housing, while others believe it is not the government's responsibility. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

### 文章

Whether the government should provide free housing to its citizens has been a subject of debate. While some people believe that housing is a basic human necessity and should be provided by the government, others argue that individuals should be responsible for securing their own accommodation. In my opinion, governments should assist low-income and vulnerable people with housing, but providing free homes to every citizen is neither practical nor financially sustainable.

On the one hand, supporters of free housing argue that everyone deserves a safe and secure place to live. Adequate housing improves people's health, safety, and overall quality of life. Without stable accommodation, families often struggle to access education, healthcare, and employment opportunities. Furthermore, vulnerable groups such as elderly people, individuals with disabilities, and low-income families may not be able to afford rising property prices or rental costs. Providing affordable or free housing to these groups can reduce homelessness and improve social equality.

On the other hand, many people believe that buying or renting a home is a personal responsibility. Governments already spend large amounts of public money on essential services such as healthcare, education, transportation, and national security. Offering free housing to every citizen would place an enormous financial burden on taxpayers and could reduce funding for these important sectors. Moreover, if housing were completely free, some people might become less motivated to work hard or save money to improve their living conditions.

In my opinion, the most effective approach is a balanced one. Governments should not provide free housing to everyone, but they should support people who genuinely cannot afford accommodation through affordable housing schemes, rental assistance, or subsidised home loans. At the same time, individuals who have the financial ability should take responsibility for meeting their own housing needs.

In conclusion, although safe housing is a basic necessity, I believe that providing free homes for every citizen is unrealistic. Instead, governments should focus their resources on helping disadvantaged people while encouraging those who can afford housing to become financially independent.

income inequality has become one of the most contentious issues in modern society. When wealth is distributed more equitably, people are more likely to have access to quality education, healthcare, and housing, regardless of their financial background. Furthermore, a narrower income gap can foster social harmony by reducing feelings of injustice and resentment that often arise in highly unequal societies. This, in turn, may contribute to lower crime rates, stronger community relationships, and improved mental well-being. In conclusion, although excessive income inequality can weaken social stability and reduce people's quality of life, maintaining a moderate difference in earnings is necessary to encourage ambition, recognise merit, and stimulate economic development. Therefore, I agree only to the extent that governments should reduce extreme income disparities while preserving a fair system that rewards ability and hard work

### 文章

In my opinion, the development of space tourism is largely a positive trend because it drives technological innovation and broadens human perspective, despite the environmental concerns it initially raises.

On the one hand, commercializing space flight acts as a powerful catalyst for scientific advancement. Private aerospace companies invest heavily in research to make rockets safer and more cost-effective, which accelerates breakthroughs in fields such as telecommunications, materials science, and renewable energy. For instance, reusable rocket technology pioneered by commercial ventures has drastically reduced the cost of launching satellites that monitor global climate change. Furthermore, this industry generates substantial economic growth and creates high-skilled engineering jobs.

On the other hand, critics argue that space tourism is a negative development due to its heavy environmental toll and socioeconomic inequality. Frequent rocket launches release significant amounts of carbon dioxide and black carbon into the upper atmosphere, potentially worsening global warming. Additionally, it currently remains an exclusive luxury for the ultra-wealthy, diverting financial resources away from pressing terrestrial crises like poverty and healthcare. However, history shows that early-stage technologies are often expensive and resource-intensive before becoming cleaner and more accessible to the general public over time.

In conclusion, although space tourism presents legitimate ecological and economic challenges, its long-term benefits in technological progress and inspiration outweigh the drawbacks.

Firstly, a robotic teacher made with artificial intelligence would lack sufficient control over its classroom students. For instance, it is widely known that kids need to be thoroughly watched by their teachers to be sure that they take their classwork seriously and do not fool around when classes are going on. Sadly, this is a task robotic teachers will be incapable of carrying out. Therefore, this makes it clear that classroom teachers will never be totally substituted by mechanisation.

Secondly, the learning process of students would be disrupted if they are taught by robotic teachers, which may slow down some students’ ability to comprehend information taught in lessons. Thus, it becomes apparent that human teachers will never be replaced by robotic teachers in a classroom.

To summarise, a robotic teacher does not have the necessary discipline to properly give instructions to students and actually works to retard the ability of a student to comprehend new lessons. Therefore, it is clear that the idea of running a classroom completely by a machine cannot be supported. ## 第583篇

### 分数

Band 7.0

### 题目

The animal species are becoming extinct due to human activities on land and in the sea. What are the reason and solution?

### 文章

Animal extinction is a major and widely believed contemporary threat to animals in continent and in aquatic ecosystems due to land pollution, aqueous contamination, habitat loss, and poaching. This essay will analyse and discuss the aforementioned reasons with the best possible solutions to demonstrate the arguments and points against this alarming situation.

Underlying factors of the drastic decline in the animal populations on the estate constitute a couple of reasons. Firstly, the zoological habitat destruction is followed by a sharp increment in the deforestation and urbanisation trends. Secondly, the irresponsible use of polythene bags, and harmful chemicals like pesticides. Thirdly, the poaching is causing a significant drop in the number of wild animals.

Aquatic species are at risk of elimination due to a number of causes. One of the key factors is water pollution, which involves the oil spillage within aquatic bodies. It causes respiratory and breeding problems for the fish and other aquatic biodiversity. Other main stimuli for the aquatic pollution are the overlooked disposal of contaminated water and industrial waste, which contains harmful compounds, in the natural aqua pura.

Sustainable solutions to prevent the animals in both environments need integrated approaches that include raising awareness against animal-habitat conservation through educational campaigns, enforcement of strict laws against poaching, and the control of dangerous chemical leakage in the clean aquatic settings. Polluted sewage should be treated properly before its release into the sea and rivers.

In conclusion, animal annihilation is a widely recognised threat which can be managed through proposed solutions for the above-discussed issues and the responsible behaviour of humans to protect the environment of other creatures.

The most important aim of science should be to improve people's lives. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement

### 文章

Science has always been a driving force behind the progress of humanity, and I wholeheartedly agree that its most important aim should be to improve people's lives. From the moment the first tools were crafted to make hunting and gathering easier, science has been dedicated to enhancing the quality of human existence.

One of the most evident ways science has improved lives is through medical advancements. In the past, diseases like smallpox and polio were rampant, causing widespread death and disability. However, through scientific research, vaccines were developed. Smallpox, for instance, has been eradicated globally, saving countless lives. This is a testament to how science can directly address life-threatening issues and improve the well-being of people. In modern times, research into cancer treatments is ongoing, and each new discovery, whether it's a more effective chemotherapy drug or a revolutionary immunotherapy technique, gives hope to patients and their families, improving their quality of life even in the face of a serious illness.

Another area where science has had a profound impact on people's lives is in technology. The invention of the internet, a result of scientific and technological research, has transformed the way we communicate, access information, and conduct business. People from remote areas can now connect with the world, access educational resources, and find job opportunities. For example, students in rural villages can take online courses from top universities around the world, expanding their knowledge and future prospects. This connectivity has also improved the lives of the elderly, who can now stay in touch with their families living far away through video calls.

Moreover, science has played a key role in environmental protection, which in turn improves people's lives. Scientists study climate change and develop solutions to mitigate its effects. Renewable energy sources, such as solar and wind power, are being developed and implemented, reducing our reliance on fossil fuels and improving air quality. Cleaner air means fewer respiratory diseases, directly benefiting the health of the population. Additionally, sustainable farming practices, developed through scientific research, ensure food security while protecting the environment, which is essential for the well-being of current and future generations.

In conclusion, science has an immense potential to improve people's lives, and making this its primary goal is not only logical but also necessary. By focusing on medical, technological, and environmental advancements, science can continue to enhance the quality of life for all.

## 第587篇

### 分数

Band 7.0

### 题目

The movement of people from agricultural areas to cities can cause serious problems in both places. What are the serious problems? What measures can be used to solve these problems?

### 文章

The relocation of citizens from rural to urban areas may result in grave issues , including the increasing of traffic volume and housing prices in the cities. However, regulating accommodations' costs by the state and building an efficient transportation system are two viable solutions.

Having individuals move from the countryside to the city will cause more traffic. Since urban zones are usually crowded, they have residents. Therefore, by welcoming more people, the traffic density will intensify subsequently, which will detrimentally affect the environment by releasing more toxic emissions into the atmosphere. Moreover, this will also increase the prices of living spaces, because of the high demand from the newcomers, thus, landlords will raise their prices, which will even impact the locals. For instance, in search of jobs, many Saudis from all around the country move to Riyadh , which has caused a surge in the cost of living spaces in the city.

The government can assess these challenges. First, it can control the prices of housing using the regulatory tools, by implementing laws against any unfair practises such as placing a limit on meter prices when selling living accommodations by real estate developers, or implementing taxes on landlords that increase accordingly with the prices of their rental units. Furthermore, the state can also build a public transportation system that is affordable and convenient , which could decrease the traffic flow since it will offer people  alternative methods of transportation rather than riding personal cars. For example, many capitals around the world , such as Riyadh, London, Paris and Tokyo, have efficient underground systems that serve the growing population of these cities.

In conclusion, although the movement of citizens from farming zones to cities has resulted in higher traffic rates and  higher housing costs, the government can confront these challenges by enforcing laws that control the accommodation prices and build an efficient public transportation system.

### 题目

The rise of convenience foods has helped people keep up with the speed of the modern life style. What are the advantages of this trend? Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?

### 文章

Nowadays, it has become easier to keep up with a fast-paced lifestyle due to the increasing availability of convenience foods. Although they are often accessible and affordable, I believe that the health concerns associated with this type of food and the low wages paid to employees in this industry outweigh the advantages.

One major advantage of ready meals is that it saves people considerable time while remaining affordable and widely available. It is particularly beneficial for individuals with fast-paced lifestyles, such as workers and travellers, who may not have enough time to prepare meals at home. Instead, they can quickly purchase ready-made food and use the time saved for work, travel, or other activities. Furthermore, prepackaged meals can be cheaper than purchasing fresh ingredients and preparing meals regularly, particularly when some groceries may expire within a few days. For instance, buying a salad from a restaurant can cost the same as purchasing four or more packets of instant noodles, making the latter a more affordable option for people with limited time or budgets.

On the other hand, the excessive consumption of convenience food can lead to various health problems. These products often contain preservatives, artificial colours, and inexpensive ingredients that allow them to remain fresh and affordable for longer. As a result, consuming them regularly instead of fresh food can negatively affect people's well-being over time. Moreover, the low prices of these products can also come at the expense of workers' wages, as manufacturers may employ low-paid workers to keep production costs down and maintain affordable prices. For instance, many prepackaged meals factories in the UAE employ migrants on relatively low wages to produce and export large quantities of goods to other Middle Eastern countries.

To conclude, even though ready meals are cheaper and easy to attain, I think that the health problems they may cause and the exploitative labour practices in the factories that produce these meals overshadow the advantages they offer.

Consequently, they may experience less stress and return to work feeling more energetic and motivated.

## 第593篇

### 分数

Band 7.0

### 题目

Today more and more tourists are visiting places where conditions are difficult, such as the Sahara desert or the Antarctic. What are the benefits and disadvantages for tourists who visit such places?

### 文章

Nowadays, an increasing number of tourists are visiting places with difficult conditions, such as the Sahara Desert and Antarctica. Although travelling to these destinations can provide unique experiences and educational benefits, it can also involve serious risks and high expenses.

One major benefit of visiting extreme destinations is that tourists can experience nature in a unique way. Unlike ordinary holidays in cities or popular tourist attractions, these places allow visitors to see unusual landscapes and wildlife. For example, tourists travelling to Antarctica can observe penguins, glaciers and other animals in their natural environment. Such experiences can also increase people's awareness of environmental issues and encourage them to protect nature.

Another advantage is that travelling to difficult destinations can help people develop confidence and independence. Visitors may need to deal with challenging weather conditions, long journeys and unfamiliar environments. Successfully managing these difficulties can be a rewarding personal experience. In addition, such trips can provide valuable knowledge about different ecosystems and cultures, particularly when tourists travel with experienced guides.

However, there are also several disadvantages. The most obvious one is the risk to tourists' health and safety. Extreme temperatures, dehydration, storms and difficult terrain can cause serious problems, especially for inexperienced travellers. For instance, a person travelling in the Sahara without sufficient water or proper guidance could become seriously dehydrated. Moreover, these holidays are often expensive because tourists may need specialist equipment, trained guides and carefully organised transportation.

In my opinion, visiting such destinations can be worthwhile if tourists are properly prepared and follow safety regulations. However, they should understand the risks and avoid travelling independently in dangerous environments. Tour operators and local authorities should also provide clear safety information and emergency support.

In conclusion, visiting places such as the Sahara Desert and Antarctica can offer unforgettable experiences, knowledge and personal growth. Nevertheless, the risks, high costs and challenging conditions mean that tourists need to prepare carefully before travelling to these destinations.

A small number of global streaming companies now decide which films and television series are made. Do you think this is a positive or a negative development?

### 文章

Commissioning power in film and television has concentrated in a handful of global platforms. I consider this a negative development, despite the fact that more programming is being made now than at any earlier point and that a great deal of it is good.

The gains are obvious and should not be dismissed. Platforms have the capital to fund expensive productions and the reach to turn a series made in Korean or Spanish into a worldwide success, which the older system of national broadcasters and export deals almost never managed. Writers and performers outside the English-speaking world now reach audiences that were previously closed to them, and viewers encounter work they would never otherwise have found. Subtitled drama, once a niche interest in most markets, now routinely reaches the largest audiences on these services, which no national broadcaster ever achieved.

The concern is not volume but the narrowing of the mechanism. When dozens of broadcasters and studios commissioned independently, a project rejected in one place could be taken to another, and the differences between their tastes were what allowed unusual work through. A small number of platforms using similar data and similar measures of success behave more like a single buyer than like many, so a project that fails their test fails everywhere at once. Cancellation after one season, which is common on the platforms, compounds this by making risk expensive for creators as well.

So the industry has more money, more output and fewer doors. I think that combination is negative, because variety in what gets made has always depended on variety in who decides, and that is precisely what has been lost. That is a structural change rather than a temporary one.

### 题目

More and more people are choosing to work from home rather than in a traditional office. Why is this happening? Do you think this is a positive or negative development?

### 文章

The shift towards remote working has accelerated dramatically in recent years, transforming how millions of professionals approach their careers. This trend is driven by technological advancement and evolving priorities, and while it presents certain challenges, I consider it a predominantly positive development for both individuals and society.

Several interconnected factors explain the migration from office to home. Most fundamentally, digital communication tools have eliminated the technical necessity of physical co-location for many knowledge-based roles. Video conferencing, cloud collaboration platforms, and project management software enable seamless coordination regardless of geography. Simultaneously, workers — particularly younger generations — increasingly prioritise flexibility, autonomy, and work-life integration over traditional markers of career success. The pandemic period demonstrated conclusively that productivity need not suffer outside conventional office environments, dismantling decades of managerial scepticism.

I view this development as largely beneficial for multiple reasons. Eliminating commutes saves workers considerable time and money while significantly reducing transport-related carbon emissions — a meaningful environmental dividend at scale. The geographical liberation of remote work enables skilled professionals to live in affordable regions rather than clustering in expensive urban centres, potentially reducing housing inequality. Companies benefit from access to global talent pools and reduced overhead costs. However, these advantages must be weighed against legitimate concerns: social isolation, difficulty maintaining professional boundaries, and the challenge of mentoring junior staff remotely demand thoughtful solutions.

Ultimately, the remote work revolution represents an evolution rather than a disruption. Organisations that develop hybrid models — combining the flexibility of remote work with purposeful in-person collaboration — will likely achieve optimal outcomes for both productivity and employee wellbeing.

## 第603篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

In many countries, the gap between the rich and the poor is widening. Some people argue that economic growth is the best way to reduce inequality, while others believe that direct government redistribution of wealth is more effective. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

### 文章

The widening wealth gap is one of the most pressing social issues of our time. While some economists maintain that sustained economic growth provides the most effective remedy, others contend that direct state intervention to redistribute resources is essential. Having considered both positions, I will argue that growth without redistribution is insufficient to achieve genuine equality.
Proponents of economic growth point to the dramatic poverty reductions achieved in rapidly developing nations. When economies expand, employment rises, wages increase, and the overall standard of living improves across social groups. South Korea's transformation from a low-income country in the 1960s to a high-income economy by the 1990s is frequently cited as evidence that growth can lift large populations out of deprivation. From this perspective, policies that stimulate investment and productivity offer a sustainable path to broader prosperity.
Nevertheless, a growing body of evidence suggests that growth alone does not automatically produce a fairer distribution of wealth. In many advanced economies, prolonged periods of expansion have coincided with sharper inequality, as the returns from investment have flowed predominantly to those who already possess assets. Consequently, direct redistribution through progressive taxation, social transfers, and investment in public education appears indispensable. Scandinavian countries, which combine strong market economies with robust welfare systems, consistently achieve the world's lowest inequality levels.
I am persuaded that both mechanisms must operate together. Economic growth generates the fiscal resources that make redistribution possible, yet without deliberate policy, the gains of growth become concentrated at the top. Governments must therefore pursue growth-oriented strategies while simultaneously ensuring that social investment distributes those gains more equitably.

The shift towards remote work has accelerated dramatically in recent years, fundamentally altering traditional employment patterns. While this arrangement presents certain challenges, I believe the advantages substantially outweigh the disadvantages for both employees and employers.

The benefits of working from home are numerous and significant. Employees save considerable time and money by eliminating daily commutes, which can amount to several hours per day in major cities. This recovered time can be invested in personal development, family relationships, or additional rest, leading to improved work-life balance and mental health. Furthermore, remote work offers unprecedented flexibility, allowing individuals to create optimal working environments tailored to their preferences and to better manage personal responsibilities such as childcare or elderly care. Studies have also shown that many remote workers report higher productivity levels due to fewer office distractions and the ability to work during their most productive hours.

However, remote work does present notable disadvantages. The lack of face-to-face interaction can hinder team cohesion and make collaborative projects more challenging. Some employees struggle with isolation and miss the social aspects of office life, which can negatively impact mental health and job satisfaction. The blurring of boundaries between work and personal life can lead to longer working hours and difficulty disconnecting from professional responsibilities. Additionally, not all homes are suitable for productive work, with issues such as inadequate space, poor internet connectivity, or family distractions potentially hampering performance. Career advancement may also suffer, as remote workers might have fewer opportunities for informal networking and may be overlooked for promotions in favor of more visible office-based colleagues.

Nevertheless, most disadvantages of remote work can be mitigated through proper management and technology. Regular video conferences can maintain team connections, co-working spaces can provide professional environments when needed, and clear boundaries can be established to separate work and personal time. As organizations continue to adapt and refine remote work policies, these challenges are becoming increasingly manageable.

In conclusion, while remote work presents genuine challenges, particularly regarding social isolation and work-life boundaries, the substantial benefits including flexibility, cost savings, and improved work-life balance clearly outweigh these drawbacks. ## 第606篇

Band 7.5

### 题目

An increasing number of students choose to complete their university degree in a foreign country rather than at home. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of this trend.

### 文章

Studying for a degree overseas has moved from being an unusual choice to being a mainstream one, particularly at postgraduate level. The trend brings real gains to the students who can afford it, but it also carries costs that fall on people other than the student.

For the individual, the advantages are substantial. A foreign university may simply teach a subject better, especially where the home system is under-resourced or where a specialism barely exists locally. Beyond the teaching, a degree taken abroad demands a kind of self-management that a degree taken from a childhood bedroom does not: administrative independence, functioning in a second language every day, and building a social network from nothing. Contacts matter too, since a graduate who has studied in another country leaves with references, acquaintances and a working knowledge of a second job market.

The disadvantages are more easily overlooked because they are not all borne by the student. Cost is the obvious one, and it is not only tuition: international fees are usually set well above domestic rates, and living costs abroad are paid without the family support that keeps domestic study affordable. Less obviously, when the most academically able students of a generation leave and a proportion of them do not return, the countries that educated them to eighteen carry the expense while another country collects the benefit.

Overall, the trend is clearly positive for those able to take part in it, and considerably more ambiguous for the societies they come from. It is worth remembering that access is uneven; a development that helps the students who already had the most options is not the same thing as a development that helps students.

## 第607篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Some people think that the best way to reduce crime is to give longer prison sentences. Others, however, believe there are better alternative ways of reducing crime. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

### 文章

Criminal justice policy represents one of the most contested areas of public debate, with opinions ranging from strictly punitive approaches to rehabilitation-focused alternatives. While longer prison sentences may serve certain limited purposes, I am convinced that evidence-based preventive measures offer far greater potential for sustained crime reduction.

The rationale for extended incarceration rests on two principles: deterrence and incapacitation. Theoretically, the prospect of lengthy imprisonment should discourage potential offenders from committing crimes, while those already convicted are physically prevented from reoffending during their sentence. This approach appeals to public sentiment, particularly following high-profile violent crimes where communities demand visible consequences. For genuinely dangerous individuals who pose ongoing threats to public safety, prolonged removal from society may indeed be the only responsible option.

However, extensive criminological research challenges the assumption that harsher sentences meaningfully deter crime. Recidivism rates in countries with punitive systems often exceed those in nations favouring rehabilitation, suggesting that prison environments may actually reinforce criminal behaviour rather than discourage it. Alternative approaches — community service programmes, restorative justice conferences, addiction treatment, educational opportunities, and early intervention in at-risk communities — address the root causes that drive individuals towards criminal activity. These measures are demonstrably more cost-effective than incarceration while producing lower reoffending rates.

In my assessment, effective crime reduction requires investing in upstream prevention rather than downstream punishment. A society that provides adequate education, mental health support, and economic opportunity will inevitably experience less crime than one which simply builds larger prisons. Incarceration should remain available for the most serious offences, but it cannot constitute a comprehensive crime strategy.

## 第608篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Many people argue that individuals are responsible for addressing environmental problems, while others believe that governments and large corporations bear the primary responsibility. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

### 文章

The question of who bears primary responsibility for reversing environmental deterioration is one of the most pressing of our time. While the individual-responsibility view has merit, I am persuaded that government policy and corporate regulation are the principal drivers of meaningful progress, with individual behaviour playing a supporting but ultimately secondary role.
Proponents of individual responsibility make a reasonable case. Consumer choices — from dietary patterns to transport habits to purchasing decisions — collectively shape demand, and if citizens consistently opt for lower-impact alternatives, markets respond accordingly. Countries with strong environmental awareness at the grassroots level have, in some cases, achieved notably cleaner cities and better recycling rates than those without such a culture.
Nevertheless, the structural argument is more compelling. Governments possess the unique authority to set binding emissions standards, price carbon, and redirect public investment towards renewable infrastructure at a scale no citizen campaign can match. The history of environmental regulation illustrates this clearly: catalytic converters, phased-out lead in petrol, and ozone-protection agreements were all achieved through legislation rather than voluntary behaviour change. Large corporations, which collectively account for the overwhelming majority of industrial emissions, will only adopt costly cleaner technologies consistently when required to do so by enforceable law.
In conclusion, while individual action is both ethically important and practically useful, only coordinated government policy and regulated corporate conduct can deliver environmental change at the necessary scale and speed.

## 第609篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Plastic pollution has become a serious environmental problem worldwide. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures can be taken to solve it?

### 文章

Plastic pollution has emerged as one of the most pressing environmental challenges of our time, threatening marine ecosystems and human health globally. This essay will explore the root causes of this crisis and propose viable solutions to address it.

The proliferation of plastic pollution stems from multiple interconnected factors. Primarily, the convenience and low cost of plastic products have led to their widespread adoption across industries, from packaging to consumer goods. Single-use plastics, such as shopping bags, bottles, and food containers, are particularly problematic as they are discarded after brief use but persist in the environment for centuries. Additionally, inadequate waste management infrastructure, especially in developing nations, means that much plastic waste ends up in rivers and oceans rather than being properly recycled or disposed of. Consumer behavior also contributes significantly, with many people lacking awareness about the environmental impact of their plastic consumption or the importance of proper disposal.

Several measures can be implemented to combat this growing problem. Governments should introduce legislation banning or heavily taxing single-use plastics, as successfully demonstrated in countries like Rwanda and Kenya. Simultaneously, investment in recycling infrastructure and waste management systems is crucial, particularly in regions where such facilities are lacking. Industries must be incentivized to develop and adopt biodegradable alternatives to conventional plastics, such as materials derived from plant sources that decompose naturally. Public education campaigns can raise awareness about plastic pollution's consequences and promote behavioral changes, such as using reusable bags and bottles.

Moreover, international cooperation is essential since plastic pollution transcends national boundaries. Global agreements similar to the Paris Climate Accord could establish binding targets for plastic reduction and ocean cleanup. Extended producer responsibility programs, where manufacturers bear the cost of managing their products' end-of-life disposal, could incentivize companies to design more sustainable products. Community-level initiatives, such as beach cleanups and plastic-free movements, can also contribute to both immediate waste removal and long-term cultural change.

In conclusion, plastic pollution results from our dependence on convenient disposable products combined with inadequate waste management. Addressing this crisis requires coordinated action including legislative measures, infrastructure development, innovation in materials, and fundamental changes in consumer behavior. Only through such comprehensive approaches can we hope to protect our planet from the mounting threat of plastic waste.

### 题目

All university undergraduate courses should include a period of time spent studying abroad or doing a work placement. Do you think the advantages of this would outweigh the disadvantages?

### 文章

Advantages and Disadvantages of Requiring Study or Work Placement Abroad for All Undergraduate Courses

The proposal to mandate international study or work placements for all undergraduates is increasingly advocated as a means to enhance graduate employability and global awareness. While such requirements entail significant logistical and financial challenges, I believe the long-term educational and professional benefits substantially outweigh these drawbacks, provided institutions implement equitable support mechanisms.

Admittedly, compulsory mobility programmes present notable disadvantages. Financially, they risk exacerbating inequality; students from low-income backgrounds may struggle with travel, accommodation, or lost part-time income, potentially forcing them into debt or discouraging enrolment altogether. Academically, integrating external placements into rigid curricula can disrupt course coherence, particularly in specialised fields like medicine or engineering where sequential learning is critical. Additionally, administrative burdens on universities - such as securing quality host organisations and ensuring academic credit transfer - can strain resources and compromise programme standards if scaled universally without adequate funding.

Nevertheless, the advantages are profound and multifaceted. Professionally, immersive experiences cultivate adaptability, cross-cultural communication, and problem-solving skills that classroom learning rarely replicates. Employers consistently value graduates with real-world exposure, as evidenced by higher employment rates and starting salaries among mobile students. Educationally, studying or working abroad fosters intellectual independence and exposes learners to diverse pedagogical or industry practices, enriching their disciplinary understanding. On a societal level, widespread mobility promotes intercultural empathy and global citizenship - qualities essential in an interconnected world facing transnational challenges like climate change and public health crises. Crucially, these benefits align with the core mission of higher education: to develop well-rounded individuals capable of contributing beyond national borders.

In conclusion, while mandatory placements pose implementation hurdles, their transformative impact on student development and societal progress justifies their inclusion. The key lies not in abandoning the idea due to its challenges, but in designing inclusive frameworks - through scholarships, flexible scheduling, and virtual alternatives - that ensure equity without sacrificing quality. Thus, the advantages decisively outweigh the disadvantages when approached thoughtfully.

## 第611篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

As countries try to reduce their carbon emissions, some argue that nuclear power must be part of the solution, while others believe that only renewable sources such as wind and solar should be developed. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

### 文章

Reducing emissions quickly enough to meet climate targets requires decisions about which low-carbon technologies to build. Some argue that nuclear generation is indispensable; others maintain that wind and solar can do the whole job. I believe nuclear power has to be included, mainly because of what happens when the weather does not cooperate.

The case against nuclear energy is not irrational. Construction costs have consistently exceeded forecasts, and plants take well over a decade to complete, which is a serious objection when the emissions problem is urgent. The waste question also remains genuinely unresolved in most countries, and although the risk of a major accident is very low, the consequences when one occurs are unusually long-lasting and fall on people who did not choose them.

The difficulty for a renewables-only strategy is reliability. Wind and solar output varies by hour and by season, and a grid must match supply to demand continuously. Storage at the scale required to cover several still, dark winter days does not yet exist at acceptable cost. Without a controllable low-carbon source, the gap tends to be filled by gas, which means a renewables-only policy can in practice mean a renewables-plus-fossil-fuel policy. The same objection applies to interconnection between countries, which only helps if a neighbour happens to have surplus power at the exact hour of the shortfall; large weather systems frequently sit over several neighbouring countries at once.

My own view is that this last point is decisive. The realistic comparison is not nuclear against renewables but nuclear against the gas plants that would otherwise cover the shortfall. Judged that way, extending the life of existing reactors and building a limited number of new ones is the lower risk, even accounting for cost overruns and the unsolved problem of long-term storage.

## 第612篇

### 题目

Some people believe that governments should take responsibility for improving the health of citizens by regulating diet and lifestyle choices, while others think that health is a personal matter and individuals should be free to make their own decisions. To what extent do you agree with the view that governments should intervene in citizens' health choices?

### 文章

The appropriate scope of government intervention in individual health choices is a genuinely contested question, made more urgent as rising rates of diet-related illness place growing pressure on public healthcare systems. My view is that governments are justified in regulating industries and environments that shape health outcomes, but that policies restricting personal behaviour cross an important boundary of individual autonomy.
The strongest argument for intervention concerns market failure rather than personal conduct. Left unregulated, food manufacturers have commercial incentives to engineer products that are highly palatable but nutritionally poor, market them aggressively, and price them below healthier alternatives. Governments can legitimately correct this imbalance through nutritional labelling requirements, taxes on high-sugar products, and restrictions on advertising to children — measures that improve the conditions under which individuals choose without dictating the choice itself.
Policies that directly restrict what individuals may eat or how they must live, however, represent a more problematic overreach. Such measures tend to generate resentment and poor compliance, and they concentrate government authority in a domain traditionally reserved for private judgment. Crucially, the harm that an individual's dietary choices causes falls primarily on that individual rather than on others — a distinction that weakens the public-health justification for compulsory restrictions.
In conclusion, governments should intervene assertively in the commercial and structural conditions that shape health, but should stop well short of controlling individual lifestyle choices. The difference between improving the environment of choice and overriding the choice itself is the key boundary that health policy should not cross.

Although more and more people use public transport. some city streets are still overcrowded with traffic. how can this problem be solved? what is your opinion and relevent example.

### 文章

Although an increasing number of people use public transport, many city streets are still overcrowded with traffic. In my opinion, this problem can be reduced by improving public transportation and introducing policies that discourage people from using private cars.

One major solution is to make public transport more convenient, reliable and affordable. Many people continue to drive because buses and trains may be overcrowded, delayed or unavailable in some areas. Therefore, governments should increase the frequency of buses and trains, expand routes and provide comfortable facilities. In addition, dedicated bus lanes could help public transportation avoid traffic jams and reach destinations more quickly. For example, if buses in a large city run frequently and have separate lanes, commuters may prefer them to driving because they can save both time and money.

Another effective measure is to discourage unnecessary car use. Governments could introduce higher parking fees in busy downtown areas and charge vehicles that enter highly congested zones. At the same time, cities should develop safe cycling lanes and pedestrian-friendly streets so that people have alternatives for short journeys. For instance, London has introduced congestion charging in central areas, which is designed to reduce the number of vehicles entering the busiest parts of the city.

In my opinion, using a combination of these measures would be more effective than relying on only one solution. If public transport is improved while private-car use becomes less convenient in crowded areas, more people are likely to choose buses, trains, cycling or walking. This would reduce traffic congestion and could also improve air quality.

## 第614篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

At many universities, live lectures are being replaced by recorded material which students watch in their own time. Do you think this is a positive or a negative development?

### 文章

Recorded lectures have moved from being an emergency measure to being a permanent arrangement at many universities. I think the development is a positive one, but only because it exposes how little of a lecture ever needed to happen in a particular room at nine in the morning.

The advantages for students are substantial and mostly practical. A recording can be paused, replayed and watched at a speed that suits the listener, which matters enormously to anyone working in a second language or meeting an unfamiliar technical vocabulary for the first time. Students who commute, who work part time or who have caring responsibilities recover hours each week that were previously spent travelling in order to hear something they could have heard anywhere. Universities can also reach students who would not have been able to attend at all.

The losses are real but they are losses of a different kind. What disappears is not the content, which transmits perfectly well through a screen, but the incidental contact: the question asked afterwards, the conversation on the way out, the sense of belonging to a cohort rather than an audience. Attendance also becomes invisible, and students who were struggling used to be identifiable by their empty seats. These are serious, though they are arguments about what should replace the lecture rather than arguments for keeping it.

That is the condition on my answer. Recording lectures is a gain if the hours it frees are spent on seminars, supervision and the kind of contact that cannot be recorded. If it is simply a way of teaching more students with fewer staff, the same change becomes a straightforward reduction in what a degree contains.

## 第615篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Some people believe that the introduction of artificial intelligence and automation will lead to widespread unemployment and social problems, while others argue that technology has always created more jobs than it has destroyed. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

### 文章

The rapid advance of artificial intelligence and automation has prompted heated debate about its consequences for employment. Pessimists predict widespread job losses and social dislocation, while optimists draw on historical precedent to argue that technological progress consistently generates more opportunities than it eliminates. My view is that the transition will be disruptive for specific sectors, but ultimately productive, provided that governments invest in workforce retraining.
Those who foresee widespread unemployment highlight the unprecedented scope of modern automation. Unlike previous technologies, AI systems can perform cognitive as well as physical tasks, threatening white-collar professions — legal research, accounting, and medical diagnostics — that were once considered immune to mechanisation. This breadth of potential disruption, they argue, means displacement could occur faster than new roles emerge, leaving large segments of the workforce in prolonged difficulty.
However, historical experience offers a more optimistic perspective. The mechanisation of agriculture displaced millions of rural workers in the nineteenth century, yet the subsequent growth of manufacturing absorbed them and raised living standards considerably. Similarly, personal computers eliminated typing pools and bookkeeping roles while creating software development, IT support, and digital marketing as entirely new fields. Each technological wave has ultimately expanded employment, even when the transition proved difficult for affected workers.
Balancing these arguments, I believe the key variable is not the technology itself but the policy response. Economies that invest proactively in adult education, digital literacy, and income support during transitions can capture the productivity gains of automation while limiting harm to displaced workers. Without such investment, those gains will accrue narrowly to capital owners, deepening rather than resolving inequality.

## 第617篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Employers are now able to record everything their staff do on company computers. Some people believe that employers should be free to do this. Do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

Almost everything done on a work computer can now be logged, and a great many employers log it. I disagree that they should be free to do so without limit, though I accept that some monitoring is legitimate and that the argument turns on scope rather than on principle.

The employer's case is easy to state. The equipment and the network belong to the company, the time is paid for, and the risks of unmonitored access are real: data leaving the building, regulated communications going unrecorded, misconduct that nobody can afterwards prove. An employer that suffers a breach and cannot establish what happened is in a poor position, and most staff accept that some record is kept, in the same way that they accept a camera at the entrance. None of this is controversial.

What is controversial is unlimited scope. There is a difference between logging which files leave a network and reading an employee's private messages, or between recording that a machine sat idle and capturing keystrokes and webcam images. The second kind produces information the employer has no legitimate use for, and it changes the relationship: people who know they are watched in detail do not become more productive, they become more careful to appear productive, which is not the same thing.

The reasonable settlement is monitoring that is proportionate, disclosed in advance and limited to what the employer actually needs. Staff should know what is recorded before they accept the job. An employer that cannot explain why a particular form of surveillance is necessary should not be conducting it. Owning the equipment establishes a right to protect it, not a right to know everything about the person using it.

## 第619篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

English has become the main language of international business, science and travel. Some people see this as a practical advantage, while others believe it threatens smaller languages and the cultures attached to them. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

### 文章

The spread of English as a common working language has been one of the most visible effects of globalisation. Supporters point to the practical convenience it creates, while others fear that smaller languages are being displaced along with the cultures they carry. I accept the value of a shared language but believe the concern about displacement is well founded.

The advantages are substantial and easy to demonstrate. A single working language allows a Brazilian engineer and a Korean supplier to negotiate without either learning the other's language, and it gives researchers access to the great majority of published work in their field. Students, too, gain entry to institutions that would otherwise be closed to them. The alternative is not a world of equal multilingualism but a world of slower and more expensive translation.

The risk to smaller languages is nevertheless real, and it operates through incentives rather than prohibition. Nobody bans a minority language; parents simply calculate that their children's prospects depend on the dominant one and stop passing theirs on. Within two generations a language can move from ordinary domestic use to something spoken only at funerals. What is lost with it is not only vocabulary but forms of classification — for plants, for weather, for kinship — that took centuries to develop. A language that has stopped being spoken at home cannot be revived by teaching it as a school subject.

My position is that both effects are genuine and that they are not symmetrical. The convenience of English is enormous but reversible, since a world that stopped using it would simply adopt something else. The disappearance of a language is permanent. That asymmetry is why I would support serious public investment in minority-language education, even while continuing to teach English to everyone.

## 第621篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Fraud committed over the internet has increased significantly in recent years. Why has this type of crime become so common? What can individuals do to protect themselves?

### 文章

Fraud committed over the internet has grown faster than almost any other category of crime. The reasons are structural rather than accidental, and while individuals cannot fix the structure, there is a good deal they can do to make themselves harder to reach.

The first reason is that the amount of exploitable information has multiplied. Shopping, banking, tax returns and social life have all moved online, so a single compromised account can expose an address, a date of birth and a list of contacts at once. Criminals no longer need to work out who a target is; the information has been published, often by the target.

The second is that the crime is unusually low-risk. An offender can operate from a jurisdiction that will not extradite, against victims whose police have no authority there, using intermediaries to move the proceeds. Investigations crossing several borders are slow, and most individual losses are too small to justify them, so the expected cost of committing this crime is close to zero. Automation compounds the problem, since a message costs nothing to send to a million people and needs to succeed only occasionally.

Individual defence therefore has to concentrate on being an unprofitable target. The single most valuable measure is two-factor authentication, which makes a stolen password useless on its own. A password manager removes the temptation to reuse credentials across sites. Beyond the technical measures, the habit that matters most is refusing to act on urgency: almost every successful scam depends on persuading somebody to move money or reveal a code immediately, so a rule of never responding to unexpected contact directly, and instead calling the organisation back on a number found independently, defeats most attempts.

None of this eliminates the risk, but fraud at this scale is a numbers business, and anyone slightly harder to defraud than average is likely to be passed over.

## 第623篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Governments have limited budgets for health care. Some people believe that public money should always be spent on preventing illness rather than on treating it. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

Every health system spends more than it has, so the choice between preventing illness and treating it is a real one rather than a theoretical exercise. I agree that prevention deserves a far larger share than it usually receives, but the word 'always' in this claim is what I would reject.

The economic argument for prevention is strong and well established. Vaccination, screening programmes and measures that reduce smoking cost a fraction of what it costs to treat the conditions they avert, and they go on delivering that saving for decades. Prevention also reaches people who would otherwise not appear at a hospital until their illness was advanced, which is the point at which treatment is least effective and most expensive. A system that funds only treatment is in effect waiting for problems it could have avoided and then paying the higher price for them.

The difficulty is that prevention and treatment are not interchangeable claims on the same budget. A person who is already ill cannot be helped by a campaign, and a government that redirected all its funding towards prevention would be abandoning identifiable people in order to benefit statistical ones. Prevention is also uncertain at the level of the individual: a screening programme saves lives without anyone being able to say whose. The visible patient tends to win that argument, and it is not obvious that they should lose it.

My view is that the balance should shift substantially towards prevention but can never become absolute. A sensible rule would protect treatment for those already ill and direct new money towards prevention, which is where each additional pound buys the most health. Existing services would be protected and the shift would happen at the margin.

## 第625篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

In many communities, local charities and clubs are finding it increasingly difficult to recruit volunteers. Why is this happening? What could be done to encourage more people to give their time?

### 文章

Many local organisations, from sports clubs to food banks, say that volunteers are becoming harder to find. In my view the main reasons lie in how people now work and live, and the most effective response is for organisations to change what they ask of volunteers.

The first reason is time, but not simply in the sense that people are busier. Growing numbers of workers have irregular hours, shift patterns that change from week to week, or more than one job, and this makes it difficult to promise to be somewhere every Tuesday evening. A second factor is mobility. People who expect to move for work within few years have less reason to become attached to a particular neighbourhood, and the informal networks through which volunteers were traditionally recruited — a word from a neighbour, a notice outside a place of worship — reach fewer of them. Finally, volunteering itself has become more demanding, with training courses, background checks and forms that can discourage someone who only wanted to help.

Several measures could reverse this trend. Organisations could offer shorter and more flexible roles, such as helping at a single event, instead of relying on long-term commitments that many people can no longer make. Employers could give staff a small number of paid volunteering days each year, which would ease the time pressure directly. Governments could also simplify the checks required for low-risk roles, while keeping them in place where people work with children or vulnerable adults.

In short, people have not become less generous; their lives have become less predictable. If voluntary organisations adapt to that, rather than waiting for the committed weekly volunteer to return, they are likely to find more help than they expect.

## 第627篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

In many companies, software and artificial intelligence now carry out routine administrative work that was previously done by employees. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?

### 文章

Routine clerical work — invoicing, scheduling, first-line customer queries — is increasingly handled by software rather than staff. On balance I believe the advantages outweigh the disadvantages, provided that the workers affected are given genuine support.

The principal benefit is that organisations stop paying skilled people to do unskilled things. An administrator who spends three days a week copying figures between systems is not producing anything that could not be produced automatically, and the hours released can be redirected towards work that does require judgement, such as handling the complaints that software cannot resolve. Accuracy improves as well, since a system that has been correctly configured will not become careless at the end of a long afternoon. Most of the value, in other words, comes from removing work that nobody chose to do.

The obvious cost is employment. Administrative roles have historically offered stable, reasonably paid work to people without university qualifications, and there is no guarantee that the jobs created by automation will be accessible for the same group. Retraining is often proposed as the answer, but it is expensive and it assumes a willingness to start again in middle age that not everyone has. There is also a quieter risk: when a process is fully automated, the institutional understanding of how it works can disappear with the staff who used to run it.

Weighed against each other, I still consider the gains greater. The efficiency benefits are permanent and they compound, whereas the disruption, though severe, is concentrated in a transition that governments and employers can plan for. What matters is that the burden is not left entirely with the individuals who happen to be holding the affected jobs.

## 第629篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

In many countries, a high proportion of young people who are released from prison commit further offences within a short period. What are the reasons for this, and how could the situation be improved?

### 文章

A striking proportion of young people released from custody are back before the courts within a year, which suggests that whatever the sentence was intended to achieve, it is not being achieved. The reasons have less to do with the severity of the punishment than with what happens immediately after it ends.

The first reason is that release removes structure without replacing it. A young person leaves custody frequently with no accommodation arranged, no employment, and a criminal record that makes obtaining either substantially harder. The people most readily available to them are the ones they knew before, which is to say the ones associated with the offending in the first place. Reoffending in these circumstances is less a decision than a default.

A second reason is that custody itself interrupts the things that ordinarily hold a young life together. Education stops, apprenticeships are lost, family relationships are strained by distance and expense. Someone who enters custody at seventeen with a partial qualification frequently leaves at nineteen with none, and two years further behind peers who were already ahead.

The measures most likely to help therefore concern the transition. Arranging housing and a training placement before release, rather than after, removes the vacuum in which reoffending occurs, and supervision by a consistent individual rather than a rotating series of officials gives a young person someone to contact before a situation becomes a crime. Restricting how long a minor offence stays disclosable would also help, since a record that permanently blocks employment guarantees the outcome it was meant to prevent.

### 题目

In many countries, companies are employing fewer permanent staff and are using more short-term contractors and gig workers. Do you think this is a positive or a negative development?

### 文章

Permanent employment is being replaced in many industries by short contracts, agency work and app-based freelancing. I regard this as a negative development overall, although my reasons have less to do with flexibility than with who now carries the cost of a bad month.

The advantages are genuine for a minority. A skilled contractor with sought-after expertise can charge more than a salaried equivalent, refuse work and take time off without asking permission. For students and for people with caring responsibilities, work that can be fitted around other commitments is often the only work available at all. Companies benefit too, since they can expand and contract quickly without the cost of redundancies, and in genuinely seasonal industries that is a reasonable arrangement rather than an abusive one.

The problem is that these conditions describe a small part of the workforce. Most gig work is low paid and easily replaced, which removes the bargaining power that made flexibility valuable in the first place. Sick pay, pensions, notice periods and holiday entitlement were never perks; they were the mechanism by which the risk of illness or a slow month sat with the employer, who could absorb it, rather than with the worker, who cannot. A salaried employee who catches flu loses nothing; a courier who catches flu loses a week of income. Reclassifying the same jobs shifts that risk downwards without changing the work at all.

This is why I consider the trend negative. Flexibility that one side can use and the other cannot is not flexibility but insecurity with a better name, and the shift has happened largely at the bottom of the labour market rather than at the top. The label has changed and the work has not.

### 题目

Caring for children is an important thing of the society. It is suggested that all mothers and fathers should be required to take childcare training courses. Do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

Since childcare is an essential aspect of society, it is suggested that all parents should be required to enrol in courses that teach them how to care for children. I strongly disagree with this view because individuals can acquire parenting skills from their own caregivers and through personal experience, as well as from various available resources.

First and foremost, people can learn useful parenting skills from their own parents. Since they were raised by them, they may have gained practical knowledge that is more applicable than the general and theoretical information provided in formal courses. Moreover, individuals with younger siblings may have already developed useful skills by caring for them, allowing them to apply this experience when raising their own children. For instance, in Saudi Arabia, older daughters in larger families often help their mothers by taking care of their younger siblings.

Furthermore, there are plenty of resources available nowadays that provide information about raising children. Parents can gain knowledge through online blogs, studies, videos, books, and many other free and accessible sources. They can also return to these resources whenever they need specific information. In contrast, formal courses may be less practical, as people can forget much of what they learn once the course ends, while some of the material may not be applicable to real-life situations. For example, many mothers and doctors use TikTok to share advice on childcare, allowing parents to access useful information whenever they need it.

In conclusion, I strongly believe that parents can develop the necessary skills through their caregivers, personal experience, and widely available resources. Therefore, formal courses should not be compulsory.

## 第633篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

In many countries, fewer school leavers are choosing to study science and mathematics at a higher level. Why is this happening? What could be done to encourage more young people into these subjects?

### 文章

In many education systems the proportion of students continuing with physics, chemistry and mathematics after the compulsory stage has been falling for years. I believe the causes are partly practical and partly cultural, and that any effective response has to address both.

The most obvious reason is risk. Where university admission depends on a single set of grades, students make a rational calculation: a mathematics paper that is marked strictly is a worse bet than a humanities subject in which a solid grade is easier to secure. A learner who is capable of physics but not certain of an excellent mark will often avoid it, and schools that are judged on results rarely discourage them.

A second cause is that these subjects are frequently taught as a body of content to be memorised rather than as a way of investigating things. Students who never design an experiment or model a real problem have no way of discovering that the work might suit them. There is also a persistent image problem, since the scientific careers are still widely imagined as solitary and poorly paid compared with finance or law.

Solutions therefore need to work on both fronts. Admissions systems could weight difficult subjects more generously, so that choosing physics no longer costs a candidate a place. Curricula could be rebalanced towards genuine investigation, with laboratory work and data projects given the time they need rather than squeezed in around examination preparation. Finally, sustained contact with working scientists and engineers — through school partnerships and paid summer placements — would correct the assumption that these careers are narrow or unrewarding.

In short, young people are responding sensibly to the incentives and impressions they are given, and it is those, rather than the students themselves, that need to change.

## 第635篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

In many countries people are having their first child at a much later age than previous generations did. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of this development.

### 文章

The average age at which people have a first child has risen sharply in a single generation. The change brings real benefits to the individuals making the choice, while most of its costs are either medical or demographic, and the second kind is easy to ignore because it arrives late.

For the parents, the advantages are concrete. A couple in their mid-thirties are likely to have settled housing, established incomes and some understanding of what they are undertaking, none of which is typical at twenty-two. For women in particular, delay protects a career at exactly the point where seniority is decided; a parent who returns from leave with an established position loses far less than one who never had it. There is reasonable evidence, too, that children of older parents do well educationally, which is presumably a function of household resources rather than of age itself.

The disadvantages fall into two categories. The first is straightforwardly biological: fertility declines with age, treatment is expensive and often unsuccessful, and both maternal and neonatal risks rise. Some couples who delay do not end up with the family they planned. The second is collective. If a whole society postpones, birth rates fall below replacement, and a shrinking working-age population is left supporting a growing retired one. Individually rational timing produces a collectively awkward result.

On balance the development seems to me positive for the people making the decision and difficult for the societies they live in. That is not a reason to advise anyone to have children earlier, but it is a reason to make having them earlier less costly than it currently is. Governments that treat the trend purely as a private choice are therefore missing half of it.

## 第637篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

In many countries, public confidence in politicians has fallen sharply in recent decades. What has caused this loss of trust? How might it be rebuilt?

### 文章

Confidence in elected representatives has weakened across much of the democratic world, and the explanation is neither simple dishonesty nor a sudden change in the character of politicians. In my view the decline has two main sources, and any attempt to reverse it has to deal with both.

The first is the gap between what campaigns promise and what governments can deliver. Politicians competing for office have every incentive to describe their intentions in confident, specific terms, yet much of what determines outcomes — global prices, court rulings, the decisions of previous administrations — lies outside their control. Voters who were promised certainty and given excuses conclude, reasonably enough, that they were misled rather than merely disappointed.

The second is visibility. Information that once circulated only among journalists is now available instantly and in full, so that every expenses claim and every awkward recording reaches the public directly. This does not mean politicians behave worse than their predecessors; it means the evidence is no longer filtered. The effect is nonetheless corrosive, because scandals accumulate in the memory while the routine competence of government goes unrecorded.

Rebuilding trust therefore depends on narrowing the gap and managing the visibility. Parties could be required to publish costed programmes that an independent office assesses before polling day, which would make the extravagant claims expensive to make. Transparency rules on lobbying and party funding would remove the suspicion that decisions are bought. Most importantly, governments should report honestly on the commitments they have failed to meet, since an admitted failure damages credibility far less than a quietly abandoned one.

None of this restores confidence quickly. But trust is rebuilt in the same way it is lost, through a long accumulation of small verifiable acts.

## 第638篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Creative artists should always be given freedom to express their own ideas (in words, pictures, music or film) in whichever way they wish. There should be no government restrictions on what they do. To what extent do you agree or disagree on this IELTS topic?

### 文章

Creative freedom is essential for artists to produce original work and contribute to cultural development. While I believe artists should generally be allowed to express their ideas without unnecessary interference, I disagree that this freedom should be absolute, as certain forms of expression may cause serious harm to individuals or society.

One major reason artists should be given considerable freedom is that it encourages creativity and original thinking. When writers, musicians and filmmakers are free to explore unconventional or controversial ideas, they can experiment with new perspectives rather than limiting themselves to socially accepted views. This freedom to experiment can lead to more innovative artistic work and encourage audiences to consider important social issues from different perspectives. For example, films addressing inequality or discrimination may stimulate public discussion about problems that are otherwise ignored. Therefore, artistic freedom not only benefits individual artists but can also contribute to broader cultural and social development.

However, complete artistic freedom may be problematic when creative content poses a genuine risk of harm to others. For instance, certain material may deliberately encourage violence or hatred against particular groups. Exposure to such content could influence vulnerable individuals or increase hostility within society, potentially threatening public safety. This risk of harm justifies limited government intervention, provided that restrictions are clearly defined and are not used simply to suppress criticism or unpopular opinions. Therefore, regulation should focus on preventing serious harm rather than controlling artistic creativity.

In conclusion, artists should enjoy substantial freedom to express unconventional ideas because this promotes creativity and social discussion. However, reasonable restrictions are justified when artistic expression directly threatens the safety or rights of others.

## 第639篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

In many countries, services that were once run by the state, such as prisons, railways and rubbish collection, are now operated by private companies under government contracts. Do you think this is a positive or a negative development?

### 文章

Over recent decades, many governments have handed the day-to-day running of prisons, railways and waste collection to private firms while continuing to pay for them. Although this has improved some services, I regard the overall trend as negative, because the conditions that make private provision work are often absent.

The case for outsourcing rests on competition. A government department that performs poorly rarely faces any real consequence, whereas a contractor that misses its targets can, in principle, lose the contract to a rival. This pressure has produced genuine improvements in services where performance is easy to observe. Refuse collection is the clearest example, either the bins are emptied on the agreed day or they are not, and a council can compare the prices and records of several bidders before choosing one.

The weakness of this model is that competition only disciplines a firm when the contract can realistically be taken away. Railways and prisons are not like bin rounds. Few companies have the capital to run a rail network, so there are rarely more than a handful of bidders, and a government that dismisses a failing operator must be ready to run the trains itself the next morning. Contractors are well aware of this, which considerably weakens the state's bargaining position. In prisons the problem is compounded by the fact that the outcomes which matter most, such as whether inmates are rehabilitated, are slow to appear and hard to attribute, so a company can meet its targets on paper while cutting staff in ways that make the prison more dangerous.

For these reasons, I believe the development is negative overall. Outsourcing should be limited to services where the market is genuinely competitive and quality can be measured easily, while complex and essential services should return to direct public control.

On the other hand, the benefits of the internet far outweigh these drawbacks by fundamentally improving human life. Firstly, the internet has democratized access to education and information. Secondly, digital connectivity has revolutionized economic activity and global commerce. E-commerce platforms, remote work opportunities, and international business collaboration have created countless jobs and boosted economic growth globally. Finally, real-time communication tools have allowed people to maintain personal and professional relationships effortlessly across long distances.

In conclusion, although the widespread adoption of the internet presents non-negligible challenges regarding privacy and mental health, its transformative benefits in education, global trade, and communication are far more significant.
