## 第703篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Some people believe that newspapers and websites should be free to publish stories about the private lives of famous people. Others think that famous people have the same right to privacy as anyone else. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

### 文章

The private lives of famous people have always sold newspapers, and online publishing has only increased the appetite for such stories. While I accept that some public figures forfeit part of their privacy, I believe that for most famous people, most of the time, the right to a private life should be protected.

Those who defend intrusive reporting usually make two arguments. The first is that fame is a bargain: actors, athletes and musicians benefit enormously from public attention, and many actively invite it by sharing details of their relationships and homes. It seems inconsistent for them to welcome coverage when it promotes a film and object to it when it reveals a divorce. The second, and stronger, argument concerns people with power. When a politician who campaigns on family values is found to be deceiving his own family, or a minister has undisclosed business interests, the press is exposing hypocrisy or corruption that voters are entitled to know about.

Those who favour stronger protection point out that most celebrity stories involve no such public interest. Photographs of an actor's children on the way to school or reports of a singer's medical treatment tell readers nothing that matters to them; they simply satisfy curiosity. The cost to the person concerned can be severe, since constant pursuit by photographers makes an ordinary life almost impossible, and the harm falls also on relatives who never sought fame at all.

In my view, the second position is more convincing, although the first contains an important exception. Politicians and others who exercise power over the public should expect scrutiny of any private conduct that relates to that power. Entertainers, however, have sold their performances rather than their lives, and publishing their private information purely because readers are curious should not be permitted.

Consequently, prioritising personal style over transient trends appears to be a more respectful and self-affirming approach.

## 第705篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Some people believe that private cars should be banned from the centres of large cities. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

Congestion and poor air quality have pushed a number of city governments towards restricting or removing private vehicles from their central districts. I agree with the policy, provided it is understood as the final stage of a transport strategy rather than the opening move.

The health argument is the most compelling. Exhaust fumes and tyre particulates are concentrated exactly where population density is highest, and the people most exposed — children at street level, delivery riders, residents of arterial roads — are rarely the ones doing the driving. Removing cars from a central zone produces measurable improvements in local air quality within a short period, and the reduction in noise is immediate.

The second argument concerns space. A car occupies a great deal of road and kerb for the small number of people it carries, and central land is the most valuable a city possesses. Reallocating it to pedestrians, cycling and outdoor trading generally raises footfall and retail turnover, and cities that have pedestrianised historic centres have usually found that the predicted collapse in trade did not arrive.

The strongest objection comes from people for whom driving is not a preference. Disabled residents, tradespeople carrying equipment and shift workers travelling at night cannot simply switch to the bus. A blanket ban would penalise them for the behaviour of commuters who do have alternatives, which is why exemptions and permit schemes are essential rather than optional.

My conclusion is that private cars should indeed be excluded from city centres, but only where frequent and affordable public transport is already in place and where genuine need is exempted. Imposed in the wrong order, the policy becomes a charge on people without choices.

## 第707篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Some people believe that voting in national elections should be compulsory for all adult citizens. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

A number of democracies fine citizens who fail to vote, and the practice is periodically proposed elsewhere as a remedy for falling turnout. I disagree with compulsion, not because turnout is unimportant but because the policy treats a symptom while leaving the condition that produced it untouched.

The argument in favour is genuinely strong and deserves acknowledgement. Where voting is voluntary, participation skews sharply towards older, wealthier and better-educated citizens, and policy tends to follow the people who turn out. Compulsory voting removes that distortion at a stroke, and a government elected by everybody has fewer excuses for ignoring anybody.

The objection I find decisive concerns what a vote is for. A ballot is a statement of preference, and a preference extracted under threat of a fine carries less information than one freely given. A significant proportion of compelled votes are likely to be cast carelessly or at random, which adds noise to the result rather than legitimacy. Abstention can itself be a message — that none of the candidates deserves support — and a system that penalises it loses the ability to hear that message at all.

There is also a diagnostic problem. Low turnout is rarely caused by laziness; it is caused by the belief that the available choices are indistinguishable or that the local outcome is already settled. Compulsion suppresses the evidence of that belief without touching the belief itself. A government could instead make registration automatic, hold elections at weekends, or reform electoral systems in which most seats never change hands.

For these reasons I do not support compulsory voting. Turnout is a symptom, and a democracy that raises it by legal penalty has improved its statistics rather than its politics. The alternative reforms are slower and far less satisfying, but they raise participation by giving people a reason to participate.

Finally, governments and schools should work together to create a healthier environment. ## 第709篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Some people think that all advertising aimed at children under the age of twelve should be banned. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

Children now meet commercial messages in more places than any previous generation, and there are recurring calls to prohibit advertising directed at the under-twelves altogether. I agree with a ban, principally because young children cannot recognise persuasion for what it is, although enforcing one is far harder than the proposal usually admits.

The central argument is about capacity. Advertising is a form of persuasion, and persuasion assumes an audience able to see that someone is trying to change its mind. Children below roughly eight lack that recognition entirely, and even at eleven the understanding is fragile under the pressure of an appealing image. Selling to an audience that cannot tell it is being sold to is not competition but exploitation of a known limitation, and the same reasoning already justifies preventing children from buying alcohol or entering a contract.

A second argument concerns content. The products marketed most heavily to children skew towards confectionery, sugary cereals and fast food, and the cumulative effect on what children come to expect from a meal is well recognised. Restrictions on this category alone have been introduced in several countries.

The difficulty is definitional. A ban on advertising aimed at children is straightforward for a toy commercial in a cartoon break, but far less so for product placement inside a game, a family film sponsored by a brand, or an online personality whose audience happens to be nine. Legislation covering only broadcast advertising simply moves the money online, where oversight is weakest and enforcement slowest.

On balance I support the ban, while recognising that it has to be written in terms of the audience actually reached rather than the audience formally intended. The test of a good rule here is whether a company could comply with its letter while defeating its purpose.

## 第711篇

### 题目

Some people think that children should not be allowed to own a smartphone until they start secondary school. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

Smartphones now reach children long before adolescence, and there is a growing view that ownership should be postponed until secondary school. I agree with this restriction, principally because primary-age children lack the self-regulation the device demands, though I would treat it as a matter of parental judgement rather than a fixed rule.

The strongest argument concerns attention. A smartphone is engineered to be difficult to put down, and an eight-year-old is being asked to resist a product designed by teams whose entire job is to make resistance fail. The consequences appear in sleep, in reading stamina and in the capacity to tolerate boredom, which is where a good deal of childhood invention comes from. Delaying ownership by three or four years does not remove the difficulty, but it postpones it until the child has more capacity to meet it.

A second argument concerns exposure. Younger children encounter material they cannot place in any context, and the social dynamics of group messaging are unforgiving at an age when friendships are already volatile. Parental controls help but are routinely circumvented.

The obvious objection is safety, and it is a genuine one: parents want to be able to reach a child walking home from school. That need, however, is met equally well by a basic handset, which provides contact without a browser or an app store. The distinction matters, because it shows the safety argument supports carrying a phone rather than owning a smartphone in particular. Parents who insist on the latter are usually solving a problem they have not named.

On balance, then, I support delaying smartphone ownership until secondary school, while accepting that the right moment depends on the individual child rather than on the school calendar.

## 第713篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Some schools teach children of all abilities together in the same class, while others divide students into groups according to how well they perform. Discuss both approaches and give your own opinion.

### 文章

Schools have to decide whether to teach children of different attainment levels together or to separate them into ability groups. Advocates of mixed classes stress fairness and mutual learning; supporters of setting argue that teaching is more effective when a class is at a similar stage. I think setting works for a minority of subjects and does more harm than good elsewhere.

The argument for teaching everyone together is partly moral and partly practical. A child placed in a bottom set at eleven tends to interpret the placement as a permanent statement about their intelligence, and lowered expectations reliably produce lowered results. There is also the difficulty that early attainment often reflects home circumstances rather than capacity, so sorting children young risks converting an accident of background into a fixed educational path.

The case for setting is harder to dismiss than its critics allow. A teacher facing a class with a four-year spread of attainment must either pitch the lesson somewhere in the middle, losing both ends, or prepare three lessons simultaneously. In subjects that build strictly on prior knowledge — mathematics above all — a student who has not mastered the previous stage genuinely cannot access the next one, and pretending otherwise helps nobody. Placing that student in a group working at their actual level is the only arrangement in which they ever catch up.

My own conclusion follows from that distinction. Where a subject is cumulative, grouping by current attainment is a practical necessity rather than a judgement about worth. Where it is not — in history, literature or the arts — a mixed class costs the stronger students little and gives the weaker ones access to better conversation. What matters most is that any grouping remains genuinely temporary and is reviewed often.

### 文章

Although healthcare professionals frequently recommend regular physical activity for older adults, many elderly individuals struggle to maintain a consistent exercise routine. This essay will discuss the main reasons for this reluctance and suggest several ways to encourage them to become more physically active.

One significant reason why older adults may be reluctant to exercise is that physical activity can be particularly demanding for those who have been inactive for many years. Individuals who lead a sedentary lifestyle may become tired relatively quickly when they begin exercising, which can undermine their motivation to continue. Furthermore, some elderly people may be accustomed to a less active daily routine and therefore find it difficult to establish a new habit. They may also be concerned about discomfort or injury, making them even less willing to participate in physical activities.

There are several effective ways to address this issue. Firstly, healthcare professionals could recommend low-impact activities that are appropriate for older adults, such as walking, swimming and gentle stretching. Rather than expecting patients to undertake strenuous workouts immediately, doctors could encourage them to set realistic and achievable goals and gradually increase the intensity of their activities. Governments could also promote active ageing by providing accessible community-based exercise programmes. Such programmes could make physical activity more enjoyable by allowing elderly people to exercise in a supportive social environment with others of a similar age.

In conclusion, older people may fail to exercise regularly because they find physical activity demanding, lack motivation, and are accustomed to a relatively inactive lifestyle. However, this problem can be addressed by recommending suitable forms of exercise, setting achievable goals and providing accessible community programmes. These measures could help older adults develop sustainable exercise habits and improve their overall quality of life.

## 第715篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Streaming platforms have largely replaced scheduled television and, for many people, trips to the cinema. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of this change.

### 文章

Watching at a time of one's own choosing has replaced watching at a time chosen by a broadcaster, and cinema attendance has fallen accordingly. The change has clear benefits for viewers, but its effects on what actually gets made are less comfortable.

The advantages for the audience are substantial and easy to state. Control over timing is the obvious one, and it matters most to the people whose hours are least predictable — shift workers, parents of small children, anyone for whom a fixed nine o'clock broadcast was simply unavailable. Beyond convenience, the range of material has widened enormously: series in other languages now reach audiences that a national broadcaster would never have commissioned them for, and older work that would once have vanished remains permanently available. Price is a further advantage for households that watch a great deal, though the proliferation of competing services has eroded it.

The disadvantages are less visible because they operate on production rather than on viewing. Platforms commission according to what their data suggests will retain subscribers, which favours material that resembles material that has already worked. The economics of cinema are affected too: a film that needs a large screen and a long run to find its audience is harder to finance when the default destination is a living room. Something is also lost socially — a broadcast watched by millions at once created a shared reference that a personalised library does not.

Overall the gains to viewers are real, and I would not want the schedule back. But it is worth being clear that convenience has been paid for in a currency the viewer never sees: a narrower range of things commissioned, and fewer occasions on which a whole country watches the same thing.

## 第717篇

### 题目

Traditional crafts such as weaving, pottery and woodcarving are dying out in many parts of the world. Why is this happening? Do you think it is important to keep these skills alive?

### 文章

Crafts such as hand-weaving, pottery and woodcarving were once part of ordinary economic life, but in many regions they are now practised by a dwindling number of elderly specialists. The causes are largely economic, and although not every traditional skill can or should survive, I believe there is a strong case for preserving most of them.

The most obvious cause is price. Industrial production has made cloth, tableware and furniture so cheap that a handmade equivalent, which may take days to produce, cannot compete except as a luxury. The market that remains is small and unpredictable, so few people can earn a reliable living from it. A second cause is the way these skills are passed on. Traditionally a craft was learned through years of apprenticeship to a master, often within the family, and young people who can earn a salary immediately in other work are understandably reluctant to spend their twenties earning very little while they learn.

Preserving these skills matters for more than sentimental reasons. A craft carries practical knowledge that is not written down anywhere, such as how a particular local clay behaves in the kiln or which wood resists to damp, and once the last practitioner dies that knowledge cannot be reconstructed from the objects alone. Crafts also give communities a distinctive identity and, in many cases, a source of income from visitors and from buyers who are willing to pay for quality.

For these reasons, I believe it is important to keep traditional crafts alive, although this cannot be achieved through nostalgia alone. The most effective approach would be to pay apprentices a proper wage during their training, since this addresses the main reason young people turn away from these skills.

## 第719篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Traffic congestion is becoming worse in many rapidly growing cities. What do you think are the causes of this, and what solutions could be introduced?

### 文章

Congestion in fast-growing cities is often described as an infrastructure failure, as though the roads were simply built too small. The truer explanation is that driving in most cities is priced at far less than it costs, and demand behaves accordingly.

The principal cause is that a driver entering a busy road pays for fuel and for the vehicle, but not for the delay imposed on everyone already there. Because that cost is invisible to the person creating it, individually rational decisions produce a collectively terrible outcome. Rising incomes then amplify the effect: as car ownership becomes affordable to a much larger population, a road network designed for a fraction of that number absorbs the difference in queueing time rather than in price.

A second cause is that alternatives are frequently uncompetitive. Where buses share the same congested lanes as cars, they are slower than driving and no more reliable, so improving them marginally changes nothing. Public transport only attracts drivers when it is faster than the car for the same journey, which usually requires separated right of way rather than better vehicles.

The solutions follow. Charging for road use at busy times and locations makes the hidden cost visible, and even a modest charge shifts enough journeys to restore flow, since congestion is highly sensitive to small changes in volume. This should be paired with dedicated bus lanes or rail, funded from the charge, so that the people priced off the road have somewhere to go. Building additional road capacity, by contrast, tends to attract the traffic it was designed to relieve, and rarely provides lasting relief.

## 第721篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

When children behave badly, some people believe that their parents rather than their schools should be held responsible. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

Children who behave badly are usually a problem for their school before they are a problem for anyone else, which is why schools are so often the first to be blamed. I agree that the primary responsibility lies with parents, but I would distinguish where behaviour originates from who is best placed to change it.

The case for parental responsibility is simply one of time and influence. A child spends its first five years almost entirely at home and learns there what is normal: how disagreements are settled, whether promises are kept, whether adults can be spoken to rudely without consequence. Teachers inherit a child whose expectations have already been formed, and they see that child for a fraction of the week in a group of thirty. Whatever a teacher then attempts has to compete with several years of consistent evidence pointing in the opposite direction. Holding a school accountable for a pattern established before the child arrived is neither fair nor useful.

Schools are not therefore blameless. One with clear rules applied consistently produces better behaviour than one that improvises, and the difference between two schools serving the same neighbourhood is often striking. What a school can do, however, is contain and redirect behaviour rather than originate it, and a teacher trying to compensate for what happens at home is working against the clock.

My position is that parents should answer for how a child behaves and schools for how they respond to it. Blaming teachers for the first is a way of avoiding a conversation nobody wants to have with parents, and it leaves the actual cause untouched. It also asks the wrong institution to solve a problem it did not create.

Nowadays, most large companies operate multi-nationally. To what extent those companies should have responsibilities towards local communities in which they operate?

### 文章

In the modern economy, many major corporations operate across national borders, often generating substantial profits from the countries in which they are based. I strongly believe that such companies should have significant responsibilities towards local communities, although these responsibilities should be practical rather than unlimited.

To begin with, multinational companies have a duty to contribute positively because they benefit directly from local resources, workers, and infrastructure. When a corporation enters a community, it often uses roads, utilities, public services, and local labour to support its operations. Therefore, it is reasonable to expect it to give something back. For example, a large manufacturing company could provide fair wages, safe working conditions, and training programmes for local employees. This would not only improve people’s living standards but also create a more skilled and loyal workforce. As a result, corporate responsibility benefits both the community and the company itself.

Furthermore, multinational businesses should help reduce any negative effects caused by their activities. Some large companies may contribute to pollution, rising living costs, or the decline of small local businesses. If they ignore these problems, local people may suffer while shareholders gain most of the profits. For instance, a mining company operating in a rural area should invest in environmental protection and community healthcare, especially if its work affects air or water quality. Such actions show that economic development should not come at the expense of public welfare.

In conclusion, large multinational companies should accept considerable responsibility towards the communities where they operate. While governments remain primarily responsible for public services, corporations must act ethically by supporting workers, protecting the environment, and investing locally. In the long term, this balanced approach creates trust, stability, and sustainable growth for everyone involved.

Nowadays, some employers think that formal academic qualifications are more important than life experience or personal qualities when they look for new employees. Why is it the case? Is it a positive or negative development

### 文章

In recent decades, a degree has become an essential requirement when employers hire new employees. I believe this trend has arisen because of the improvement of modern education. This means that more people now have degrees, and employers use them as a quick sign of basic skill when there are many applicants for one job. In my view, this is largely a negative development.

Admittedly, a degree is an international standard for getting a job, especially in medicine, education and finance. Employers trust degrees because they may show basic knowledge, hard work, and the ability to finish a long course. For this reason, a degree serves as a convenient filter, simplifying headhunters’ search. Degrees vary by level—bachelor’s, master’s or doctoral—or by university prestige. However, this also means that degrees may become a standard requirement even for jobs where practical skills matter more.

In contrast, the drawbacks are substantial. By ignoring practical skills and personal characteristics, companies may miss good workers or make poor hiring choices. For example, an experienced salesperson without a degree may be rejected for a sales manager role, while a less capable graduate is hired; this can cost the firm clients and revenue. Similarly, a skilled cook without a degree may be overlooked for a head chef role, which can reduce a restaurant’s quality. This trend can leave skilled people feeling unfulfilled. Consequently, the negative repercussions outweigh the benefits, as a degree does not guarantee competence.

In conclusion, although degrees help employers screen candidates and show basic knowledge and commitment, this trend is predominantly negative because it undervalues practical experience and personal qualities. A balanced approach considering both degrees and real-world skills would be fairer and more effective.

Band 7.5

Nowadays technology is increasingly being used to monitor what people are saying and doing. Do you think the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?

### 文章

Nowadays, technology is increasingly being used to monitor what people say and do in both public and private settings. Although this development can improve safety and help prevent crime, I believe that its disadvantages, particularly the loss of privacy and the possibility of misuse, outweigh its benefits.

One major advantage of technological monitoring is that it can improve public safety. Security cameras, for example, can be installed in shopping centres, streets and public transport stations to discourage criminal activities. If a crime occurs, recorded footage can also help the police identify suspects and investigate the incident. In addition, monitoring technology can be useful in workplaces because employers can ensure that employees follow safety rules and protect company information. Therefore, reasonable monitoring can contribute to a safer environment.

However, excessive monitoring can seriously affect people's privacy. When individuals know that their conversations, movements or online activities are being tracked, they may feel uncomfortable and less free to express their opinions. Furthermore, personal information collected through cameras, mobile applications and websites could be misused or shared without people's knowledge. If such data falls into the wrong hands, it may result in identity theft, financial loss or other forms of harm. Another concern is that governments or companies could use monitoring technology excessively, giving them too much information about individuals.

In conclusion, although technological monitoring can enhance security and help prevent and investigate crime, excessive surveillance can threaten privacy and create opportunities for the misuse of personal information. Therefore, I believe that the disadvantages outweigh the advantages, and monitoring should be used only when there is a clear and reasonable purpose.

Nowadays the way many people interact with each other has changed because of technology. In what ways has technology affected the types of relationships that people make? Has this been a positive or negative development?

### 文章

Technology has transformed the way people communicate, and this has significantly changed the kinds of relationships they form. While it has made social connections wider and more convenient, I believe this development is mainly positive, provided that online interaction does not completely replace face-to-face communication.

One major effect of technology is that people can now build relationships beyond their immediate surroundings. In the past, friendships were usually formed at school, work, or within the local community. Today, social media, messaging applications, and video calls allow individuals to maintain contact with people across different cities and countries. In addition, excessive reliance on digital communication may reduce people’s ability to develop deeper emotional bonds through direct conversation, body language, and shared experiences. Despite this, these problems are not caused by technology itself, but by how people use it.

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Older generations often hold some traditional ideas on the correct way of life, thought and behaviour. Most people argue that these are not helpful for younger generations to prepare for modern life. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

It is often argued that traditional ideas held by older generations are no longer useful for preparing younger people for modern life. I strongly disagree with this view because many traditional values remain relevant, while the practical experience of older people can help young adults make sensible decisions.

Many traditional values are still important in contemporary society. Principles such as discipline, honesty, respect and responsibility remain useful because people still need to cooperate, meet deadlines and behave professionally at work. Although technology has changed rapidly, these basic qualities are not made outdated by modern developments. For example, an older family member may teach a young adult to keep promises and complete responsibilities on time. Such habits can help them become reliable at university and in the workplace. As a result, traditional values can complement modern technical skills and help individuals adapt successfully to contemporary life.

Another way older people can support the younger generation is through their practical experience. Having dealt with different financial, professional and family situations, they can explain the possible consequences of important choices. For instance, a family member with years of working experience may advise a young employee to save part of their salary and avoid unnecessary spending. Such guidance can prevent inexperienced adults from making similar mistakes. However, not every traditional belief should be preserved. If a custom limits women's access to education or employment simply because of their gender, it conflicts with the principle of equal opportunity and should be reconsidered. Therefore, useful life lessons should be retained, whereas unfair traditions should be adapted to modern social values.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree that traditional ideas are generally unhelpful for younger generations. Discipline, honesty and respect remain valuable in modern life, while the experience of older people can provide useful guidance. Nevertheless, traditions that create unfairness or restrict equal opportunities should be changed.

## 第741篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Practice Question for IELTS Submit your responses and I will evaluate each response. An increasing number of people are choosing to have cosmetic surgery in order to improve their appearance. Why are more people choosing to have operation to change the way they look? Do you think this a positive or negative development?Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

### 文章

Regarding the question of why the number of cosmetic surgeries has increased, I am of the opinion that social pressures continue to increase due to the overexposure to social media. This strikes me as an increasingly dangerous trend, because it preys on vulnerabilities.

With the widespread access to social media, our society has become increasingly reliant on being perceived as conventionally attractive. Content creators measure their success in money and engagement through comments and „likes".

Therefore, to be successful, one has to steadily attract new followers and keep them motivated to comment on your content. YouTube's statistics show the continued success of „beauty-influencers" throughout the years. While other trends typically experience fluctuations in popularity, the interest in being seen as beautiful has not diminished. This leads to a culture in which being beautiful is a legitimate profession.  This continued stream of revenue is only feasible, however, if the beauty of the creator is upheld. Because of this, surgeries have become the standard to ensure long-lasting youth and good looks. The film industry has faced similar issues for decades, with stars being both praised and criticised for their choices regarding cosmetic procedures. Consequently, these trends can lead to many fans emulating the behaviours of their idols.

Since cosmetic surgeries have become so commonplace online, many young women especially feel the need to fit into this skewed perception of beauty. This has been an issue in my youth over a decade ago, but when asked, younger acquaintances have assured me that the pressures have increased drastically. Feelings and fears commonly described, such as fear-of-missing-out or „FOMO“, along with the social pressure to present a filtered, perfect version of oneself online, may result in an increase in cosmetic procedures.

There is a myriad of dangers associated with this development, from an increase in rates of body dysmorphia to the financial strain, especially on young people. It is not uncommon for teenagers to feel uncomfortable in their changing bodies. But rigid, unachievable standards set by beauty gurus online only heighten the discrepancy between a young person's appearance and their idolised aesthetic. The prevalence of surgical means to rectify perceived flaws is presented as the correct, socially acceptable choice. This can have detrimental effects on teenagers, encouraging dangerous behaviours such as self-harm tendencies and other maladaptive coping mechanisms. When the possibility of having a surgical procedure performed is offered, those desperate enough are willing to go into debt to afford it. Especially in countries like the United States, this debt can accompany somebody for decades to come. It might even impede other choices, such as going to college or buying a house, due to negative credit scores.

Overall, the rise in cosmetic procedures can be at least in part attributed to the online culture around beauty standards. This is a distinctly negative development, because it exploits deep-seated insecurities, especially in young people and might lead to decisions that have a detrimental effect on a person's future.

## 第742篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Scientists and technlogy experts seem to be more valued by modern society than musicians and artists. To what extent do you agree?

### 文章

Modern society does appear to reward scientists and technology experts more generously than musicians and artists. While this emphasis is understandable, I largely agree that it reflects an imbalance, since the creative arts deserve far greater recognition than they receive.

There are clear reasons why scientific and technological professionals are prized. Their work produces tangible, measurable results: vaccines save lives, engineers build infrastructure, and software developers drive economic growth. Governments and corporations therefore invest heavily in research, and graduates in these fields typically enjoy secure, well-paid careers. By contrast, artists often struggle with unstable incomes, and parents frequently discourage children from pursuing creative paths.

However, this hierarchy overlooks the profound contribution that the arts make to human wellbeing. Music, literature and painting shape cultural identity, foster empathy and offer comfort during difficult times, as the surge in creative activity during recent global lockdowns demonstrated. Moreover, creativity is not separate from innovation; many technological breakthroughs, from product design to film animation, depend on artistic imagination.

Admittedly, one could argue that basic needs such as healthcare, food and energy must take priority over entertainment, and that scientific progress therefore deserves greater financial support. This is a fair point, yet it does not justify the social undervaluing of artists. A society that measures worth solely by practical utility risks neglecting the emotional and spiritual dimensions of life.

In conclusion, although scientists and technology experts make indispensable contributions, I believe modern society undervalues musicians and artists. Governments should fund arts education and cultural institutions more generously, so that both disciplines are respected as complementary pillars of a fulfilling civilisation.

## 第743篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Should a city try to preserve its old, historic buildings or destroy them and replace them with modern buildings?

### 文章

Cities should usually preserve old, historic buildings rather than demolish them and replace them with modern ones. Although modern development is sometimes necessary, historic architecture gives a city identity, supports the economy, and connects people with their past. Therefore, I believe preservation should be the main priority, except when a building is genuinely unsafe or impossible to restore.

The strongest reason to protect historic buildings is that they represent a city’s culture and character. Modern buildings often look similar across the world, with glass towers, shopping centres, and concrete apartment blocks. Old buildings, however, show the traditions, materials, and artistic skills of earlier generations. For example, the old markets of Istanbul and the historic streets of Rome make these cities instantly recognisable. If such places were replaced by ordinary modern structures, the cities would lose much of their uniqueness.

Historic buildings can also bring clear economic benefits. Many tourists travel specifically to see ancient houses, castles, temples, or traditional neighbourhoods. This creates income for hotels, restaurants, guides, and local shops. For instance, a restored old town can become a major attraction, while a newly built office block may interest only a small number of businesses. Because of this, preservation can support both cultural pride and local employment.

However, cities should not keep every old building without question. Some structures may be dangerous, severely damaged, or unsuitable for modern needs. In these cases, the best solution is often renovation rather than destruction. An old factory, for example, can be turned into a museum, library, or apartment complex while keeping its original appearance.

In conclusion, cities should generally preserve their historic buildings because they protect identity, educate future generations, and strengthen tourism. Modern buildings are useful, but development should not erase the history that makes a city special.

## 第746篇

### 题目

Some believe that pets should stay at home at all times, while others feel they should be allowed outside the home. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

### 文章

It is often argued that pets should remain indoors at all times, while others believe that they should be allowed to spend time outside. Both perspectives have clear advantages; however, I believe that supervised outdoor access is the better option.

On the one hand, keeping pets indoors can be beneficial in several ways. A major benefit of this approach is that it protects animals from possible dangers. This is important because pets may face traffic accidents, aggressive animals, or harmful substances when they are outside alone. Keeping them indoors also reduces the risk of getting lost, which can give owners greater peace of mind. For example, an indoor cat is less likely to be injured by a moving vehicle; as a result, its safety can be better protected. Because of this, many owners prefer to keep their pets inside.

On the other hand, I believe that allowing pets outside offers greater benefits. What makes this option more appealing is that outdoor activity can improve their physical and mental health. Not only does this provide animals with regular exercise, but it also gives them opportunities to explore new surroundings. At the same time, outdoor activity can reduce boredom and encourage healthier behaviour. For instance, a dog that is taken for daily walks can release excess energy; consequently, it may become calmer and more active at home.

In conclusion, keeping pets indoors certainly provides greater safety; however, I believe that supervised outdoor access is preferable because regular exercise and mental stimulation are essential for their overall well-being.

## 第747篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Some believe that protecting the environment is the responsibility of individuals, while others think that governments and large companies should take the lead. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

### 文章

It is often argued that protecting the environment is primarily the responsibility of individuals, while others believe that governments and large corporations should take the lead. Although individuals have an important role to play, I believe that governments and major companies have a far greater ability to create meaningful and long-term environmental change.

On the one hand, individuals can contribute significantly to environmental protection through their daily choices. For example, people can reduce their use of plastic, recycle household waste, use public transport and avoid wasting water and electricity. If millions of people adopt these habits, the combined effect can be substantial. Furthermore, individual behaviour can influence businesses, as consumers who prefer environmentally friendly products may encourage companies to adopt greener production methods.

On the other hand, governments and large corporations have much greater resources and influence. Governments can introduce and enforce environmental laws, invest in renewable energy and improve public transport infrastructure. They can also impose taxes or penalties on companies that cause excessive pollution. Large corporations, meanwhile, control huge production and supply chains, meaning that changes in their manufacturing processes can have an impact on millions of consumers. For instance, a major company that replaces fossil fuels with renewable energy across its factories could reduce its carbon emissions on a much larger scale than an individual household ever could.

In my view, environmental protection requires cooperation between individuals, governments and businesses. However, governments and large corporations should take the lead because they have the financial resources, authority and technological capacity to make large-scale changes. Individuals should support these efforts through responsible choices in their everyday lives.

In conclusion, individuals undoubtedly have a responsibility to protect the environment, but governments and large companies are in a much stronger position to tackle environmental problems on a national and global scale. Therefore, I believe that they should take the primary responsibility while encouraging individuals to contribute.

## 第748篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Some countries have introduced laws to limit the working hours that an employer can ask from an employee. Why are these law introduced? Is this a positive or negative trend?

### 文章

In recent decades, a considerable number of changes concerning the relationship between employers and employees have been enacted by governments. For instance, some authorities have introduced legislation that reduces working days for employees; consequently, contemporary society is experiencing heightened levels of stress, while a shortage of family time undermines traditional family values. I firmly believe that this is a predominantly positive trend owing to its beneficial effects on both businesses and individuals.

One of the principal reasons for implementing such laws is the growing prevalence of stress. Governments are expressing concern about residents’ well-being and mental health, given the increasing number of employees seeking psychological counselling. Another justification for introducing these measures is that family members encounter obstacles to spending leisure time together because of excessive workloads in the office. Policymakers are worried about the erosion of traditional family values and the adverse impact on children’s upbringing. Therefore, adjustments to working hours are essential in order to establish a healthier work-life balance and reduce burnout rates.

Moreover, reduced working hours positively affect both employees and businesses. Workers gain more time for family and rest; as a result, happier and healthier employees tend to be more focused and productive. For businesses, this translates into higher efficiency, lower staff turnover, and reduced costs. For example, Microsoft Japan’s four-day working week boosted productivity by 40% while cutting electricity costs. Hence, shorter hours create a mutually beneficial outcome: individuals enjoy greater well-being, and companies become more efficient and profitable.

In conclusion, laws that reduce working days are a predominantly positive trend. They alleviate rising stress and safeguard family values, while simultaneously benefiting businesses through higher productivity and lower costs. Therefore, governments should continue supporting such reforms to enhance both people’s well-being and economic efficiency.

## 第749篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Some parents think it is good to give their children mobile phones while others disagree. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

### 文章

Some parents believe that giving children mobile phones is beneficial, while others think that children should not have access to them. Although mobile phones can be useful for communication and education, I believe that children should only be given them at an appropriate age and with clear limits.

On the one hand, there are several advantages to giving children mobile phones. The most important benefit is that parents can easily contact their children, especially in emergencies. For example, if a child is travelling home from school alone or becomes lost, they can immediately call their parents for help. In addition, smartphones can be useful educational tools. Children can use learning applications, online dictionaries and educational videos to support their studies. Mobile phones may also help young people become familiar with technology, which is an important skill in modern society.

On the other hand, there are also significant disadvantages. Children may become addicted to their phones and spend too much time playing games, watching videos or using social media. As a result, they may spend less time studying, exercising or communicating with family members face to face. Another concern is online safety. Young children may be exposed to inappropriate content, cyberbullying or strangers on social media. Furthermore, excessive use of mobile phones, particularly before bedtime, can negatively affect children's sleeping habits and concentration.

In my opinion, completely preventing children from using mobile phones is unrealistic because technology is now an important part of everyday life. However, parents should not give smartphones to children without supervision. They should set limits on screen time, control the applications their children use and teach them how to behave safely online.

In conclusion, mobile phones can provide children with greater safety and educational opportunities, but they can also create problems such as addiction and exposure to harmful online content. Therefore, I believe children can have mobile phones as long as their parents carefully supervise their use.

### 文章

It is often claimed that the prevalence of the internet has reduced the need for libraries. I disagree with this statement because numerous people still prefer reading physical materials, and these institutions provide access to publications through legitimate and authorised sources.

There are many individuals who would rather read and obtain printed books than read from a screen. With this method, they can focus solely on reading instead of getting distracted by notifications or pop-up ads. Moreover, many people, especially those who use electronic devices for work, consider reading a tangible book to be a break from looking at screens. For example, in South Korea, some public libraries have introduced phone-free reading spaces where visitors are encouraged to put away their electronic devices and read printed works without digital distractions. Thus, such facilities remain valuable for individuals who wish to maintain their reading habits.

Although reading or searching for specific data on the internet can be more convenient than going to a library, the latter ensures that the information and reading materials are obtained from legitimate sources. This is especially important when the knowledge being sought is contained in an ancient or rare book, as it may be difficult to determine whether information found online is accurate or reliable. Furthermore, some may choose not to pay for online publications when unauthorised or stolen versions are available on the internet, allowing them to access these works without purchasing them. Although this violates copyright laws, in contrast, libraries allow people to access legitimate copies of such materials for free. For instance, since 2024, to encourage citizens to read more and use legitimate sources for free, the Saudi Ministry of Culture has established public reading facilities in many neighbourhoods in Riyadh.

In conclusion, I strongly believe in the importance of libraries, which allow people to access physical reading materials in a legitimate and authorised way.

## 第751篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Some people argue that universities should focus primarily on specific vocational training and practical skills for the workplace, rather than teaching a broad range of traditional academic subjects. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

Whether universities should prioritise vocational training and practical skills over traditional academic subjects has become a topic of debate. While some people believe that practical skills are more valuable because they prepare students for the workplace, I disagree with the idea that universities should focus primarily on them. In my view, a balanced approach is more beneficial because students need both practical abilities and academic knowledge.

On the one hand, there are strong arguments for giving greater importance to practical skills at university. Modern employers often expect graduates to have job-specific knowledge that can be applied immediately in the workplace. For example, an accounting graduate may need to know how to use accounting software, prepare financial reports and follow relevant financial procedures. These practical skills can help graduates adapt to their jobs more quickly and reduce the amount of workplace training required. Therefore, vocational education can play an important role in improving students' employability.

On the other hand, traditional academic subjects should not be overlooked because they develop a range of transferable skills. Studying subjects such as history, literature and the arts can improve students' critical thinking, research and communication abilities. For instance, a history student learns to examine evidence, evaluate different perspectives and construct logical arguments. These abilities can be useful in a wide variety of careers, even when the job itself is unrelated to history. Furthermore, exposure to different academic fields can help young people discover their interests and make better-informed career choices.

In my opinion, universities should combine practical training with traditional academic education rather than prioritising one at the expense of the other. Practical skills can prepare students for immediate employment, while academic knowledge can help them develop the critical thinking and adaptability required throughout their careers.

In conclusion, although vocational training is highly valuable in preparing graduates for the modern workplace, universities should not focus primarily on practical skills. A combination of academic knowledge and workplace-oriented training is the most effective way to prepare students for both employment and long-term professional development.

## 第752篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Some people believe movie reviews are useful. Others argue the reviews may spoil the audience’s mindset before watching the movie. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

### 文章

Whether reading movie reviews before watching a film is beneficial remains a subject of debate. While some people believe reviews help audiences make informed choices and gain a deeper understanding of a film, others argue that they influence expectations and reduce the enjoyment of watching it. In my opinion, reviews are valuable as long as they provide balanced opinions without revealing important plot details.

On the one hand, movie reviews serve as a useful source of information for people who want to spend their time and money wisely. Since hundreds of films are released every year, viewers often rely on reviews to decide which ones are worth watching. Professional critics usually assess factors such as the quality of the acting, the storyline, cinematography, and originality, enabling audiences to select films that match their interests. For example, before buying tickets for a newly released film, many people read reviews on websites such as IMDb or Rotten Tomatoes to avoid spending money on a poorly made production. In addition, well-written reviews often explain hidden themes or cultural references, allowing viewers to appreciate the film on a deeper level rather than simply following the plot.

Despite these advantages, many people believe that reviews can negatively affect the viewing experience. A glowing review may create expectations that are impossible for any film to satisfy, whereas an extremely negative one may discourage people from watching a movie they would otherwise enjoy. This happens because people naturally compare their own opinions with those of professional critics, making it harder to judge the film independently. Moreover, some reviews reveal major plot twists or even the ending. As suspense and surprise are often essential parts of storytelling, knowing these details beforehand can significantly reduce the emotional impact of the film.

In my view, movie reviews are undoubtedly beneficial, provided that they remain spoiler-free and present balanced evaluations instead of attempting to dictate public opinion. Their main purpose should be to inform audiences about a film's strengths and weaknesses while leaving enough mystery for viewers to experience the story for themselves. In this way, people can make informed decisions without sacrificing the excitement of discovering the plot on their own.

In conclusion, although movie reviews can sometimes shape expectations or reveal important story elements, they generally help audiences choose films more wisely and understand them more deeply. Therefore, when written responsibly, reviews contribute positively to the overall cinematic experience rather than diminishing it.

### 文章

While some people believe that governments should invest more in public transportation, others argue that constructing additional roads is a more effective solution. In my opinion, improving public transport is the better approach because it can reduce the number of private vehicles on the roads.

On the one hand, building more roads can help reduce congestion in areas where existing roads are overcrowded. When new roads are constructed, traffic can be distributed across a larger network, which may shorten travelling times for drivers. For example, a new road connecting residential areas with business districts can provide an alternative route and prevent large numbers of cars from using the same streets. Therefore, expanding road networks can be useful, particularly in rapidly developing cities.

On the other hand, investing in public transportation is likely to have a more long-term impact. If buses, trains and underground systems are affordable, reliable and convenient, more people may choose them instead of private cars. As a result, the number of vehicles on major roads could decrease considerably. Furthermore, effective public transport can be particularly beneficial in large cities because it allows many people to travel at the same time without requiring additional road space. For instance, an efficient metro system can transport thousands of passengers during peak hours, potentially reducing pressure on the road network.

In conclusion, although constructing new roads can provide additional routes and temporarily reduce congestion, I believe that governments should give greater priority to public transportation. A reliable and affordable transport system can encourage people to leave their cars at home and therefore provide a more sustainable solution to traffic problems.

## 第755篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Some people believe that it is good to share as much information as possible in scientific research, business and the academic world. Others believe that some information is too important or too valueable to be shared freely. Discuss both view and give your own opinion

### 文章

The unrestricted exchange of information is widely regarded as a driving force behind scientific progress, commercial innovation and academic advancement. Nevertheless, there are circumstances in which making knowledge freely accessible may expose individuals or organisations to considerable risks. This essay will examine both perspectives and argue that, although information-sharing should be encouraged in principle, material that is commercially sensitive or potentially harmful should be subject to appropriate safeguards.

There are compelling reasons to favour the broad dissemination of information. Scientific and academic knowledge, in particular, tends to generate greater value when it is subjected to scrutiny from a diverse range of researchers and practitioners. Sharing findings enables others to challenge assumptions, replicate results and identify shortcomings that the original author may have overlooked. The resulting exchange of perspectives can, in turn, accelerate innovation by allowing subsequent researchers to build upon existing discoveries rather than duplicating work that has already been undertaken. In this respect, openness is not merely a matter of cooperation; it is an important mechanism through which knowledge can be refined and cumulative progress achieved.

That said, unrestricted disclosure is not universally desirable. In the commercial sphere, companies may invest substantial resources in developing proprietary technologies, business strategies or market research, and revealing such information without safeguards could effectively transfer the benefits of that investment to competitors. Similarly, premature disclosure of certain scientific findings could have unintended consequences if the information were misinterpreted, exploited or disseminated without adequate oversight. This does not necessarily justify secrecy, but rather suggests that access should sometimes be regulated according to the sensitivity and potential consequences of the information involved.

In conclusion, the widespread sharing of information is essential to scientific, academic and technological advancement, as knowledge becomes more valuable when it can be scrutinised and built upon by others. However, this principle should not be interpreted as requiring unrestricted disclosure. In my view, information should be shared by default, while commercially sensitive, confidential or potentially harmful material should be subject to proportionate restrictions.

It is often claimed that athletes need to be physically fit to succeed, while others believe that mental strength is more important for controlling their bodies and pursuing their goals. Personally, I believe that both are necessary for sporting success.

On the one hand, physical fitness is essential in various sports to ensure effective competition. Each sport requires specific physical abilities, and if these requirements are not met by the athlete, they might struggle to compete with others at the same level. They may also be prone to injuries if they push their bodies beyond their physical abilities. Therefore, this could hold them back from reaching their goals and achieving a high position in their sport. That is why I believe having a good physique and sufficient strength is vital for athletes, but I think these qualities are not enough on their own to ensure success.

On the other hand, athletes need a strong mentality to reach milestones in their careers. Often, when engaging in a sport, a person has to compete with others who might have various advantages over them. In order not to be intimidated by these advantages, pressure, or difficult circumstances, athletes should remain calm, focused and most importantly, believe in themselves. Even if they fail, they should have the mentality to keep trying and preparing again and again. ## 第761篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Some people believe that the government should spend money on building train and subway lines to reduce traffic congestion. Others think that building more and wider roads is the better way to reduce traffic congestion. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

### 文章

It is often argued that governments should invest in train and subway lines to reduce traffic congestion, while others believe that building more and wider roads would be more effective. Both views have some valid points. However, I personally favour greater investment in rail transport because it can reduce reliance on private vehicles and move large numbers of commuters efficiently.

On the one hand, I believe that governments should give greater priority to train and subway systems. One important advantage is that reliable rail services can reduce people's reliance on private vehicles. When commuters have a convenient alternative, they can travel to work without driving for the entire journey. For instance, an office worker living in a residential area could take a bus to a nearby station and complete the rest of the journey by subway. In this way, fewer cars would be needed on busy urban roads each day. Rail transport also has a much greater passenger-carrying capacity than private vehicles. A frequent subway service, for example, can move thousands of commuters through a busy city centre during peak hours. This can reduce pressure on roads and lower the demand for parking, making rail investment a useful long-term use of public funds.

On the other hand, some people consider road expansion a more practical solution. Giving vehicles additional space can improve traffic flow, particularly during busy periods. If a major two-lane road is widened to four lanes, for example, more vehicles can travel along it at the same time, which may shorten journeys in the short term. Wider roads are also necessary in smaller towns and locations without rail services because buses, delivery vehicles and emergency services depend on them. Nevertheless, this approach may have limitations in major cities. Easier driving can encourage more people to use private vehicles, so the initial improvement may gradually disappear as traffic increases. In some cases, congestion may simply shift to another road or junction rather than disappear completely. For this reason, road construction can be useful where rail transport is impractical, but it is less likely to provide a lasting solution to congestion in densely populated cities.

In conclusion, although wider roads can improve traffic flow in some locations, I believe that greater priority should be given to train and subway systems. Their ability to reduce private-car use and transport large numbers of commuters makes them a more sustainable approach to congestion, particularly in densely populated cities.

It is increasingly argued that university students should focus exclusively on subjects related to their main field of study. While there are reasonable arguments on both sides of this issue, I largely disagree with this view because studying broader subjects can develop valuable skills and prepare students for an unpredictable job market.

The strongest argument against restricting students’ choices is that exposure to different disciplines can broaden their intellectual abilities. This is largely because subjects outside a student’s major often require different ways of thinking, meaning that learners can develop skills such as critical thinking, creativity and effective communication. For instance, an engineering student who takes psychology or public speaking may become better at understanding people and presenting complex ideas clearly. Taken together, these factors demonstrate that a broader education can produce more versatile graduates, thereby strengthening the case for allowing students greater academic freedom.

A further consideration is that modern employment increasingly requires people to work across different fields. The underlying reason is that many professional roles involve a combination of technical knowledge and transferable skills, particularly when employees are expected to adapt to rapidly changing technologies and business practices. A case in point is a financial analyst who may need not only a strong understanding of economics but also knowledge of data analysis and computer science to perform effectively. Overall, this suggests that studying a wider range of subjects can improve graduates’ adaptability, which further supports the view that students should not be limited to courses directly related to their major.

In conclusion, although specialising in one’s main field may provide certain academic benefits, I remain convinced that university students should have the freedom to explore other subjects. This is primarily because broader study develops transferable abilities, while greater academic flexibility can help graduates adapt to changing professional demands.

Violence in television programmes and computer games has become a common concern in modern society. Millions of people watch action films or play violent games without becoming aggressive or criminal. Moreover, behaviour is usually shaped by deeper factors, such as family background, education, poverty, and mental health. It is often argued that manufacturers and supermarkets should reduce the amount of packaging used for goods, while others believe that customers should avoid purchasing heavily packaged products. Both views have some valid points. However, I personally believe that businesses should bear greater responsibility because they control packaging decisions and can reduce waste on a much larger scale.

On the one hand, I believe that manufacturers and supermarkets should take greater responsibility for reducing excessive packaging. One important reason is that they control how products are packed and presented to consumers. If businesses remove unnecessary materials and replace them with recyclable alternatives, the amount of waste can be reduced at its source. For instance, a large supermarket could replace excessive plastic wrapping with recyclable paper. This would reduce plastic waste and environmental pollution. Furthermore, large manufacturers usually have the financial and technical resources to develop more sustainable packaging. By introducing recyclable materials across thousands of products, they can create a much larger environmental benefit than individual consumers can achieve.

On the other hand, some people argue that customers should avoid buying products with excessive packaging. Their purchasing decisions can influence businesses because companies usually respond to changes in consumer demand. When shoppers consistently choose products with minimal or recyclable packaging, supermarkets may offer more environmentally friendly alternatives. For example, if customers regularly choose products with simple recyclable packaging, a supermarket may increase its supply of such goods. As a result, consumer behaviour can contribute to wider changes in the market. Nevertheless, customers cannot directly control how products are designed and packaged. Although responsible purchasing is useful, it should complement rather than replace the responsibility of manufacturers and supermarkets.

Some individuals dislike change and prefer to spend their lives doing the same things, as they feel comfortable in familiar surroundings, while others believe that change can bring valuable opportunities. I believe that humans should not live in monotony, although major changes should be considered carefully before being made.

From one perspective, some people prefer staying in their comfort zone rather than experiencing new situations. They feel secure repeating activities they are familiar with, particularly when they have become successful at them after overcoming many difficulties. Therefore, they may be unwilling to start again and experience the stress and uncertainty associated with unfamiliar circumstances. Moreover, others avoid trying new products or activities because they fear being disappointed and consequently stick to what they already enjoy. For example, many elderly citizens in Saudi Arabia mainly eat traditional dishes because these were the foods they grew up with, making them less willing to experiment with unfamiliar cuisines.

From another perspective, many individuals see change as an opportunity for growth because it exposes them to different experiences, friends and environments. As a result, they may gain knowledge, develop relationships and create memorable experiences. I believe that changing one’s circumstances is particularly important when the alternative offers clear benefits. For instance, people should consider moving to a better home if their current one has serious problems or accepting a significantly better job opportunity rather than remaining somewhere simply because it is familiar. However, such decisions should be based on careful consideration. An employee receiving a higher salary, for example, should also assess the new job’s location, working hours and responsibilities before accepting the offer.

## 第775篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Some people think that good health is a basic human need and the medical service should not be run by profit-making companies. Do disadvantages outweigh advantages? Give your opinion.

### 文章

Access to adequate healthcare is widely regarded as a fundamental human right, leading many to argue that medical services ought to be managed by public authorities rather than commercial enterprises. While allowing profit-making companies to operate in the healthcare sector does present certain economic advantages, I believe that the drawbacks—specifically regarding equity and quality of care—far outweigh the benefits.

On the one hand, private healthcare providers can introduce significant advantages through efficiency and innovation. Driven by the profit motive, private medical companies often invest heavily in state-of-the-art technology, advanced research, and modern infrastructure. This competitive drive can shorten waiting lists and attract top-tier medical professionals, offering a higher standard of comfort and specialized care for those who can afford it. Furthermore, private sector involvement can relieve some of the financial burden on state-funded healthcare systems by accommodating patients who would otherwise rely entirely on public hospitals.

On the other hand, the disadvantages of running medical services for profit are profound, primarily concerning social inequality. When healthcare is treated as a commodity, access is determined by financial capability rather than medical need. Consequently, lower-income populations may be priced out of essential treatments, preventive care, and life-saving medications, exacerbating societal divisions. Additionally, profit-driven management often prioritizes lucrative medical procedures over less profitable fields, such as mental health care or rural medicine, leaving critical public health needs unmet.

In conclusion, although the private sector brings financial investment and technological advancement to medicine, these benefits are overshadowed by the severe inequalities it creates. Because health is a universal necessity, I firmly believe that medical services should remain primarily under public stewardship to ensure equal access for all members of society, regardless of wealth.

Hosting major international sporting events, such as the Olympic Games or the Football World Cup, can bring both benefits and challenges to the host country. Although organising such events requires substantial investment and can cause temporary disruption, I believe the advantages outweigh the disadvantages because they can create employment and stimulate economic growth.

One major advantage of hosting an international sporting event is the positive impact it can have on the local economy. Such events attract thousands of domestic and international visitors who spend money on accommodation, food, transportation and entertainment. This increased demand allows local businesses to generate greater profits and may encourage them to recruit additional workers. As a result, more employment opportunities become available to local residents, enabling them to earn a stable income. Furthermore, increased consumer spending can generate additional tax revenue for the government, which can be invested in public services and infrastructure. Therefore, major sporting events can contribute considerably to the economic development of the host country.

Nevertheless, there are some significant disadvantages associated with hosting these events. A sudden influx of visitors can put considerable pressure on transportation systems, resulting in traffic congestion and longer commuting times for residents. Moreover, governments often have to spend substantial amounts of public money on stadiums, security and transport infrastructure. This may temporarily reduce the funding available for essential services such as healthcare and education. However, many of these problems are relatively short-term, while improved infrastructure and increased tourism can continue to benefit the country after the event has ended.

In conclusion, although hosting major sporting events can cause traffic problems and require significant initial investment, I believe the economic benefits are more substantial. Increased tourism, employment and business activity, together with improved infrastructure, can provide lasting benefits to the host country.

Some people think that money spend on technology development for space exploration is unjustified. They believe there are other beneficial ways to spend it. To what you agree or disagree with this statement?

### 文章

Some people argue that spending large amounts of money on space exploration is unnecessary and that these financial resources should instead be used to address more urgent problems on Earth. While I acknowledge that governments have many important domestic responsibilities, I disagree with this view because investment in space technology generates long-term scientific, economic and social benefits.

Those who oppose space exploration believe that public funds should be directed towards pressing issues such as healthcare, education and poverty reduction. Millions of people around the world still lack access to quality medical services, clean drinking water and adequate housing. Therefore, critics argue that it is difficult to justify spending billions of dollars on missions to space when many citizens struggle to meet their basic needs. For example, monitoring climate change, predicting natural disasters and detecting potentially dangerous asteroids all depend on advanced space technology. Without continued research, scientific progress would be significantly slowed.

In my opinion, governments should adopt a balanced approach by investing in both space exploration and essential public services. Scientific advancement and social welfare should not be viewed as competing priorities because technological breakthroughs often provide long-term solutions to problems facing society. At the same time, governments must ensure that basic human needs are adequately addressed.

In conclusion, although many people believe that money allocated to space exploration should instead be spent on urgent social issues, I disagree. ## 第786篇
