## 第1355篇

### 分数

Band 9.0

### 题目

Some people think that all advertising aimed at children under the age of twelve should be banned. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

A ban is the right instrument, but the usual justification for it — that advertising makes children want things — is too weak to carry the argument, since that is what advertising does to everyone and we permit it. The reason for treating children differently is narrower and a great deal stronger.

Persuasion is legitimate between parties who both know it is happening. An adult watching a commercial may well be influenced, but the influence operates through a defence: the viewer knows the source has an interest, discounts what is said accordingly, and can reasonably be held responsible for what they do next. That defence is absent in a six-year-old and only half-assembled at eleven. A message pitched at that audience does not persuade so much as install, and the transaction has no informed party on one side of it.

This is why the objection about parental responsibility misses its target. Parents are indeed the ones holding the money, but the strategy is not aimed at the purchase; it is aimed at the child, who is then deployed against the parent in a supermarket aisle. Placing the burden on families amounts to asking them to win, repeatedly and in public, an argument that has been professionally engineered for them to lose.

The real difficulty is not principle but drafting. Advertising to children is no longer a slot between cartoons. It is a character skin in a game, a cereal woven into an animated series, a video made by someone whose audience is nine, and any statute framed around intent will be complied with exactly and evaded entirely. The test has to be the audience a message actually reaches, and the liability has to sit with the brand paying for it rather than the platform carrying it.

Written that way, the ban is enforceable and I would support it without reservation. Written as a rule about television, it redirects a budget rather than reducing one.

## 第1358篇

### 分数

Band 9.0

### 题目

Some people think that children should not be allowed to own a smartphone until they start secondary school. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

The proposal is sound and the reasoning usually offered for it is not, and the difference matters because it decides what happens on the child's eleventh birthday. The case is almost always made in terms of protection — screen time, strangers, unsuitable material — as though a smartphone were a hazard to be kept away from small children until they have grown large enough to survive it.

What that framing misses is that the difficulty is not the child's size but the device's design. A phone is not a passive object that becomes safe with maturity; it is an interface refined by continuous experimentation to capture as much attention as it possibly can, and it works on adults who understand precisely what is being done to them. Handing one to a nine-year-old is not unwise because nine-year-olds are fragile. It is unwise because nobody at any age has the willpower the arrangement quietly assumes, and a nine-year-old has not yet built the habits that partially compensate for lacking it.

That is why I would delay ownership, and equally why I am sceptical of the assumption buried in the question, that secondary school marks the point where the problem dissolves. Eleven is not a threshold of competence. It is the age at which social exclusion begins to cost more than the device does, so most families concede. Treating that concession as a graduation invites the worst possible handover: full ownership, no scaffolding, on the grounds that the child is now old enough.

So keep smartphones out of primary schools, but for the honest reason. Those years are worth protecting not because children are too young to cope, but because they are the last stretch in which sustained attention can be practised without competition. What should follow is a slow, supervised loosening, in a household where the adults are visibly subject to the same discipline they are imposing. A rule about age, on its own, relocates the problem to the following September.

## 第1360篇

### 分数

Band 9.0

### 题目

Some schools teach children of all abilities together in the same class, while others divide students into groups according to how well they perform. Discuss both approaches and give your own opinion.

### 文章

Most of the damage attributed to ability grouping is not caused by the grouping. It is caused by the way schools assign children to groups and then decline to move them. A set allocated at eleven on the basis of a single test, taught a narrower curriculum by less experienced staff and revisited once a year at most, is not really a teaching arrangement at all; it is a prediction that arranges for its own fulfilment.

The practical case for setting deserves more respect than it usually gets. A teacher facing a class whose attainment spans four years has three options, all bad: aim at the middle and lose both ends, prepare three parallel lessons for one room, or let the strongest students spend a term revisiting what they already know. In subjects that build strictly on what came before, this is not a matter of preference. A student who cannot manipulate fractions will not learn algebra by sitting in a lesson about algebra, and no amount of good intention alters that.

The objection to sorting, though, is not really about pedagogy either. Attainment at eleven correlates heavily with how much reading happened at home, so a system that sorts early is partly sorting by background while telling children it has measured their ability. That message is the injury, and it is administered by the label rather than by the teaching. A child who understands themselves to be in the group that is not expected to progress will, with remarkable consistency, stop expecting it too.

Both views therefore describe something true, and the argument between them is less important than a third thing neither mentions. Group where the subject is genuinely cumulative and teach together where it is not; but make the groups small, temporary and frequently reassessed, put the most capable teachers with the students furthest behind, and ensure that moving up is a routine event rather than an exception. Setting done that way is a timetable. Done the usual way, it is a verdict.

## 第1362篇

### 分数

Band 9.0

### 题目

Streaming platforms have largely replaced scheduled television and, for many people, trips to the cinema. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of this change.

### 文章

The convenience argument is settled and not very interesting. Of course it is better to watch a programme when you are free than when a scheduler decides you are; nobody who has waited a week for an episode wants that week back. The change worth examining is what happens to the things being watched, and to the fact that we are no longer watching them together.

On the production side, the shift has been genuinely liberating in one direction and quietly constricting in another. A series in Korean or Danish can now find a global audience without a broadcaster in each country deciding in advance that its viewers would not tolerate subtitles, and work that would once have been deleted from an archive stays available indefinitely. Against that, platforms commission from behavioural data, and data is necessarily a record of what has already happened. The result is a catalogue that is wide but strangely uniform: enormous choice among things that resemble other things.

The loss that receives least attention is simultaneity. A programme broadcast to a whole country at once produced something no library of on-demand titles can — a conversation the next morning that nobody had to arrange, between participants who had not chosen each other. That was never the point of broadcasting, but it was one of its effects, and it is gone. Cinema attendance matters for a related reason: a film watched among strangers in the dark is a different experience from the same film watched with a phone within reach, and the second is not simply a portable version of the first.

So the advantages are real and belong to viewers, while the disadvantages are structural and belong to everyone, including the viewers who cannot see them. I would not restore the schedule. But it is worth saying that we have traded a shared, imposed, occasionally boring culture for a private and infinitely responsive one, and that the second is better in almost every respect except the ones that only become visible once they are missing.

## 第1364篇

### 分数

Band 9.0

### 题目

Traditional crafts such as weaving, pottery and woodcarving are dying out in many parts of the world. Why is this happening? Do you think it is important to keep these skills alive?

### 文章

Traditional crafts rarely disappear because people stop admiring them. Handwoven cloth and thrown pottery are admired more than ever; what has vanished is the arrangement that once allowed someone to make a living by producing them. That distinction answers both parts of this question.

The first cause is that a craft now competes with a machine rather than with other craftspeople. A village weaver once supplied cloth that could not be bought elsewhere; today the same cloth, or something close enough for most buyers, arrives from a factory at a fraction of the price. The handmade version survives only as a luxury, and a luxury market is too small and too fickle to support many workers. The second cause follows from the first. Crafts were traditionally learned over years, by working alongside a master for little or no pay, and that bargain made sense only when the trade guaranteed a livelihood at the end of it. A young person who turns down such an apprenticeship for a salary elsewhere is not rejecting tradition; they are making the calculation their grandparents would have made.

Whether the skills are worth preserving depends on what preservation means. Keeping a loom in a museum, with a label explaining how it was once used, preserves very little. The knowledge that mattered, such as how a local clay behaves in a particular kiln or how to judge the moisture in timber by its weight, lives only in the hands of people who practise it, and it disappears with the last of them. That knowledge is worth keeping, partly because it records how a community adapted to its own materials and partly because it is still useful: restorers of historic buildings, for instance, depend on joiners and stonemasons trained in methods industry abandoned long ago.

These skills should therefore be preserved, but as working trades rather than as exhibits. The most effective support is unglamorous: paying apprentices while they learn, and awarding public contracts, from repairing old buildings to furnishing civic spaces, to workshops that still use traditional methods. A craft that someone can live by will survive without further help; one that cannot will end up in a museum however much it is admired.

## 第1366篇

### 分数

Band 9.0

### 题目

Traffic congestion is becoming worse in many rapidly growing cities. What do you think are the causes of this, and what solutions could be introduced?

### 文章

Every growing city eventually discovers the same thing, and almost always the expensive way: a road built to relieve congestion fills up. The new capacity makes driving quicker, quicker driving attracts journeys that were previously made by another mode or not made at all, and within a few years the queue has re-formed at a higher volume. This is not a failure of engineering. It is what happens when a scarce resource is given away free and the only limit on demand is how long people are prepared to wait.

Seen that way, congestion is a rationing mechanism, and a peculiarly wasteful one. It allocates road space by willingness to sit in a queue rather than by the value of the trip, so an ambulance and an unhurried shopper are charged the same price, which is nothing, and both pay in the same currency, which is time. The reason cities keep building roads instead of addressing this is that congestion is visible and its cause is not; the queue looks like a shortage of asphalt.

The measures that work all involve making the cost explicit. Charging for entry to the busiest areas at the busiest hours removes the marginal trips first, and because flow collapses non-linearly, removing a small fraction of vehicles restores a disproportionate amount of speed. Revenue then funds the alternative, which must be genuinely faster than driving to attract anyone: separated bus lanes and rail, not simply newer buses stuck in the same queue.

The obstacle is not technical. Charging is regressive at first glance and intensely unpopular before it is introduced, though rarely afterwards. Any honest proposal has to acknowledge that, and to spend the revenue visibly on the people least able to pay — which is also, conveniently, the group most dependent on the buses the charge would speed up.

## 第1368篇

### 分数

### 题目

When children behave badly, some people believe that their parents rather than their schools should be held responsible. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

Blame is a poor instrument for this, because it can only be awarded to one party at a time and the thing being explained has more than one cause. Still, if the question is where a child's behaviour is formed, the honest answer is at home, and I agree that parents carry the greater responsibility for it. What follows from that is less obvious than it looks.

By the time a school meets a child, the important lessons have been taught. Whether adults keep their word, whether shouting works, whether a rule survives contact with a determined five-year-old: these are settled long before a timetable is involved, and settled by repetition in the only setting the child has known. A teacher then receives that child for six hours a day alongside twenty-nine others and is expected to reverse the finding. Some teachers manage it. That they occasionally succeed is not a reason to hold them accountable for failing.

The complication is that responsibility and capacity have come apart. Parents cause the behaviour, but a struggling parent is often the person least equipped to change it, while the school has the training, the structure and the daily contact that any change would require. This is why saying the fault lies with parents is both true and useless as policy. Identifying the blame accurately does not put the remedy in the hands of whoever can apply it.

So I would keep the judgement and abandon the conclusion usually drawn from it. Parents are responsible, and schools should still be where the work is done, not because they caused the problem but because they are where the child is, five days a week, with adults paid to notice. The alternative is a system that correctly establishes whose fault it is and then waits.

## 第1375篇

### 分数

Band 9.0

### 题目

Some people say that parents have the most important role in a child development. However, others argue that other things like Television or friends have the most significant influence. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

### 文章

Consider the yeti. Reputed to live in the mountainous regions of Tibet, Bhutan, and Nepal. Also known by the alias Abominable Snowman. Overgrown, in both senses: eight or ten or twelve feet tall; shaggy. Shy. Possibly a remnant of an otherwise extinct species. More possibly an elaborate hoax, or an inextinguishable hope. Closely related to the Australian Yowie, the Canadian Nuk-luk, the Missouri Momo, the Louisiana Swamp Ape, and Bigfoot. O.K., then: on a scale not of zero to ten but of, say, leprechaun to zombie, how likely do you think it is that the yeti exists?

One of the strangest things about the human mind is that it can reason about unreasonable things. It is possible, for example, to calculate the speed at which the sleigh would have to travel for Santa Claus to deliver all those gifts on Christmas Eve. It is possible to assess the ratio of a dragon’s wings to its body to determine if it could fly. And it is possible to decide that a yeti is more likely to exist than a leprechaun, even if you think that the likelihood of either of them existing is precisely zero.

Never mind, for now, whether or not you actually believe in any of these creatures. We are interested here not in whether they are real but in to what extent they seem as if they could be. Your job, accordingly, is to rank them in order of plausibility, from most likely (No. 1) to least likely (No. 20). Better still, if you are in the mood for a party game this Halloween season, try having a lot of people rank them collectively. I guarantee that this will produce a surprising amount of concord—who among us could rank the tooth fairy above the Leviathan?—as well as a huge amount of impassioned disagreement. The Loch Ness monster will turn out to have a Johnnie Cochran-level defense attorney. Good friends of yours will say withering things about mermaids.

What’s odd about this exercise is that everyone knows that “impossible” is an absolute condition. “Possible versus impossible” is not like “tall versus short.” Tall and short exist on a gradient, and when we adjudge the Empire State Building taller than LeBron James and LeBron James taller than Meryl Streep, we are reflecting facts about the world we live in. But possibility and impossibility are binary, and when we adjudge the yeti more probable than the leprechaun we aren’t reflecting facts about the world we live in; we aren’t reflecting the world we live in at all. So how, exactly, are we drawing these distinctions? And what does it say about our own wildly implausible, unmistakably real selves that we are able to do so?

In the fourth century B.C., several hundred years after the advent of harpies and some two millennia before the emergence of dementors, Aristotle sat down to do some thinking about supernatural occurrences in literature. On the whole, he was not a fan; in his Poetics, he mostly discouraged would-be fabulists from messing around with them. But he did allow that, if forced to choose, writers “should prefer a probable impossibility to an unconvincing possibility.” Better for Odysseus to return safely to Ithaca with the aid of ghosts, gods, sea nymphs, and a leather bag containing the wind than for his wife, Penelope, to get bored with waiting for him, grow interested in metalworking, and abandon domestic life for a career as a blacksmith.

Some people think that human needs for farmland, housing, and industry are more important than saving land for endangered animals. Do you agree or disagree with this point of view?

There is a common belief that prioritizing human needs for farmland, housing, and industry is more essential than preserving land for endangered animals. However, I disagree with this point of view and firmly believe that maintaining the ecological balance is vital. Flora and fauna play a significant role in sustaining life on our planet, and every living organism has its unique contribution to the well-being of Earth and humanity.

Firstly, the importance of ecological balance cannot be overstated. The natural world functions as a delicate and interconnected chain, where the extinction of one species can disrupt entire ecosystems. For instance, the extinction of large herbivores such as the mammoth caused significant changes in the vegetation patterns of their habitats, which in turn affected other species. If we continue to prioritize human expansion at the expense of biodiversity, we risk further destabilizing this balance, leading to unforeseen consequences for both the environment and human populations.

Secondly, flora and fauna are crucial for the survival of humanity. For example, ocean plankton, though small and seemingly insignificant, play an essential role in producing oxygen and absorbing carbon dioxide. Without these organisms, the air we breathe would be far less clean, and the effects of climate change would be even more severe. Similarly, the loss of predators like dingo dogs in Australia has led to an increase in invasive species, causing harm to local ecosystems and agriculture. These examples highlight how every living organism has a purpose, and by preserving endangered creatures, we protect the systems that sustain human life.

In conclusion, while the needs for farmland, housing, and industry are important, they should not come at the cost of the environment and the living organisms that depend on it. Preserving land for endangered animals is essential for maintaining ecological balance, which, in turn, ensures the long-term survival of humanity and the planet itself.

### 题目

Some people think that schools are too competitive and that this has a negative impact on children. Others believe the competitive environment encourages children to achieve.

### 文章

The issue of what kind of environment should be provided by schools has long been a thorny one. While many feel that the level of competitiveness found within education is excessive, others believe that it is necessary in order to inspire children to excel.

The case against excessive competition in school is a compelling one. By definition, not everyone can win a contest: where one child wins, another loses. Should a child lose consistently, he may be demotivated in his studies or dismissed by his peers, which could in turn lead to feelings of inadequacy and even a lack of drive later in life. Secondly, many believe that bringing out other qualities in children would be more beneficial. For example, former US President Franklin D. Roosevelt strongly advocated the promotion of co-operation over competition as a far more useful life skill. Were it the case that children were taught to work with instead of against each other, they may go on to accomplish far more.

On the other hand, learning to compete has its benefits too. Many argue that it better prepares the next generation for the real world. Whether they are applying to a top university, seeking a new promotion, or running their own company, adult life is full of experiences where one is in competition with others. If pupils are primed for this from an early age, they are perhaps more likely to push themselves harder to succeed as adults. Take students from Asia as an example: they are often raised in an extremely competitive environment and, as a result, tend to achieve more academically than western children.

To conclude, it is clear that this is not a straightforward issue. However, I believe that as much as learning to compete is an essential life skill in today’s world, co-operation between children should also be at the forefront of education to ensure a balanced future generation.

The exponential surge in global population presents multifaceted challenges that transcend economic boundaries, affecting both impoverished, underdeveloped nations and affluent, industrialized countries alike. This demographic phenomenon necessitates a nuanced approach to sustainable development, encompassing a spectrum of socioeconomic and environmental dimensions.

Moreover, the environmental impact is profound, with escalated consumption of natural resources leading to deforestation, loss of biodiversity, and increased greenhouse gas emissions. These environmental pressures are compounded by the challenges of managing waste and ensuring sustainable energy production.

In both contexts, the need for comprehensive policy frameworks is paramount. Governments must invest in family planning initiatives and education to curb population growth rates. Economic policies should focus on creating job opportunities and fostering innovation to accommodate the expanding workforce. Additionally, international cooperation is crucial in addressing the global nature of these issues. Climate change mitigation, resource management, and humanitarian aid are areas where collective action can yield significant benefits.

In conclusion, the dramatic rise in population presents complex challenges that require immediate and sustained attention. It found that 66% of children who focused solely on academics reported higher levels of anxiety compared to those who participated in a more diverse curriculum. This highlights the importance of providing children with a well-rounded education that includes both academic and practical learning experiences.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with the idea of removing non-academic subjects from schools. some people think that hosting an international sporting event is beneficial for a country while others disagree. Do the advantages of hosting major sporting events outweigh the disadvantages?

### 文章

In today's rapidly evolving world, some argue that hosting international sporting events can bring about positive consequences such as economic growth, while others believe that it can lead to serious social problems. However, I tend to believe that the advantages of international sporting events are more likely to outweigh the drawbacks because they can play a vital role in the development of a country by improving the tourism industry.

One of the major benefits of hosting international sporting events is that they usually attract many people from all around the world who desire to watch sports in person. This can create more job opportunities and contribute significantly to local businesses because visitors spend money on restaurants, accommodations, and local products, resulting in economic growth. Moreover, international events provide unique opportunities for local people to deepen their understanding of various cultural backgrounds, traditions, and perspectives, improving their essential skills such as creativity, communication, and critical thinking. For instance, the FIFA World Cup enables a country to gain a huge profit during the event because it hosts millions of people who desire to spend quality time in the country by participating in various outdoor activities while enjoying watching matches in person. Hence, such events can play an indispensable role in driving economic growth and promoting cultural awareness.

Nonetheless, international sporting events can also have disadvantages. One of the main drawbacks of international events is that they can place additional pressure on the security system because in such events, there are risks of serious offences, posing a threat to the public. In addition, governments should invest more in preparing modern and adequate facilities for visitors, which can leave them with limited resources to modernize other public services, including public transport and the healthcare system. As a result, hosting such events can exert a burden on government budgets. For example, some visitors often take part in irresponsible actions which give rise to serious social problems such as increased noise pollution and traffic congestion, particularly in city centres. Thus, such events can generate serious challenges, which threaten public security and contribute to financial issues.

To sum up, from my perspective, while international sporting events can exert additional pressure on the security system and government budgets, they have a positive impact on the tourism industry, cultural awareness, and economic growth. ## 第1409篇

### 分数

Band 6.0

### 题目

University students are increasingly studying abroad as part of their studies. discuss both advantages and disadvantages.

### 文章

In recent years, pursuing higher education in foreign countries has become increasingly common. While this trend offers substantial benefits in terms of cultural immersion and institutional revenue, it also presents significant emotional and financial hurdles for students and their families.

​On the one hand, studying abroad provides distinct personal and educational advantages. Primarily, international students gain invaluable cross-cultural exposure and develop independence by living away from their familiar support systems. Immersing oneself in a new linguistic and social environment enhances communication skills and fosters adaptability—qualities highly prized in today's globalized job market. Additionally, host universities benefit economically from international enrolments, as foreign tuition fees are typically higher than domestic rates. This financial influx enables institutions to upgrade research facilities and broaden academic programs, ultimately benefiting the entire student body.

​On the other hand, overseas education carries notable drawbacks. The most immediate challenge is emotional distress, particularly severe homesickness and isolation. Being separated from family during major cultural celebrations, often exacerbated by the high cost of international travel, can lead to anxiety and loneliness. Furthermore, the financial strain on families can be overwhelming. Currency exchange disparities and high tuition fees frequently force students to take on demanding part-time jobs alongside their studies, which can adversely affect their academic performance.

​In conclusion, although studying abroad poses serious challenges regarding financial pressure and emotional isolation, the opportunity to gain international qualifications and personal independence makes it a worthwhile endeavor for many.

## 第1415篇

### 分数

Band 6.5

### 题目

Nowadays, most of the information is available on the Internet, whereas in the past, knowledge was stored in books and on paper. Do you think the advantages of this situation outweigh its disadvantages?

### 文章

The proliferation of digital information has fundamentally transformed how knowledge is accessed and disseminated, shifting from traditional paper-based sources to online platforms. While this transition has undeniably revolutionized information accessibility, it is essential to evaluate whether the benefits of this shift outweigh its drawbacks.

The advantages of online information are substantial and multifaceted. Firstly, the internet provides unprecedented accessibility, allowing users to retrieve information instantaneously from virtually any location, provided they have a device and internet connectivity. This eliminates geographical barriers, enabling students, researchers, and professionals to access global knowledge resources without physical constraints. Secondly, digital platforms significantly reduce environmental impact by minimizing the need for paper production and physical storage spaces such as libraries. Additionally, online information is often more cost-effective—users can access vast amounts of data without the expense of purchasing physical books or journals. The rise of e-books and digital archives further enhances this convenience, offering instant downloads and portable access.

Nevertheless, the shift to online information is not without challenges. One notable disadvantage is the digital divide, where socioeconomic disparities limit access for low-income individuals or those in remote areas. High internet costs, unreliable infrastructure, and limited digital literacy exacerbate this issue, leaving certain populations disadvantaged. Another critical concern is the credibility of online sources. The lack of regulation on digital content means that misinformation, fake news, and biased narratives can spread rapidly, undermining trust in information. Unlike printed books, which undergo editorial scrutiny, online content often lacks rigorous verification, leading to the proliferation of unreliable or harmful information.

In conclusion, while the internet has undeniably enhanced information accessibility, convenience, and sustainability, its drawbacks—such as inequality of access and the spread of misinformation—cannot be ignored. A balanced approach, combining digital literacy, critical evaluation of sources, and efforts to bridge the digital divide, is essential to maximize the benefits of online information while mitigating its risks. Ultimately, the advantages of this transition are significant, but they must be harnessed responsibly to ensure a well-informed and equitable society

On the other hand, some people claim that making a restriction on travelling by air is directing individuals to use another kind of transportation. For instance, when every person drives his own car, this will produce a lot of gas emissions that cause an environmental crisis, especially for humans, because cars are driven on land.

## 第1423篇

### 分数

Band 6.5

### 题目

When students study a foreign language,,they should also study the culture and lifestyles of the people who speak the language. Do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

It is often claimed that language learners should also study the traditions and daily habits of native speakers. I disagree, since most learners study a language for a specific purpose such as work or an examination, and cultural knowledge is not necessary for that goal.

Students preparing for IELTS sometimes spend time learning about British culture rather than focusing on their weak points, such as essay structure, complex sentences, or the vocabulary the examiners actually reward. As a result, they score lower than they need, which can affect their future plans.

Furthermore, employees who want to learn another language for work often do not need to learn about lifestyles or culture for a formal email, meeting, or small talk. A formal meeting needs correct grammar, writing, and vocabulary to sound professional. None of that needs cultural knowledge. An employee who writes an email full of errors will look careless to clients, no matter how much they know about local traditions.

Admittedly, learning about culture usually makes learners avoid awkward moments. For example, in Japan there are specific customs around giving and receiving gifts, and getting them wrong can cause embarrassment. However, these customs are usually learned through direct contact with native speakers rather than formal lessons, and anyone working in another country will pick them up within weeks of arriving.

In conclusion, although cultural knowledge can occasionally prevent misunderstandings, I do not believe it should be a required part of language study, since most learners have specific goals that grammar and vocabulary serve far better.

### 题目

Some children spend hours every day on their smartphones. Why is this the case? Do you think this is a positive or a negative development

### 文章

The pervasive presence of smartphones in the lives of children has become an undeniable reality of modern childhood. This essay will argue that this trend is driven by both the inherent appeal of digital entertainment and parental convenience, and that it constitutes a predominantly negative development due to its detrimental effects on cognitive development and social well-being.

Several factors contribute to this phenomenon. Primarily, smartphone applications are engineered to be highly engaging, utilizing algorithms that reward continuous interaction through likes, notifications, and immersive games. Consequently, children find it difficult to disengage. Furthermore, parents often utilize devices as a form of digital babysitting. In busy households, handing a child a smartphone is perceived as an efficient method to ensure quietness and safety, inadvertently fostering a dependency on screens for emotional regulation and boredom alleviation.

However, the implications of this shift are largely adverse. Excessive screen time is strongly correlated with reduced attention spans, making sustained focus on academic tasks increasingly challenging. Moreover, the sedentary nature of smartphone usage displaces physical activity, contributing to rising rates of childhood obesity. Socially, while digital platforms offer connectivity, they often replace face-to-face interactions, which are crucial for developing empathy and complex social skills. As observed in various studies, heavy users often exhibit heightened anxiety and irritability when disconnected, suggesting a psychological reliance that undermines mental health.

In conclusion, while the allure of digital media and the practicality it offers parents explain the ubiquity of smartphones among children, the long-term consequences are concerning. The erosion of concentration, physical health, and genuine social connection marks this as a significant negative development. Parents and educators must therefore intervene to promote balanced digital habits.

## 第1429篇

### 分数

Band 7.0

### 题目

Some people say that your first impressions when you meet someone are always right. To what extent do you agree with this statement?

### 文章

It is often argued that the first impression is a lasting impression. This issue has sparked considerable debate, and I firmly disagree with this statement because people's behaviour and personality can change over time. This essay will present well-supported arguments to justify my stance.

Firstly, one of the most compelling reasons is that a first encounter does not necessarily reflect a person's inner personality. This is because an individual may appear shy, nervous or unfriendly when meeting someone for the first time. However, deep down, they may actually be friendly, cooperative and capable. For instance, when you first meet a new employee at the office, you may perceive them as unfriendly because they are quiet or reserved. However, after working with them for some time, you may discover that they are cooperative, helpful and sociable. Therefore, it is unfair to judge someone's character based solely on an initial encounter.

Moreover, a first impression may only represent a person's temporary state of mind or circumstances. It is possible that an individual behaves in a particular way during a first meeting simply because they want to create a positive impression. For example, people may behave extremely efficiently and professionally in the workplace when they are being observed, while their behaviour in other situations may be quite different. Thus, a first impression does not always provide an accurate picture of someone's true personality.

In my opinion, first impressions should not be considered a reliable measure of a person's character. People experience different situations throughout their lives, and these experiences can have a significant impact on their behaviour and personality. They learn new skills, develop different perspectives and adapt to changing circumstances. As a result, their personalities may evolve considerably over time.

In conclusion, a first impression is not always an accurate reflection of a person's true character because it may be influenced by their emotions, circumstances and desire to make a positive impression. Although physical appearance and initial behaviour can affect people's opinions, a person's behaviour over time is a much more reliable indicator of their actual personality.

Personally, I firmly believe that individuals can achieve true contentment without vast amounts of money, and I maintain that physical health and family bonds are far more crucial factors for doing so.

First and foremost, materialistic wealth is not a mandatory prerequisite for achieving emotional well-being. When an individual's basic life necessities are met, acquiring excessive luxury does not directly translate to deeper joy; instead, it often brings unnecessary psychological burdens. Instead, finding satisfaction in simple daily activities allows people to live a balanced life free from corporate stress. For instance, global surveys frequently show that communities in developing countries report high happiness indices despite having lower average incomes. Consequently, this proves that mental peace and satisfaction are entirely independent of one's bank balance.

Turning to the other factors, meaningful human relationships and robust physical health contribute far more significantly towards long-term happiness. No amount of money can purchase the genuine affection of supportive family members and lifelong friends, which are essential during times of crisis. Furthermore, if a person suffers from severe illnesses, their financial capital becomes practically useless in terms of generating real life satisfaction. To cite a clear example, many wealthy individuals frequently struggle with loneliness and depression, proving that emotional stability cannot be obtained through commercial means.

In conclusion, while money is necessary to cover fundamental living costs, it is not the ultimate source of human joy. I re-emphasize that true happiness is entirely constructed upon the foundations of excellent health and strong familial relationships, rather than economic prosperity.

### 题目

Young people who commit crimes should be treated in the same way as adults. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

oung people who commit crimes are often believed to deserve the same punishment as adults. While some people argue that equal treatment ensures justice, I largely disagree with this view because juveniles are less mature and have a greater capacity for rehabilitation. However, in cases of serious crime, stricter measures may be justified.

One of the main reasons why young offenders should not be treated in exactly the same way as adults is that they are still developing psychologically and emotionally. Teenagers are more likely to make impulsive decisions and can be strongly influenced by friends or their social environment. Consequently, they may not fully understand the consequences of their actions. For instance, a teenager may become involved in theft or vandalism due to peer pressure rather than criminal intent. Therefore, it would be unfair to hold them to the same level of responsibility as a mature adult.

Furthermore, the purpose of the juvenile justice system should be rehabilitation rather than punishment. Since young people are still forming their values and behaviour, they are generally more capable of change. Measures such as counselling, education programmes and community service can help them become productive members of society. In contrast, sending young offenders to adult prisons may expose them to hardened criminals and increase the likelihood of reoffending. As a result, rehabilitation is often a more effective solution than severe punishment.

Nevertheless, there are situations in which young offenders should face penalties similar to those imposed on adults. Crimes such as murder, rape or armed robbery can have devastating consequences for victims and society. In these circumstances, the seriousness of the offence must be taken into account. While the offender's age should remain a consideration, it should not completely shield them from significant legal consequences.

In conclusion, I disagree that young criminals should always be treated in the same way as adults. Although severe crimes may require harsher punishment, most juvenile offenders should receive treatment that focuses on rehabilitation, as this approach offers a better chance of reducing future crime and helping them reintegrate into society.

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目



### 文章

The rapid expansion of remote working, accelerated by advances in connectivity software and the widespread disruption of recent years, has prompted legitimate disagreement about its long-term merits. While I recognise the substantial benefits that flexible working arrangements offer, I believe that an exclusively home-based model carries social and professional costs that a well-designed hybrid approach can avoid.

Advocates of remote working point, understandably, to the efficiency gains it delivers. The elimination of daily commutes — which, in many cities, consumes upwards of two hours per day — returns significant time and energy to workers. Additionally, research consistently shows that employees in self-managed environments report lower stress levels and, in many task types, higher output. For knowledge workers in particular, the ability to structure the working day around periods of peak concentration is a genuine productivity advantage.

Those who favour office-based work, however, identify losses that remote arrangements struggle to replicate. Spontaneous professional exchange — the corridor conversation that solves a problem, the informal mentoring that shapes a junior colleague's development — does not transfer easily to a scheduled video call. Furthermore, the boundary between professional and domestic life becomes genuinely difficult to maintain when both occupy the same physical space, a challenge that falls disproportionate on those with caring responsibilities.

My own position is that neither extreme is optimal. A structured hybrid model, where teams meet in person two or three days per week and work remotely for the remainder, preserves the productivity benefits of flexible working while sustaining the social dimension of professional life. The technology that makes remote work possible also makes such coordination straightforward; the question is whether organisations are willing to design it deliberately.

## 第1437篇

Band 7.5

### 题目



### 文章

The question of whether secondary schools should offer a broad, compulsory curriculum or allow students to concentrate on subjects that genuinely engage them has long divided educational policymakers. While both positions have considerable merit, I believe that a structured foundation of core subjects, combined with meaningful elective choice, produces the best outcomes for young people.

Those who advocate a wide curriculum argue, with justification, that adolescence is too early for rigid specialisation. Students who have not yet encountered a subject cannot know whether it will ignite a lasting passion or unlock an unexpected aptitude. Moreover, universities and employers consistently value candidates who demonstrate the capacity to think across disciplines — a skill that narrow early specialisation rarely develops. Exposure to history, science, and the arts in parallel encourages the kind of flexible reasoning that proves valuable throughout adult life.

Proponents of student-led choice, however, point to a genuine weakness in compulsory breadth: when students are required to spend years on subjects they find irrelevant, disengagement often follows. Research in educational psychology suggests that intrinsic motivation is among the strongest predictors of academic achievement, and a timetable that ignores student interest risks undermining it. There is also a practical dimension — modern professions demand specialist depth that a generalist secondary education alone cannot provide.

My own view is that these positions are less contradictory than they appear. A core of foundational subjects — literacy, numeracy, and basic scientific understanding — should remain compulsory for all students, as these underpin virtually every career pathway. Beyond this core, structured elective choice allows students' aptitudes and interests to inform their studies without foreclosing essential learning. This hybrid model respects both the value of breadth and the motivating power of personal engagement.

### 题目

Surveillance cameras in banks, offices, shops and streets have been very successful in reducing crime in the workplace and public, but they are also took for their users to spy on people's private business. what problems do surveillance cameras create? what are the solutions?

### 文章

Surveillance cameras have become a common feature in public places and workplaces because they help prevent crime and improve security. However, despite these advantages, they can also lead to serious concerns about privacy and misuse. This essay will discuss the problems caused by surveillance cameras and suggest effective solutions.

One major problem is the invasion of personal privacy. People may feel uncomfortable knowing that their daily activities are constantly being recorded, even when they are not doing anything wrong. This can create stress and reduce their sense of freedom. Another issue is the misuse of recorded footage. In some cases, individuals or organisations may access or share videos without permission, leading to blackmail, harassment, or damage to a person’s reputation. Furthermore, weak cybersecurity systems can allow hackers to steal or manipulate surveillance data, putting sensitive information at risk.

Several measures can be taken to address these issues. First, governments should introduce strict laws regulating where surveillance cameras can be installed and how recorded footage can be used. Only authorised personnel should have access to the recordings, and severe penalties should be imposed on anyone who misuses them. Second, organisations should invest in secure storage systems and encryption technology to protect video data from cyberattacks. Finally, the public should be informed whenever surveillance cameras are operating, ensuring transparency and helping people understand that the cameras are installed primarily for safety rather than unnecessary monitoring.

In conclusion, although surveillance cameras play a significant role in reducing crime and improving public safety, they can also threaten personal privacy and be misused. These concerns can be minimised through stronger legal regulations, improved data security, and greater transparency regarding the use of surveillance systems.

Today, more and more students are choosing to move to another country for their higher education studies. Do the benefits of studying abroad outweigh the problems associated with it? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

### 文章

Today, an increasing number of students choose to pursue higher education in foreign countries. Although studying abroad presents certain financial and emotional challenges, I firmly believe that the long-term benefits significantly outweigh these temporary difficulties.

One major advantage is the access to high-quality education and broader career opportunities. Many internationally recognised universities provide advanced facilities, distinguished academics, and research opportunities that may not be available in students' home countries. As a result, graduates often acquire specialised knowledge, practical skills, and internationally respected qualifications that enhance their employability. For example, a medical student who completes clinical training at a leading overseas institution is likely to gain exposure to cutting-edge technology and diverse healthcare systems, making them more competitive in the global job market.

In addition to academic benefits, living abroad promotes substantial personal growth. Students must adapt to unfamiliar cultures, communicate with people from different backgrounds, and manage everyday responsibilities independently. These experiences cultivate resilience, confidence, and cross-cultural communication skills, all of which are highly valued by employers. Admittedly, international education can be expensive, and many students experience homesickness during the initial months. Nevertheless, these challenges usually diminish over time as students establish social networks and adjust to their new environment. Moreover, scholarships, part-time employment, and financial planning can considerably reduce the economic burden.

## 第1449篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Today more countries import food from different parts of the world. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this trend?

### 文章

International trade has made it increasingly common for countries to import food from different parts of the world. Although this trend provides consumers with a greater variety of food throughout the year, it can also create significant challenges for domestic farmers and agricultural businesses.

One significant advantage of importing food is that it provides consumers with access to a wider variety of products. Since climatic conditions differ considerably between countries, certain fruits, vegetables and other agricultural products cannot be produced locally throughout the year. By importing these products from regions where growing conditions are more favourable, countries can maintain a consistent supply of food regardless of the local season. Consequently, consumers can enjoy a greater variety of fresh produce throughout the year rather than being restricted to locally available products.

However, excessive reliance on imported food can negatively affect domestic farmers and agricultural businesses. When imported products are available at lower prices, consumers may choose them over locally produced alternatives. This can reduce demand for domestic produce, making it increasingly difficult for local farmers to compete with large overseas suppliers. As a result, farmers may experience declining incomes, and some agricultural businesses may eventually be forced to close. For example, a local fruit producer may struggle to remain profitable if supermarkets consistently sell cheaper imported alternatives.

In conclusion, importing food allows consumers to access a wider range of products regardless of local climate and seasonal limitations. However, excessive dependence on imported produce can reduce demand for locally grown food and negatively affect the livelihoods of domestic farmers.

## 第1450篇

### 分数

Band 7.5

### 题目

Topic: It is the responsibility of individuals to save and provide for their own retirement. Governments have no obligation to provide this benefit. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

In the modern economic landscape, the question of who should bear the financial burden of retirement has sparked intense global debate. While some argue that individuals must be entirely self-reliant in securing their senior years, I strongly disagree with the assertion that governments have no obligation to provide retirement benefits. A functional society requires a dual-responsibility model where state-funded safety nets and personal savings work in tandem.

To begin with, the premise that governments have no duty to support retirees ignores the fundamental social contract between a state and its citizens. Throughout their working lives, individuals contribute to their nation's economic growth through labor and taxation. Therefore, the provision of a retirement pension is not an act of charity, but a reciprocal obligation. For instance, in countries like Sweden and the Netherlands, robust state pension systems are funded directly by decades of taxpayer contributions. These systems ensure that citizens, having dedicated their productive years to building the nation, are guaranteed financial security and dignity in their twilight years.

Furthermore, relying solely on individual savings is a highly precarious approach that exacerbates social inequality. Not all citizens have equal opportunities to accumulate wealth; those in low-income brackets, individuals with chronic illnesses, or caregivers who take career breaks often lack the disposable income to invest in private retirement portfolios. Without a state-guaranteed baseline pension, a vast segment of the elderly population would inevitably slip into extreme poverty. A government-provided safety net is therefore essential to uphold human dignity and prevent systemic socio-economic collapse among vulnerable demographic groups.

However, this is not to say that individuals bear no responsibility. While the government must guarantee a survival-level baseline, personal financial planning remains vital for those wishing to maintain a higher standard of living. In nations like Canada and the United States, employer-sponsored schemes and private investment accounts (such as RRSPs or 401ks) successfully complement public pensions. This multi-pillar approach relieves pressure on the public treasury while encouraging fiscal responsibility among workers. Nevertheless, individual initiative should serve as a supplement to, rather than a replacement for, state welfare.

In conclusion, I completely disagree that governments are free from the obligation of providing retirement benefits. An equitable society must ensure that old age does not equate to financial destitution. The most sustainable and ethical path forward is a collaborative framework where the state provides a secure, dignified foundation, and individuals build upon it according to their means.

### 题目

The best way to reduce traffic accidents is to raise the age limit for younger drivers and to lower the age limit for elderly ones. Do you agree or disagree?

### 文章

In today’s world the number of traffic accidents is constantly rising as well as the number of injuries and deaths they cause. A better regulative approach is required for traffic accidents can be reduced. Some people say that changing the drivers’ age limits is the best solution to the problem. However, there are other, more practical ways to deal with this problem.

One alternative is imposing heavier fines at the drivers who exceed the permitted alcohol consumption. According to recent datas , a great proportion of traffic accidents has alcohol as its reason. Utilising technology and installing devices that detect drunk drivers and lock car ignition can be used to keep people with track record of drunk driving off the roads. On some occasions and for repeat offenders in particular, a prison sentence may also be considered.

Furthermore, people should be better educated and more careful while behind the wheel. To be more specific, people should learn to obey road rules and respect the other drivers instead of causing tension or submitting to road rage. In addition, heavy fines should also be levied for exceeded speed limits. Last but not least, safer and wider roads should be constructed to make for easier and more comfortable driving.

Tightening age limits for drivers can be a complementary approach. For example, the elderly with vision problems or other important health issues should be excluded from driving. Besides, young people under 18 years old are considered immature to drive. However, maturity does not necessarily always increases with one’s age, which is why other measures are needed to reducing dangerous driving.

In conclusion, I believe that stronger measures should be implemented for the prevention of traffic accidents, and drivers should have a more responsible attitude. Setting age limits could be helpful but should not be considered the optimal and only solution to the problem.

Parents and family provide a nurturing environment, values, and life skills, while schools offer a comprehensive education, knowledge acquisition, and social growth. ### 题目

Some people think that schools should teach students according to their academic abilities, while others believe that it is better to have students with different abilities to study together. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

### 文章

It is sometimes argued that schools should teach students in groups based on academic ability, whereas others believe that children of different levels should study together. I accept that ability grouping can be useful in some situations, but I believe that mixed-ability classes should remain the normal approach.

On the one hand, teaching students according to ability may make lessons more efficient. In a class of high achievers, teachers can move at a faster pace, introduce more demanding tasks and avoid spending too much time on basic explanations. Similarly, pupils who find academic work difficult may benefit from slower lessons, clearer explanations and more individual attention. If these groups are flexible rather than permanent, they can help different learners make progress at a pace that suits them.

However, I would argue that separating children too early can do more harm than good. Students placed in lower groups may feel that they have been labelled as weak, which could damage both their confidence and their ambition. By contrast, mixed classes allow learners to cooperate with classmates who have different strengths. A capable student who explains a problem to a friend, for example, often understands it more deeply, while the friend receives support in a relaxed and less intimidating way. It also prepares them for a society in which people rarely work only with those at the same level.

In my view, the best solution is to keep most classes mixed, while providing extra support for struggling learners and extension tasks for high achievers. This approach recognises academic differences without turning them into permanent labels.

In conclusion, although ability-based teaching has some advantages, mixed-ability education is generally better because it supports both academic progress and social development.

### 文章

It is believed by some people that acceptance is the ultimate way of dealing with bad situations, such as a non-appealing job; others believe that you should try and change the bad circumstances you are put into. I believe that both opinions should be viewed as complementary ideas rather than opposing ones.

On the one hand, those who argue that we should accept any condition we are put into might present valid points. This is because gratefulness is the key trait anyone should have in order to reach a peaceful and satisfactory job. Conversely, adopting  greedy behaviour towards any unfair state would not make it vanish; instead, you will develop envy and hatred towards other people whose lives seem perfect. Moreover, a lot of the circumstances that life puts us in are likely unchangeable; thus, greed and envy will be a waste of time and effort that can be put into making the best of our current situation. For instance, a high school graduate, who did not get into his dream profession, should not be wasting time in sadness but rather make the best of his new major and accept his upcoming job.

On the other hand, viewing acceptance and effort-making as two opposing approaches rather than complementary notions when dealing with problems is  a misleading and unfair assumption. In other words, working hard to improve your circumstances does not contradict the level of acceptance and gratefulness you establish but rather is  proof of your drive to have a better life that suits your needs. For example, an adequate-level person trying to provide his children with higher-quality education does not exactly indicate the lack of financial management of that father but instead is proof of him trying to fix his financial situation through investing in the literacy of his kids, which will eventually pay him back. Looking at the other side of the argument, if that father did not care about his children’s education and chose to “accept” his social/financial level, he and his family would likely remain in poverty for the rest of their lives.

In conclusion, there is no doubt that approval of different affairs is a demanded criterion that everyone should be able to adopt. However, working hard to improve that affair does not reduce the level of gratefulness a person has.

Young people are often influenced in their behaviors by others in the same age group. Some argue that peer pressure is important while others feel it has distinct disadvantages. Do the disadvantages of peer pressure outweigh the advantages?

### 文章

Peer pressure refers to the influence young people experience within the same age group, affecting their behaviours. In my opinion, cohorts do have more positive impact than negative on adolescents and young adults. 

On one hand, peer pressure often leads the young to engage in risky behaviours. For instance, teenagers may feel compelled to experiment with drugs due to the effect of their peers who engage in such activities. The desire to fit in and be accepted can override their better judgment, exposing them to serious short-term health risks and potential addiction later in life. Moreover, succumbing to negative peer pressure can adversely affect academic performance, as students may prioritize social acceptance over their studies. This desire for approval can result in poor grades, limited educational opportunities, and long-term negative consequences.

On the other hand, positive peer pressure can inspire adolescents to set higher goals, adopt healthier habits, and strive for academic excellence. Many teenagers are pressured by their peers to join a study group, leading to improved learning outcomes and academic success. Relatedly, supportive friends can inspire young adults to engage in physical fitness activities or pursue positive hobbies and talents, promoting a healthier and more well-rounded lifestyle. This sense of camaraderie and mutual encouragement fostered within positive groups can contribute significantly to personal growth and self-confidence. Actively seeking out positive and active cohorts and engaging in activities aligned with one’s personal values can help mitigate the adverse effects of negative peer pressure while harnessing the advantages of positive influence.

In conclusion, although peers can encourage risky behaviours and hinder personal growth, the motivational and emotional advantages make this pressure a positive phenomenon on the whole. Ultimately, striking some degree of balance between independence and positive peer interactions is crucial to minimizing the disadvantages and embracing the benefits.

## 第1481篇

### 分数

Band 9.0

### 题目

Should school children be given homework (opinion)?

### 文章

The benefits of giving or not giving homework to children are often debated. Some people feel that children have enough work to do during one day whilst at school, whereas others feel that the more work set, the better.

It is true that schools today place more and more demands and pressure on children. The competition to do well, to enter a good university and to get a good job is significant. This has led to the ideology that children should do as much schoolwork as possible in order to help their intellectual development. The argument, however, that more is better is not always valid. There comes a point, especially for a child, when more knowledge cannot be absorbed in a day. When a child has possibly 7 or 8 classes a day on different subjects, he or she is processing a lot of information already. To give more work to be done at home, therefore, would be pointless and even counterproductive. In addition to this, although it is important to be educated, childhood should also be a time when there is an opportunity to just play and enjoy unstructured time. Homework can significantly lessen the possibilities of doing this.

On the other hand, it can be argued that there is a place for homework. If study at school is not overdone, the opportunity to look at work again and extend ideas can be an invaluable exercise. It’s easy to forget one thing that has been taught once, but if that concept is revisited a second time, the brain has time to reprocess and likely better understand and remember.

It seems to me that there is a place for homework for today’s children. What must be remembered, though, is that homework needs to be limited to age-appropriate parameters, so that a balance can be struck between study and free time and relaxation.

## 第1482篇

### 分数

Band 9.0

### 题目



### 文章

The shift towards remote working, made viable by advances in connectivity and collaboration technologies, represents one of the more consequential changes in modern professional life. Whether it constitutes progress, however, depends on how the question is framed — and both sides of this debate are identifying something real.

The productivity argument for remote work is well-founded. Stripped of the commute and the structural interruptions of open-plan offices, many workers produce more, particularly those whose output depends on sustained concentration rather than real-time collaboration. Evidence from organisations that adopted flexible models before such arrangements became a necessity suggests that, for individual knowledge tasks, location matters far less than autonomy over one's own time.

What this framing misses, though, is that organisations are not simply collections of individuals completing tasks in parallel. They are communities in which meaning, trust, and professional identity are built through proximity and unscripted interaction. The junior employee who learns by observation, the team that solves an unexpected problem by converging on a whiteboard, the colleague who notices that something is wrong before any formal meeting is scheduled — these are not inefficiencies that remote working can be said to optimise away. They are the connective tissue of high-functioning teams, and they are genuinely difficult to replicate through a screen.

The most defensible position, I would argue, is neither blanket enthusiasm for remote work nor a nostalgic insistence on the pre-pandemic office. It is the deliberate design of a hybrid model that allocates in-person time to the collaborative and social functions where physical presence is irreplaceable, and remote time to the focused individual work where it demonstrably helps. The same technologies that enable remote work also make such intentional coordination entirely feasible. The question is whether leaders are willing to design for it, rather than defaulting to habit in either direction.

## 第1483篇

### 分数

Band 9.0

### 题目



### 文章

Few educational debates are as persistent as this one, perhaps because both sides are genuinely correct about what they are describing, even when they draw incompatible conclusions. The question is not, at root, whether breadth or depth matters more; it is how secondary education can deliver both, and in what sequence.

The case for a broad compulsory curriculum is stronger than its critics acknowledge. The objection that students know best what interests them at thirteen or fourteen systematically underestimates the degree to which interests are formed by exposure rather than discovered in a vacuum. A student who has never encountered economics, philosophy, or computer science cannot meaningfully choose to pursue or avoid them. Compulsory breadth, then, is not an imposition of irrelevant content; it is the structural precondition for informed choice. There is also a cognitive argument: engagement across disparate disciplines — mathematics alongside literature, history alongside natural science — develops forms of reasoning that no single subject can cultivate in isolation.

What the advocates of specialisation are correctly identifying, however, is the cost of an undifferentiated compulsory curriculum extended too far and too long. Sustained disengagement from subjects a student finds genuinely purposeless is not a minor inconvenience; it actively corrodes the motivation and self-efficacy on which all learning depends. The secondary years are also a period during which vocational aptitudes begin to crystallise, and a system that offers no room for that process does those students a structural disservice.

The resolution I would propose is a sequenced one: a common foundation in the early secondary years that ensures every student acquires the cognitive tools and cultural literacy that adult life requires, followed by a progressively expanding zone of elective study as students mature. Breadth enables depth; the foundations of genuine specialisation are often laid in subjects one would not have chosen for oneself.

### 题目

Many young people leave school with negative attitudes towards learning. What are the causes？How to encourage young people to study？

### 文章

It is true that in modern society, numerous young graduates hold negative attitudes towards learning. There are various possible reasons for this, but steps can definitely be taken to address this issue.

In my opinion, there are three main factors contributing to the negative attitudes young individuals have toward learning. Firstly, school tuition tends to be too standardized and lacks personalized attention. Many schools do not provide sufficient resources for students to explore their specific interests or talents. Secondly, the educational system places too much emphasis on curricula and examinations, causing students to view learning solely to achieve high test scores. This narrow focus can undermine their intrinsic motivation to learn. Finally, peer pressure can also have a detrimental effect. Young people may feel inferior to their peers, which can diminish their motivation to study and, in some cases, negatively impact their mental health.

However, there are several ways to encourage young people to develop a genuine interest in learning. I believe that the training sector must lead this change by modernizing traditional approaches and tailoring services to meet the diverse needs of scholars. Schools should offer more opportunities for students to easily access various learning resources, allowing them to develop practical skills in fields they are passionate about. Furthermore, the public can play an important role in creating a positive learning environment. For instance, organizing knowledge competitions could inspire participants and rekindle their interest in learning. Additionally, parents have a crucial responsibility to set a good example for their children. They should help their children set clear learning goals, create feasible study plans, and provide recognition and encouragement for their achievements.

In conclusion, young people may lose the motivation to study after graduation unless parents, the educational sector, and society at large work together to foster a positive learning environment.

### 题目

Research indicates that the characteristics we are born with have much more influence on our personality and development than any experiences we may have in our life. Which do you consider to be the major influence? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

### 文章

Studies have concluded that our personality and development rely more on the characteristics we are born with than any events that may occur and affect our lives. Even though our genetic background plays a significant role in our later development, it disagrees that they may be a greater influence than exposure to incidents or circumstances in life, and this essay will prove it.

Firstly, consider the plasticity of the human brain, particularly in early childhood. During this period, neural connections are made through interactions with caretakers or other peers. For instance, a child raised in a nurturing and stimulating environment is likely to develop better cognitive and social skills compared to one who experiences neglect or abuse. This phenomenon underscores the impact of external stimuli on development, illustrating how experiences can alter the trajectory set by genetic predispositions.

Moreover, personal circumstances and social influences provide convincing evidence of the power of experience. Individuals who overcome significant adversity often emerge with resilience and unique perspectives, demonstrating that challenging experiences can foster growth and positive personality traits. For example, people who have faced wars or hard times are more inclined to develop resilience and the ability to overcome urgent or stressful situations, characteristics not necessarily rooted in genetics, but in the need to adapt to their circumstances.

In conclusion, while genetic predispositions provide a foundational blueprint for personality and development, it is the experiences we encounter throughout life that have a more substantial and transformative impact. The adaptability and resilience developed through life's challenges further underscore the significant role of nurture in determining who we become. Therefore, experiences are the major influence in shaping our personalities and guiding our development.

### 题目

What discovery in the last 100 years has been most beneficial for people in your country?

### 文章

China, the most populous country in the world, had been struggling to feed billions of mouths for centuries until hybrid rice was invented. This innovation fundamentally transformed the nation and corroborated the remarkable economic growth that followed in the next two decades. It has not only saved millions of lives but also facilitated the country’s advancement, which makes it the greatest modern innovation in my country.

To begin with, only ten years before this fecund species came out, Chinese people had just undergone the deadliest catastrophe—the Great Chinese Famine—during which nearly 50 million lives starved to death. The disaster was caused by a wide range of misconduct and nonsensical policies, including poor agricultural techniques and commanding farmers to abandon their lands and switch to iron production. The direct impact was the sheer nationwide population decline, and the long-term consequence was that the fear of starvation morphed into a genetic and inextricable feature embedded in every Chinese citizen. From then on, making rice available for everyone became the sole aim of the government. 

With billions of dollars and uncountable human resources spent on the agricultural sector, the concerted effort finally paid off in the year 1972, when a man called Yuan Longping, who would later be remembered as the father of hybrid rice, successfully cultivated the new rice that fundamentally changed not just China but the world. For example, the introduction of this technology has raised China’s rice production by 40%, significantly alleviating the food crisis and improving living conditions. As a result, most of the younger ones do not know what hunger feels like, and the word famine has been made archaic. Moreover, thanks to the stability underscored by the growing food storage, China entered a period characterised by dynamism and energy in the 1990s, boosting its economic and political influence and becoming a global powerhouse. Thus, it can be said that the birth of hybrid rice was the watershed between the decline and rise of the country.

In summary, the innovation of hybrid rice is the greatest domestic accomplishment that has ever been achieved in centuries because it facilitates social and economic development and nearly eliminates hunger in China.
